  auto *Else = llvm::BasicBlock::Create(Ctx, "else", F);
  auto *Merge = llvm::BasicBlock::Create(Ctx, "merge", F);
  auto *A = F->getArg(0), *C = F->getArg(1);

  llvm::IRBuilder<> B(Entry);
  // A 128-bit <4 x i32> source, each dword arg-derived and sign-mixed so the
  // sign-extend (vpmovsxdq) and zero-extend (vpmovzxdq) results diverge.
  llvm::Value *VD = llvm::UndefValue::get(V4d);
  for (unsigned I = 0; I < 4; ++I) {
    llvm::Value *Dv =
        B.CreateXor(B.CreateMul(A, B.getInt32(I * 0x1B7 + 7)),
                    B.CreateSub(B.getInt32(I * 5 + 1), B.CreateMul(C, A)));
    VD = B.CreateInsertElement(VD, Dv, uint64_t(I));
  }

  // +avx2 anchor (x86-64): keep the 256-bit YMM domain so the dword->qword widen
  // lowers to vpmovsxdq / vpmovzxdq ymm rather than two split xmm widens.
  if (IsX64) {
    llvm::Value *VAa = llvm::UndefValue::get(V8d);
    llvm::Value *VSa = llvm::UndefValue::get(V8d);
    for (unsigned I = 0; I < 8; ++I) {
      VAa =
          B.CreateInsertElement(VAa, B.CreateAdd(A, B.getInt32(I)), uint64_t(I));
      VSa = B.CreateInsertElement(
          VSa, B.CreateAnd(B.CreateAdd(C, B.getInt32(I)), B.getInt32(7)),
          uint64_t(I));
    }
    (void)B.CreateIntrinsic(llvm::Intrinsic::x86_avx2_psllv_d_256, {},
                            {VAa, VSa});
  }

  // Dword->qword widen: sign-extend (vpmovsxdq) and zero-extend (vpmovzxdq).
  // The auto-upgraded native form of llvm.x86.avx2.pmovsxdq / pmovzxdq is a
  // <4 x i32> sext / zext to <4 x i64> (dst.q[i] = ext(src.d[i])).
  llvm::Value *SX = B.CreateSExt(VD, V4q);
  llvm::Value *ZX = B.CreateZExt(VD, V4q);

  // Fold each 64-bit result (lo ^ hi) so the sign-fill high dword (sext) vs zero
  // (zext) is observable, with distinct ascending / descending per-lane weights.
  llvm::Value *S = B.getInt32(0);
  for (unsigned L = 0; L < 4; ++L) {
    llvm::Value *E = B.CreateExtractElement(SX, uint64_t(L));
    llvm::Value *Lo = B.CreateTrunc(E, I32);
    llvm::Value *Hi = B.CreateTrunc(B.CreateLShr(E, B.getInt64(32)), I32);
    S = B.CreateAdd(S, B.CreateMul(B.CreateXor(Lo, Hi), B.getInt32(L + 1)));
  }
  for (unsigned L = 0; L < 4; ++L) {
    llvm::Value *E = B.CreateExtractElement(ZX, uint64_t(L));
    llvm::Value *Lo = B.CreateTrunc(E, I32);
    llvm::Value *Hi = B.CreateTrunc(B.CreateLShr(E, B.getInt64(32)), I32);
    S = B.CreateAdd(S, B.CreateMul(B.CreateXor(Lo, Hi), B.getInt32(8 - L)));
  }

  auto *T = B.CreateXor(B.CreateXor(B.CreateAdd(A, C), B.CreateSub(A, C)),
                        B.getInt32(0x4E4E));
  auto *U = B.CreateOr(B.CreateAnd(A, C), B.CreateAdd(T, B.getInt32(29501)));
  auto *Base = B.CreateAdd(S, U);
  B.CreateCondBr(B.CreateICmpNE(B.CreateAnd(B.CreateXor(A, C), B.getInt32(1)),
                                B.getInt32(0)),
                 Then, Else);

  B.SetInsertPoint(Then);
  auto *R1 = B.CreateAdd(Base, A);
  B.CreateBr(Merge);

  B.SetInsertPoint(Else);
  auto *R2 = B.CreateXor(Base, C);
  B.CreateBr(Merge);

  B.SetInsertPoint(Merge);
  auto *Pc = B.CreatePHI(I32, 2);
  Pc->addIncoming(R1, Then);
  Pc->addIncoming(R2, Else);
  B.CreateRet(Pc);
  assert(!llvm::verifyModule(*M, &llvm::errs()));
  return M;
}

// 256-bit AVX2 byte->dword integer widening on YMM -- vpmovsxbd / vpmovzxbd
// (the low 8 bytes of a 128-bit source widened to a 256-bit <8 x i32> dest:
// dst.d[i] = ext(src.b[i]) for the eight lanes).  Sibling of vimovextbw256
// (byte->word, 2x) and vimovextdq256 (dword->qword, 2x) at a *skip* step: a
// 4x byte->dword widen that consumes only eight source bytes yet spans the full
// 256-bit register.  Because it discards bytes 8-15 of the xmm source, a decoder
// that mistakes it for the 2x byte->word form (consuming 16 bytes) or that
// mis-strides the source bytes mis-fills every dword lane.
//
// Cross-ISA: llvm.x86.avx2.pmovsxbd / pmovzxbd were auto-upgraded to native IR,
// i.e. a plain <8 x i8> sext / zext to <8 x i32>.  On x86-64 a dead
// llvm.x86.avx2.psllv.d.256 anchors +avx2 so the widen lowers to vpmovsxbd /
// vpmovzxbd ymm (one xmm source -> ymm dest) rather than split xmm widens -- an
// undecoded YMM op faults the Unicorn baseline (UC_ERR_INSN_INVALID).  Every
// other cell lowers the identical sext / zext to native widening moves (NEON
// sshll/ushll chains, split SSE), libcall-free.  Each source byte is arg-derived
// and sign-mixed so sext (vpmovsxbd) and zext (vpmovzxbd) diverge; the eight
// sign-extended dwords carry ascending weights and the eight zero-extended
// dwords descending weights, so both widens -- and any byte where they differ --
// are observable.  No L1 pass touches the widen sub-graph, so the original and
// obfuscated copies stay byte-identical over it, while integer add/sub/and/or/xor
// + non-folding constants (0x7C7C/40903) + a data-dependent diamond + PHI drive
// the subst / const-enc / opaque / flatten / bogus / indirect L1 passes.
//
//   int vimovextbd256(int a, int c) {
//     int8x8 vb;                                   // low 8 bytes, arg-derived
//     int32x8 sx = (int32x8)vb;                    // vpmovsxbd (sign-extend)
//     uint32x8 zx = (uint32x8)(uint8x8)vb;         // vpmovzxbd (zero-extend)
//     int s = sum(sx[i]*(i+1)) + sum(zx[i]*(8-i));
//     ... data-dependent diamond ...
//   }
std::unique_ptr<llvm::Module> buildVecAvxIMovExtBD256IR(llvm::LLVMContext &Ctx,
                                                        const char *Triple) {
  auto M = std::make_unique<llvm::Module>("substtest", Ctx);
  M->setTargetTriple(llvm::Triple(Triple));
  llvm::Triple TT(Triple);
  bool IsX64 = TT.getArch() == llvm::Triple::x86_64;
  auto *I8 = llvm::Type::getInt8Ty(Ctx);
  auto *I32 = llvm::Type::getInt32Ty(Ctx);
  auto *V8b = llvm::FixedVectorType::get(I8, 8);
  auto *V8d = llvm::FixedVectorType::get(I32, 8);
  auto *FTy = llvm::FunctionType::get(I32, {I32, I32}, false);
  auto *F = llvm::Function::Create(FTy, llvm::Function::ExternalLinkage,
                                   "vimovextbd256", M.get());
  F->addFnAttr("min-legal-vector-width", "256");
  auto *Entry = llvm::BasicBlock::Create(Ctx, "entry", F);
  auto *Then = llvm::BasicBlock::Create(Ctx, "then", F);
  auto *Else = llvm::BasicBlock::Create(Ctx, "else", F);
  auto *Merge = llvm::BasicBlock::Create(Ctx, "merge", F);
  auto *A = F->getArg(0), *C = F->getArg(1);

  llvm::IRBuilder<> B(Entry);
  // The low 8 bytes of the source, each byte arg-derived and sign-mixed so the
  // sign-extend (vpmovsxbd) and zero-extend (vpmovzxbd) results diverge.
  llvm::Value *VB = llvm::UndefValue::get(V8b);
  for (unsigned I = 0; I < 8; ++I) {
    llvm::Value *Bv = B.CreateTrunc(
        B.CreateXor(B.CreateMul(A, B.getInt32(I * 0x95 + 3)),
                    B.CreateAdd(C, B.getInt32((uint32_t)((int)I - 4)))),
        I8);
    VB = B.CreateInsertElement(VB, Bv, uint64_t(I));
  }

  // +avx2 anchor (x86-64): keep the 256-bit YMM domain so the byte->dword widen
  // lowers to vpmovsxbd / vpmovzxbd ymm rather than split xmm widens.
  if (IsX64) {
    llvm::Value *VAa = llvm::UndefValue::get(V8d);
    llvm::Value *VSa = llvm::UndefValue::get(V8d);
    for (unsigned I = 0; I < 8; ++I) {
      VAa =
          B.CreateInsertElement(VAa, B.CreateAdd(A, B.getInt32(I)), uint64_t(I));
      VSa = B.CreateInsertElement(
          VSa, B.CreateAnd(B.CreateAdd(C, B.getInt32(I)), B.getInt32(7)),
          uint64_t(I));
    }
    (void)B.CreateIntrinsic(llvm::Intrinsic::x86_avx2_psllv_d_256, {},
                            {VAa, VSa});
  }

  // Byte->dword widen: sign-extend (vpmovsxbd) and zero-extend (vpmovzxbd).  The
  // auto-upgraded native form of llvm.x86.avx2.pmovsxbd / pmovzxbd is exactly a
  // <8 x i8> sext / zext to <8 x i32> (dst.d[i] = ext(src.b[i])).
  llvm::Value *SX = B.CreateSExt(VB, V8d);
  llvm::Value *ZX = B.CreateZExt(VB, V8d);

  // Reduce: sext dwords with ascending weights, zext dwords with descending
  // weights, so both widens -- and any byte where they differ -- are observable.
  llvm::Value *S = B.getInt32(0);
  for (unsigned L = 0; L < 8; ++L) {
    auto *Sw = B.CreateExtractElement(SX, uint64_t(L));
    auto *Zw = B.CreateExtractElement(ZX, uint64_t(L));
    S = B.CreateAdd(S, B.CreateMul(Sw, B.getInt32(L + 1)));
    S = B.CreateAdd(S, B.CreateMul(Zw, B.getInt32(8 - L)));
  }

  auto *T = B.CreateXor(B.CreateXor(B.CreateAdd(A, C), B.CreateSub(A, C)),
                        B.getInt32(0x7C7C));
  auto *U = B.CreateOr(B.CreateAnd(A, C), B.CreateAdd(T, B.getInt32(40903)));
  auto *Base = B.CreateAdd(S, U);
  B.CreateCondBr(B.CreateICmpNE(B.CreateAnd(B.CreateXor(A, C), B.getInt32(1)),
                                B.getInt32(0)),
                 Then, Else);

  B.SetInsertPoint(Then);
  auto *R1 = B.CreateAdd(Base, A);
  B.CreateBr(Merge);

  B.SetInsertPoint(Else);
  auto *R2 = B.CreateXor(Base, C);
  B.CreateBr(Merge);

  B.SetInsertPoint(Merge);
  auto *Pc = B.CreatePHI(I32, 2);
  Pc->addIncoming(R1, Then);
  Pc->addIncoming(R2, Else);
  B.CreateRet(Pc);
  assert(!llvm::verifyModule(*M, &llvm::errs()));
  return M;
}

// 256-bit AVX2 word->dword integer widening on YMM -- vpmovsxwd / vpmovzxwd
// (a 128-bit <8 x i16> source widened to a 256-bit <8 x i32> dest:
// dst.d[i] = ext(src.w[i]) for the eight lanes).  Completes the 2x widen trio
// alongside vimovextbw256 (byte->word) and vimovextdq256 (dword->qword): the
// middle word->dword step, the one whose source fills the whole 128-bit xmm yet
// produces i32 (not i16 or i64) lanes.  A decoder that mistakes the element
// stride (reading bytes instead of words, or the 4x word->qword form) mis-fills
// every dword lane.
//
// Cross-ISA: llvm.x86.avx2.pmovsxwd / pmovzxwd were auto-upgraded to native IR,
// i.e. a plain <8 x i16> sext / zext to <8 x i32>.  On x86-64 a dead
// llvm.x86.avx2.psllv.d.256 anchors +avx2 so the widen lowers to vpmovsxwd /
// vpmovzxwd ymm (one xmm source -> ymm dest) rather than two split xmm widens
// -- an undecoded YMM op faults the Unicorn baseline (UC_ERR_INSN_INVALID).
// Every other cell lowers the identical sext / zext to native widening moves
// (NEON sshll / ushll, split SSE), libcall-free.  Each source word is arg-derived
// and sign-mixed so sext (vpmovsxwd) and zext (vpmovzxwd) diverge; the eight
// sign-extended dwords carry ascending weights and the eight zero-extended
// dwords descending weights, so both widens -- and any word where they differ --
// are observable.  No L1 pass touches the widen sub-graph, so the original and
// obfuscated copies stay byte-identical over it, while integer add/sub/and/or/xor
// + non-folding constants (0x5B5B/47351) + a data-dependent diamond + PHI drive
// the subst / const-enc / opaque / flatten / bogus / indirect L1 passes.
//
//   int vimovextwd256(int a, int c) {
//     int16x8 vw;                                  // 128-bit, word arg-derived
//     int32x8 sx = (int32x8)vw;                    // vpmovsxwd (sign-extend)
//     uint32x8 zx = (uint32x8)(uint16x8)vw;        // vpmovzxwd (zero-extend)
//     int s = sum(sx[i]*(i+1)) + sum(zx[i]*(8-i));
//     ... data-dependent diamond ...
//   }
std::unique_ptr<llvm::Module> buildVecAvxIMovExtWD256IR(llvm::LLVMContext &Ctx,
                                                        const char *Triple) {
  auto M = std::make_unique<llvm::Module>("substtest", Ctx);
  M->setTargetTriple(llvm::Triple(Triple));
  llvm::Triple TT(Triple);
  bool IsX64 = TT.getArch() == llvm::Triple::x86_64;
  auto *I16 = llvm::Type::getInt16Ty(Ctx);
  auto *I32 = llvm::Type::getInt32Ty(Ctx);
  auto *V8w = llvm::FixedVectorType::get(I16, 8);
  auto *V8d = llvm::FixedVectorType::get(I32, 8);
  auto *FTy = llvm::FunctionType::get(I32, {I32, I32}, false);
  auto *F = llvm::Function::Create(FTy, llvm::Function::ExternalLinkage,
                                   "vimovextwd256", M.get());
  F->addFnAttr("min-legal-vector-width", "256");
  auto *Entry = llvm::BasicBlock::Create(Ctx, "entry", F);
  auto *Then = llvm::BasicBlock::Create(Ctx, "then", F);
  auto *Else = llvm::BasicBlock::Create(Ctx, "else", F);
  auto *Merge = llvm::BasicBlock::Create(Ctx, "merge", F);
  auto *A = F->getArg(0), *C = F->getArg(1);

  llvm::IRBuilder<> B(Entry);
  // A 128-bit <8 x i16> source, each word arg-derived and sign-mixed so the
  // sign-extend (vpmovsxwd) and zero-extend (vpmovzxwd) results diverge.
  llvm::Value *VW = llvm::UndefValue::get(V8w);
  for (unsigned I = 0; I < 8; ++I) {
    llvm::Value *Wv = B.CreateTrunc(
        B.CreateXor(B.CreateMul(A, B.getInt32(I * 0x4D3 + 5)),
                    B.CreateAdd(C, B.getInt32((uint32_t)((int)I - 4) * 0x111))),
        I16);
    VW = B.CreateInsertElement(VW, Wv, uint64_t(I));
  }

  // +avx2 anchor (x86-64): keep the 256-bit YMM domain so the word->dword widen
  // lowers to vpmovsxwd / vpmovzxwd ymm rather than two split xmm widens.
  if (IsX64) {
    llvm::Value *VAa = llvm::UndefValue::get(V8d);
    llvm::Value *VSa = llvm::UndefValue::get(V8d);
    for (unsigned I = 0; I < 8; ++I) {
      VAa =
          B.CreateInsertElement(VAa, B.CreateAdd(A, B.getInt32(I)), uint64_t(I));
      VSa = B.CreateInsertElement(
          VSa, B.CreateAnd(B.CreateAdd(C, B.getInt32(I)), B.getInt32(7)),
          uint64_t(I));
    }
    (void)B.CreateIntrinsic(llvm::Intrinsic::x86_avx2_psllv_d_256, {},
                            {VAa, VSa});
  }

  // Word->dword widen: sign-extend (vpmovsxwd) and zero-extend (vpmovzxwd).  The
  // auto-upgraded native form of llvm.x86.avx2.pmovsxwd / pmovzxwd is exactly a
  // <8 x i16> sext / zext to <8 x i32> (dst.d[i] = ext(src.w[i])).
  llvm::Value *SX = B.CreateSExt(VW, V8d);
  llvm::Value *ZX = B.CreateZExt(VW, V8d);

  // Reduce: sext dwords with ascending weights, zext dwords with descending
  // weights, so both widens -- and any word where they differ -- are observable.
  llvm::Value *S = B.getInt32(0);
  for (unsigned L = 0; L < 8; ++L) {
    auto *Sw = B.CreateExtractElement(SX, uint64_t(L));
    auto *Zw = B.CreateExtractElement(ZX, uint64_t(L));
    S = B.CreateAdd(S, B.CreateMul(Sw, B.getInt32(L + 1)));
    S = B.CreateAdd(S, B.CreateMul(Zw, B.getInt32(8 - L)));
  }

  auto *T = B.CreateXor(B.CreateXor(B.CreateAdd(A, C), B.CreateSub(A, C)),
                        B.getInt32(0x5B5B));
  auto *U = B.CreateOr(B.CreateAnd(A, C), B.CreateAdd(T, B.getInt32(47351)));
  auto *Base = B.CreateAdd(S, U);
  B.CreateCondBr(B.CreateICmpNE(B.CreateAnd(B.CreateXor(A, C), B.getInt32(1)),
                                B.getInt32(0)),
                 Then, Else);

  B.SetInsertPoint(Then);
  auto *R1 = B.CreateAdd(Base, A);
  B.CreateBr(Merge);

  B.SetInsertPoint(Else);
  auto *R2 = B.CreateXor(Base, C);
  B.CreateBr(Merge);

  B.SetInsertPoint(Merge);
  auto *Pc = B.CreatePHI(I32, 2);
  Pc->addIncoming(R1, Then);
  Pc->addIncoming(R2, Else);
  B.CreateRet(Pc);
  assert(!llvm::verifyModule(*M, &llvm::errs()));
  return M;
}

// 256-bit AVX2 word->qword integer widening on YMM -- vpmovsxwq / vpmovzxwq
// (the low 4 words of a 128-bit source widened to a 256-bit <4 x i64> dest:
// dst.q[i] = ext(src.w[i]) for the four lanes).  Sibling of vimovextbd256
// (byte->dword, 4x) at the *other* 4x step: a word->qword widen that consumes
// only eight source bytes (four words) yet spans the full 256-bit register.
// Because it discards words 4-7 of the xmm source, a decoder that mistakes it
// for the 2x word->dword form (consuming eight words) or that mis-strides the
// source words mis-fills every qword lane.
//
// Cross-ISA: llvm.x86.avx2.pmovsxwq / pmovzxwq were auto-upgraded to native IR,
// i.e. a plain <4 x i16> sext / zext to <4 x i64>.  On x86-64 a dead
// llvm.x86.avx2.psllv.d.256 anchors +avx2 so the widen lowers to vpmovsxwq /
// vpmovzxwq ymm (one xmm source -> ymm dest) rather than split xmm widens -- an
// undecoded YMM op faults the Unicorn baseline (UC_ERR_INSN_INVALID).  Every
// other cell lowers the identical sext / zext to native widening moves (NEON
// sshll/ushll chains, split SSE), libcall-free.  Each source word is arg-derived
// and sign-mixed so sext (vpmovsxwq) and zext (vpmovzxwq) diverge; each 64-bit
// lane is folded (lo ^ hi) so the sign-fill high dword (sext) vs zero (zext) is
// observable, with distinct ascending / descending per-lane weights.  No L1 pass
// touches the widen sub-graph, so the original and obfuscated copies stay
// byte-identical over it, while integer add/sub/and/or/xor + non-folding
// constants (0x6D6D/53617) + a data-dependent diamond + PHI drive the subst /
// const-enc / opaque / flatten / bogus / indirect L1 passes.
//
//   int vimovextwq256(int a, int c) {
//     int16x4 vw;                                  // low 4 words, arg-derived
//     int64x4 sx = (int64x4)vw;                    // vpmovsxwq (sign-extend)
//     uint64x4 zx = (uint64x4)(uint16x4)vw;        // vpmovzxwq (zero-extend)
//     int s = sum((lo^hi)(sx[i])*(i+1)) + sum((lo^hi)(zx[i])*(8-i));
//     ... data-dependent diamond ...
//   }
std::unique_ptr<llvm::Module> buildVecAvxIMovExtWQ256IR(llvm::LLVMContext &Ctx,
                                                        const char *Triple) {
  auto M = std::make_unique<llvm::Module>("substtest", Ctx);
  M->setTargetTriple(llvm::Triple(Triple));
  llvm::Triple TT(Triple);
  bool IsX64 = TT.getArch() == llvm::Triple::x86_64;
  auto *I16 = llvm::Type::getInt16Ty(Ctx);
  auto *I32 = llvm::Type::getInt32Ty(Ctx);
  auto *I64 = llvm::Type::getInt64Ty(Ctx);
  auto *V4w = llvm::FixedVectorType::get(I16, 4);
  auto *V4q = llvm::FixedVectorType::get(I64, 4);
  auto *V8d = llvm::FixedVectorType::get(I32, 8);
  auto *FTy = llvm::FunctionType::get(I32, {I32, I32}, false);
  auto *F = llvm::Function::Create(FTy, llvm::Function::ExternalLinkage,
                                   "vimovextwq256", M.get());
  F->addFnAttr("min-legal-vector-width", "256");
  auto *Entry = llvm::BasicBlock::Create(Ctx, "entry", F);
  auto *Then = llvm::BasicBlock::Create(Ctx, "then", F);
  auto *Else = llvm::BasicBlock::Create(Ctx, "else", F);
  auto *Merge = llvm::BasicBlock::Create(Ctx, "merge", F);
  auto *A = F->getArg(0), *C = F->getArg(1);

  llvm::IRBuilder<> B(Entry);
  // The low 4 words of the source, each word arg-derived and sign-mixed so the
  // sign-extend (vpmovsxwq) and zero-extend (vpmovzxwq) results diverge.
  llvm::Value *VW = llvm::UndefValue::get(V4w);
  for (unsigned I = 0; I < 4; ++I) {
    llvm::Value *Wv = B.CreateTrunc(
        B.CreateXor(B.CreateMul(A, B.getInt32(I * 0x6B5 + 9)),
                    B.CreateAdd(C, B.getInt32((uint32_t)((int)I - 2) * 0x131))),
        I16);
    VW = B.CreateInsertElement(VW, Wv, uint64_t(I));
  }

  // +avx2 anchor (x86-64): keep the 256-bit YMM domain so the word->qword widen
  // lowers to vpmovsxwq / vpmovzxwq ymm rather than split xmm widens.
  if (IsX64) {
    llvm::Value *VAa = llvm::UndefValue::get(V8d);
    llvm::Value *VSa = llvm::UndefValue::get(V8d);
    for (unsigned I = 0; I < 8; ++I) {
      VAa =
          B.CreateInsertElement(VAa, B.CreateAdd(A, B.getInt32(I)), uint64_t(I));
      VSa = B.CreateInsertElement(
          VSa, B.CreateAnd(B.CreateAdd(C, B.getInt32(I)), B.getInt32(7)),
          uint64_t(I));
    }
    (void)B.CreateIntrinsic(llvm::Intrinsic::x86_avx2_psllv_d_256, {},
                            {VAa, VSa});
  }

  // Word->qword widen: sign-extend (vpmovsxwq) and zero-extend (vpmovzxwq).  The
  // auto-upgraded native form of llvm.x86.avx2.pmovsxwq / pmovzxwq is exactly a
  // <4 x i16> sext / zext to <4 x i64> (dst.q[i] = ext(src.w[i])).
  llvm::Value *SX = B.CreateSExt(VW, V4q);
  llvm::Value *ZX = B.CreateZExt(VW, V4q);

  // Fold each 64-bit result (lo ^ hi) so the sign-fill high dword (sext) vs zero
  // (zext) is observable, with distinct ascending / descending per-lane weights.
  llvm::Value *S = B.getInt32(0);
  for (unsigned L = 0; L < 4; ++L) {
    llvm::Value *E = B.CreateExtractElement(SX, uint64_t(L));
    llvm::Value *Lo = B.CreateTrunc(E, I32);
    llvm::Value *Hi = B.CreateTrunc(B.CreateLShr(E, B.getInt64(32)), I32);
    S = B.CreateAdd(S, B.CreateMul(B.CreateXor(Lo, Hi), B.getInt32(L + 1)));
  }
  for (unsigned L = 0; L < 4; ++L) {
    llvm::Value *E = B.CreateExtractElement(ZX, uint64_t(L));
    llvm::Value *Lo = B.CreateTrunc(E, I32);
    llvm::Value *Hi = B.CreateTrunc(B.CreateLShr(E, B.getInt64(32)), I32);
    S = B.CreateAdd(S, B.CreateMul(B.CreateXor(Lo, Hi), B.getInt32(8 - L)));
  }

  auto *T = B.CreateXor(B.CreateXor(B.CreateAdd(A, C), B.CreateSub(A, C)),
                        B.getInt32(0x6D6D));
  auto *U = B.CreateOr(B.CreateAnd(A, C), B.CreateAdd(T, B.getInt32(53617)));
  auto *Base = B.CreateAdd(S, U);
  B.CreateCondBr(B.CreateICmpNE(B.CreateAnd(B.CreateXor(A, C), B.getInt32(1)),
                                B.getInt32(0)),
                 Then, Else);

  B.SetInsertPoint(Then);
  auto *R1 = B.CreateAdd(Base, A);
  B.CreateBr(Merge);

  B.SetInsertPoint(Else);
  auto *R2 = B.CreateXor(Base, C);
  B.CreateBr(Merge);

  B.SetInsertPoint(Merge);
  auto *Pc = B.CreatePHI(I32, 2);
  Pc->addIncoming(R1, Then);
  Pc->addIncoming(R2, Else);
  B.CreateRet(Pc);
  assert(!llvm::verifyModule(*M, &llvm::errs()));
  return M;
}

// 256-bit AVX2 byte->qword integer widening on YMM -- vpmovsxbq / vpmovzxbq
// (the low 4 bytes of a 128-bit source widened to a 256-bit <4 x i64> dest:
// dst.q[i] = ext(src.b[i]) for the four lanes).  The widest widen of the
// pmovsx/pmovzx family: an 8x byte->qword step that consumes only four source
// bytes yet spans the full 256-bit register, completing the family alongside the
// 2x (vimovextbw256/wd256/dq256) and 4x (vimovextbd256/wq256) forms.  Because it
// discards bytes 4-15 of the xmm source, a decoder that mistakes it for a
// narrower stride (the 4x byte->dword form, or reading words) mis-fills every
// qword lane.
//
// Cross-ISA: llvm.x86.avx2.pmovsxbq / pmovzxbq were auto-upgraded to native IR,
// i.e. a plain <4 x i8> sext / zext to <4 x i64>.  On x86-64 a dead
// llvm.x86.avx2.psllv.d.256 anchors +avx2 so the widen lowers to vpmovsxbq /
// vpmovzxbq ymm (one xmm source -> ymm dest) rather than split xmm widens -- an
// undecoded YMM op faults the Unicorn baseline (UC_ERR_INSN_INVALID).  Every
// other cell lowers the identical sext / zext to native widening moves (NEON
// sshll/ushll chains, split SSE), libcall-free.  Each source byte is arg-derived
// and sign-mixed so sext (vpmovsxbq) and zext (vpmovzxbq) diverge; each 64-bit
// lane is folded (lo ^ hi) so the sign-fill high dword (sext) vs zero (zext) is
// observable, with distinct ascending / descending per-lane weights.  No L1 pass
// touches the widen sub-graph, so the original and obfuscated copies stay
// byte-identical over it, while integer add/sub/and/or/xor + non-folding
// constants (0x7E7E/58393) + a data-dependent diamond + PHI drive the subst /
// const-enc / opaque / flatten / bogus / indirect L1 passes.
//
//   int vimovextbq256(int a, int c) {
//     int8x4 vb;                                   // low 4 bytes, arg-derived
//     int64x4 sx = (int64x4)vb;                    // vpmovsxbq (sign-extend)
//     uint64x4 zx = (uint64x4)(uint8x4)vb;         // vpmovzxbq (zero-extend)
//     int s = sum((lo^hi)(sx[i])*(i+1)) + sum((lo^hi)(zx[i])*(8-i));
//     ... data-dependent diamond ...
//   }
std::unique_ptr<llvm::Module> buildVecAvxIMovExtBQ256IR(llvm::LLVMContext &Ctx,
                                                        const char *Triple) {
  auto M = std::make_unique<llvm::Module>("substtest", Ctx);
  M->setTargetTriple(llvm::Triple(Triple));
  llvm::Triple TT(Triple);
  bool IsX64 = TT.getArch() == llvm::Triple::x86_64;
  auto *I8 = llvm::Type::getInt8Ty(Ctx);
  auto *I32 = llvm::Type::getInt32Ty(Ctx);
  auto *I64 = llvm::Type::getInt64Ty(Ctx);
  auto *V4b = llvm::FixedVectorType::get(I8, 4);
  auto *V4q = llvm::FixedVectorType::get(I64, 4);
  auto *V8d = llvm::FixedVectorType::get(I32, 8);
  auto *FTy = llvm::FunctionType::get(I32, {I32, I32}, false);
  auto *F = llvm::Function::Create(FTy, llvm::Function::ExternalLinkage,
                                   "vimovextbq256", M.get());
  F->addFnAttr("min-legal-vector-width", "256");
  auto *Entry = llvm::BasicBlock::Create(Ctx, "entry", F);
  auto *Then = llvm::BasicBlock::Create(Ctx, "then", F);
  auto *Else = llvm::BasicBlock::Create(Ctx, "else", F);
  auto *Merge = llvm::BasicBlock::Create(Ctx, "merge", F);
  auto *A = F->getArg(0), *C = F->getArg(1);

  llvm::IRBuilder<> B(Entry);
  // The low 4 bytes of the source, each byte arg-derived and sign-mixed so the
  // sign-extend (vpmovsxbq) and zero-extend (vpmovzxbq) results diverge.
  llvm::Value *VB = llvm::UndefValue::get(V4b);
  for (unsigned I = 0; I < 4; ++I) {
    llvm::Value *Bv = B.CreateTrunc(
        B.CreateXor(B.CreateMul(A, B.getInt32(I * 0x71 + 11)),
                    B.CreateAdd(C, B.getInt32((uint32_t)((int)I - 2) * 0x17))),
        I8);
    VB = B.CreateInsertElement(VB, Bv, uint64_t(I));
  }

  // +avx2 anchor (x86-64): keep the 256-bit YMM domain so the byte->qword widen
  // lowers to vpmovsxbq / vpmovzxbq ymm rather than split xmm widens.
  if (IsX64) {
    llvm::Value *VAa = llvm::UndefValue::get(V8d);
    llvm::Value *VSa = llvm::UndefValue::get(V8d);
    for (unsigned I = 0; I < 8; ++I) {
      VAa =
          B.CreateInsertElement(VAa, B.CreateAdd(A, B.getInt32(I)), uint64_t(I));
      VSa = B.CreateInsertElement(
          VSa, B.CreateAnd(B.CreateAdd(C, B.getInt32(I)), B.getInt32(7)),
          uint64_t(I));
    }
    (void)B.CreateIntrinsic(llvm::Intrinsic::x86_avx2_psllv_d_256, {},
                            {VAa, VSa});
  }

  // Byte->qword widen: sign-extend (vpmovsxbq) and zero-extend (vpmovzxbq).  The
  // auto-upgraded native form of llvm.x86.avx2.pmovsxbq / pmovzxbq is exactly a
  // <4 x i8> sext / zext to <4 x i64> (dst.q[i] = ext(src.b[i])).
  llvm::Value *SX = B.CreateSExt(VB, V4q);
  llvm::Value *ZX = B.CreateZExt(VB, V4q);

  // Fold each 64-bit result (lo ^ hi) so the sign-fill high dword (sext) vs zero
  // (zext) is observable, with distinct ascending / descending per-lane weights.
  llvm::Value *S = B.getInt32(0);
  for (unsigned L = 0; L < 4; ++L) {
    llvm::Value *E = B.CreateExtractElement(SX, uint64_t(L));
    llvm::Value *Lo = B.CreateTrunc(E, I32);
    llvm::Value *Hi = B.CreateTrunc(B.CreateLShr(E, B.getInt64(32)), I32);
    S = B.CreateAdd(S, B.CreateMul(B.CreateXor(Lo, Hi), B.getInt32(L + 1)));
  }
  for (unsigned L = 0; L < 4; ++L) {
    llvm::Value *E = B.CreateExtractElement(ZX, uint64_t(L));
    llvm::Value *Lo = B.CreateTrunc(E, I32);
    llvm::Value *Hi = B.CreateTrunc(B.CreateLShr(E, B.getInt64(32)), I32);
    S = B.CreateAdd(S, B.CreateMul(B.CreateXor(Lo, Hi), B.getInt32(8 - L)));
  }

  auto *T = B.CreateXor(B.CreateXor(B.CreateAdd(A, C), B.CreateSub(A, C)),
                        B.getInt32(0x7E7E));
  auto *U = B.CreateOr(B.CreateAnd(A, C), B.CreateAdd(T, B.getInt32(58393)));
  auto *Base = B.CreateAdd(S, U);
  B.CreateCondBr(B.CreateICmpNE(B.CreateAnd(B.CreateXor(A, C), B.getInt32(1)),
                                B.getInt32(0)),
                 Then, Else);

  B.SetInsertPoint(Then);
  auto *R1 = B.CreateAdd(Base, A);
  B.CreateBr(Merge);

  B.SetInsertPoint(Else);
  auto *R2 = B.CreateXor(Base, C);
  B.CreateBr(Merge);

  B.SetInsertPoint(Merge);
  auto *Pc = B.CreatePHI(I32, 2);
  Pc->addIncoming(R1, Then);
  Pc->addIncoming(R2, Else);
  B.CreateRet(Pc);
  assert(!llvm::verifyModule(*M, &llvm::errs()));
  return M;
}

// 256-bit AVX floating-point runtime variable blend on YMM -- vblendvps
// (<8 x float>, dword lane, mask bit 31) and vblendvpd (<4 x double>, qword
// lane, mask bit 63).  This is the floating-point dual of the byte-granular
// integer viblendvb256 (vpblendvb): where vpblendvb selects per byte from a
// runtime <32 x i8> mask, vblendvps/vblendvpd select per dword/qword from a
// runtime float/double-domain mask, exercising the wider-lane, FP-domain
// variable-blend path no prior 256-bit shape reaches.  Like vpblendvb they use
// the 4-operand VEX /is4 encoding (the mask register is named in imm8[7:4]), but
// a decoder that read the mask per byte, dropped the high 128-bit lane, or
// treated it as an immediate blend would mis-select lanes -- a classic mis-decode
// magnet.  fork-Unicorn already decodes vblendvps (0F3A 4A) and vblendvpd
// (0F3A 4B) in the same gen_sse_256 branch as the covered vpblendvb (0F3A 4C,
// esz=1), so this needs no Unicorn change; it is the first end-to-end exercise of
// the 4A/4B (dword/qword) arms through the rewrite/patch chain.
//
// Cross-ISA: the x86-64 cell pins the dedicated intrinsics
// llvm.x86.avx.blendv.ps.256 / blendv.pd.256 (the "avx" substring makes
// detectTargetFeaturesX86 add +avx), which lower straight to vblendvps /
// vblendvpd ymm.  Every other cell open-codes the identical sign-bit select --
// select(icmp slt <8 x i32>/<4 x i64> mask, 0, b, a), matching the intrinsic's
// "lane = (mask < 0) ? b : a" semantics -- over the SAME integer masks (NEON bsl
// / scalarised, zero libcall on every ISA; no FP touches the non-x86 masks at
// all).  The two runtime masks are input-derived so their sign bits vary at
// runtime -- LLVM cannot fold to a constant blend, so the real variable
// vblendvps/vblendvpd survive to the machine layer.  Data lanes are exact small
// integers via scalar sitofp, so the blend (pure lane move) and the fptosi back
// are bit-exact with no rounding; the two blends swap sources so both are
// observable, and their lanes are reduced with ascending (ps) / descending (pd)
// per-lane weights so any mis-routed lane changes the sum.  No obfuscation pass
// touches the blend sub-graph (orig/obf byte-identical over it); an undecoded YMM
// blend faults the Unicorn baseline (UC_ERR_INSN_INVALID) and any value
// divergence is a genuine backend / fork-Unicorn bug.  Integer add/sub/and/or/xor
// + non-folding constants (0x6D6D/27983) + a data-dependent diamond + PHI drive
// the subst/const-enc/opaque/flatten/bogus/indirect passes.
std::unique_ptr<llvm::Module> buildVecAvxBlendV256IR(llvm::LLVMContext &Ctx,
                                                     const char *Triple) {
  auto M = std::make_unique<llvm::Module>("substtest", Ctx);
  M->setTargetTriple(llvm::Triple(Triple));
  llvm::Triple TT(Triple);
  bool IsX64 = TT.getArch() == llvm::Triple::x86_64;
  auto *I32 = llvm::Type::getInt32Ty(Ctx);
  auto *I64 = llvm::Type::getInt64Ty(Ctx);
  auto *Flt = llvm::Type::getFloatTy(Ctx);
  auto *Dbl = llvm::Type::getDoubleTy(Ctx);
  auto *V8f = llvm::FixedVectorType::get(Flt, 8);
  auto *V8i = llvm::FixedVectorType::get(I32, 8);
  auto *V4d = llvm::FixedVectorType::get(Dbl, 4);
  auto *V4q = llvm::FixedVectorType::get(I64, 4);
  auto *V4i = llvm::FixedVectorType::get(I32, 4);
  auto *FTy = llvm::FunctionType::get(I32, {I32, I32}, false);
  auto *F = llvm::Function::Create(FTy, llvm::Function::ExternalLinkage,
                                   "vblendv256", M.get());
  F->addFnAttr("min-legal-vector-width", "256");
  auto *Entry = llvm::BasicBlock::Create(Ctx, "entry", F);
  auto *Then = llvm::BasicBlock::Create(Ctx, "then", F);
  auto *Else = llvm::BasicBlock::Create(Ctx, "else", F);
  auto *Merge = llvm::BasicBlock::Create(Ctx, "merge", F);
  auto *A = F->getArg(0), *C = F->getArg(1);

  llvm::IRBuilder<> B(Entry);
  // Small (<~1060) so every sitofp lane is an exact integer float and every
  // fptosi back stays in range on all ISAs (no rounding, no overflow).
  auto *Alo = B.CreateAnd(A, B.getInt32(1023));
  auto *Clo = B.CreateAnd(C, B.getInt32(1023));

  // <8 x float> data sources + a runtime per-dword mask (bit 31 varies).
  llvm::Value *PsA = llvm::UndefValue::get(V8f);
  llvm::Value *PsB = llvm::UndefValue::get(V8f);
  llvm::Value *MaskPs = llvm::UndefValue::get(V8i);
  for (unsigned I = 0; I < 8; ++I) {
    PsA = B.CreateInsertElement(
        PsA, B.CreateSIToFP(B.CreateAdd(Alo, B.getInt32(I * 3 + 1)), Flt),
        uint64_t(I));
    PsB = B.CreateInsertElement(
        PsB, B.CreateSIToFP(B.CreateAdd(Clo, B.getInt32(I * 5 + 2)), Flt),
        uint64_t(I));
    MaskPs = B.CreateInsertElement(
        MaskPs,
        B.CreateXor(B.CreateMul(A, B.getInt32(I * 0x1B7 + 5)),
                    B.CreateAdd(C, B.getInt32((uint32_t)((int)I - 4)))),
        uint64_t(I));
  }

  // <4 x double> data sources + a runtime per-qword mask (bit 63 varies via a
  // sign-extended runtime i32).
  llvm::Value *PdA = llvm::UndefValue::get(V4d);
  llvm::Value *PdB = llvm::UndefValue::get(V4d);
  llvm::Value *MaskPd = llvm::UndefValue::get(V4q);
  for (unsigned I = 0; I < 4; ++I) {
    PdA = B.CreateInsertElement(
        PdA, B.CreateSIToFP(B.CreateAdd(Alo, B.getInt32(I * 7)), Dbl),
        uint64_t(I));
    PdB = B.CreateInsertElement(
        PdB, B.CreateSIToFP(B.CreateAdd(Clo, B.getInt32(I * 9 + 3)), Dbl),
        uint64_t(I));
    llvm::Value *Mv = B.CreateXor(B.CreateMul(C, B.getInt32(I * 13 + 7)),
                                  B.CreateAdd(A, B.getInt32(I + 1)));
    MaskPd = B.CreateInsertElement(MaskPd, B.CreateSExt(Mv, I64), uint64_t(I));
  }

  // vblendvps ymm / vblendvpd ymm on x86-64; sign-bit select over the same
  // integer masks elsewhere.  Both give lane = (mask < 0) ? b : a; the two
  // blends swap sources so each source is observed.
  llvm::Value *BlPs =
      IsX64 ? B.CreateIntrinsic(llvm::Intrinsic::x86_avx_blendv_ps_256, {},
                                {PsA, PsB, B.CreateBitCast(MaskPs, V8f)})
            : B.CreateSelect(
                  B.CreateICmpSLT(MaskPs, llvm::Constant::getNullValue(V8i)),
                  PsB, PsA);
  llvm::Value *BlPd =
      IsX64 ? B.CreateIntrinsic(llvm::Intrinsic::x86_avx_blendv_pd_256, {},
                                {PdB, PdA, B.CreateBitCast(MaskPd, V4d)})
            : B.CreateSelect(
                  B.CreateICmpSLT(MaskPd, llvm::Constant::getNullValue(V4q)),
                  PdA, PdB);

  auto *PsI = B.CreateFPToSI(BlPs, V8i);
  auto *PdI = B.CreateFPToSI(BlPd, V4i);
  llvm::Value *S = B.getInt32(0);
  for (unsigned L = 0; L < 8; ++L)
    S = B.CreateAdd(S, B.CreateMul(B.CreateExtractElement(PsI, uint64_t(L)),
                                   B.getInt32(L + 1)));
  for (unsigned L = 0; L < 4; ++L)
    S = B.CreateAdd(S, B.CreateMul(B.CreateExtractElement(PdI, uint64_t(L)),
                                   B.getInt32(4 - L)));

  auto *T = B.CreateXor(B.CreateXor(B.CreateAdd(A, C), B.CreateSub(A, C)),
                        B.getInt32(0x6D6D));
  auto *U = B.CreateOr(B.CreateAnd(A, C), B.CreateAdd(T, B.getInt32(27983)));
  auto *Base = B.CreateAdd(S, U);
  B.CreateCondBr(B.CreateICmpNE(B.CreateAnd(B.CreateXor(A, C), B.getInt32(1)),
                                B.getInt32(0)),
                 Then, Else);

  B.SetInsertPoint(Then);
  auto *R1 = B.CreateAdd(Base, A);
  B.CreateBr(Merge);

  B.SetInsertPoint(Else);
  auto *R2 = B.CreateXor(Base, C);
  B.CreateBr(Merge);

  B.SetInsertPoint(Merge);
  auto *Pc = B.CreatePHI(I32, 2);
  Pc->addIncoming(R1, Then);
  Pc->addIncoming(R2, Else);
  B.CreateRet(Pc);
  assert(!llvm::verifyModule(*M, &llvm::errs()));
  return M;
}

// Vector floating-point — completes the FP dimension (ffp covers scalar double;
// this covers a <4 x float> SIMD vector).  Exercises the vector FP codegen
// path: vector sitofp/fmul/fadd, vector fptosi, and — the headline — *two
// distinct <4 x float> constants* that lower to a 16-byte mergeable-constant
// pool entry
// (.rodata.cst16 on ELF, __literal16 on Mach-O, and a per-constant COMDAT
// .rdata on COFF), exactly the same multi-read-only / COFF-COMDAT layout the
// integer-vector vbyte/vmix samples stress, now in floating point.  Every op
// lowers to hardware SIMD (SSE mulps/addps/cvttps2dq on x86, NEON
// vmul.f32/vcvt on ARM/AArch64) — fptosi targets <4 x i32> (NOT i64), and the
// inputs are pre-scaled by 2^-5 so each lane stays well below 2^31, so the
// conversion never overflows and there is no libcall on any ISA.  The vector is
// reduced to a scalar (lane sum) for the harness's integer return, and integer
// add/sub/and/or/xor + integer constants drive --subst / --const-enc; no pass
// touches the FP vector sub-graph, so it is identical in both copies.
//
//   int fvec(int a, int b) {
//     float fa = (float)a * 0.03125f, fb = (float)b * 0.03125f;
//     float4 v = { fa, fb, fa + fb, fa - fb };
//     float4 q = v * (float4){1.5,0.5,0.25,2.0} + (float4){0.1,0.2,0.3,0.4};
//     int4  qi = (int4)q;                         // |lane| < 2^31
//     int   s  = qi[0] + qi[1] + qi[2] + qi[3];
//     int   t    = ((a + b) ^ (a - b)) ^ 0x33;
//     int   u    = (a & b) | (t + 777);
//     int   base = s + u;
//     return ((a ^ b) & 1) ? base + a : base ^ b;  // branch ->
//     flatten/indirect
//   }
std::unique_ptr<llvm::Module> buildFloatVecIR(llvm::LLVMContext &Ctx,
                                              const char *Triple) {
  auto M = std::make_unique<llvm::Module>("substtest", Ctx);
  M->setTargetTriple(llvm::Triple(Triple));
  auto *I32 = llvm::Type::getInt32Ty(Ctx);
  auto *Flt = llvm::Type::getFloatTy(Ctx);
  auto *V4f = llvm::FixedVectorType::get(Flt, 4);
  auto *V4i = llvm::FixedVectorType::get(I32, 4);
  auto *FTy = llvm::FunctionType::get(I32, {I32, I32}, false);
  auto *F = llvm::Function::Create(FTy, llvm::Function::ExternalLinkage, "fvec",
                                   M.get());
  auto *Entry = llvm::BasicBlock::Create(Ctx, "entry", F);
  auto *Then = llvm::BasicBlock::Create(Ctx, "then", F);
  auto *Else = llvm::BasicBlock::Create(Ctx, "else", F);
  auto *Merge = llvm::BasicBlock::Create(Ctx, "merge", F);
  auto *A = F->getArg(0), *C = F->getArg(1);

  llvm::IRBuilder<> B(Entry);
  // 2^-5 scale keeps every lane below 2^31 so the vector fptosi never
  // overflows.
  auto *Scale = llvm::ConstantFP::get(Flt, 0.03125);
  auto *Fa = B.CreateFMul(B.CreateSIToFP(A, Flt), Scale);
  auto *Fb = B.CreateFMul(B.CreateSIToFP(C, Flt), Scale);
  llvm::Value *V = llvm::UndefValue::get(V4f);
  V = B.CreateInsertElement(V, Fa, uint64_t(0));
  V = B.CreateInsertElement(V, Fb, uint64_t(1));
  V = B.CreateInsertElement(V, B.CreateFAdd(Fa, Fb), uint64_t(2));
  V = B.CreateInsertElement(V, B.CreateFSub(Fa, Fb), uint64_t(3));
  // Two <4 x float> constants -> 16-byte pool (.rodata.cst16 / __literal16 /
  // COFF COMDAT .rdata) — the FP counterpart of vbyte/vmix's constant merging.
  float KElems[] = {1.5f, 0.5f, 0.25f, 2.0f};
  float OffElems[] = {0.1f, 0.2f, 0.3f, 0.4f};
  auto *K = llvm::ConstantDataVector::get(Ctx, KElems);
  auto *Off = llvm::ConstantDataVector::get(Ctx, OffElems);
  auto *Q = B.CreateFAdd(B.CreateFMul(V, K), Off);
  auto *Qi = B.CreateFPToSI(Q, V4i);
  auto *S = B.CreateAdd(B.CreateAdd(B.CreateExtractElement(Qi, uint64_t(0)),
                                    B.CreateExtractElement(Qi, uint64_t(1))),
                        B.CreateAdd(B.CreateExtractElement(Qi, uint64_t(2)),
                                    B.CreateExtractElement(Qi, uint64_t(3))));
  auto *T = B.CreateXor(B.CreateXor(B.CreateAdd(A, C), B.CreateSub(A, C)),
                        B.getInt32(0x33));
  auto *U = B.CreateOr(B.CreateAnd(A, C), B.CreateAdd(T, B.getInt32(777)));
  auto *Base = B.CreateAdd(S, U);
  // A data-dependent branch so the control-flow passes (flatten / indirect)
  // have real structure to transform — they no-op on a single straight-line
  // block (vbyte/vmix carry one too); the vector FP work above is identical in
  // both copies regardless.
  auto *Sel = B.CreateAnd(B.CreateXor(A, C), B.getInt32(1));
  B.CreateCondBr(B.CreateICmpNE(Sel, B.getInt32(0)), Then, Else);

  B.SetInsertPoint(Then);
  auto *RT = B.CreateAdd(Base, A);
  B.CreateBr(Merge);
  B.SetInsertPoint(Else);
  auto *RE = B.CreateXor(Base, C);
  B.CreateBr(Merge);

  B.SetInsertPoint(Merge);
  auto *Res = B.CreatePHI(I32, 2, "res");
  Res->addIncoming(RT, Then);
  Res->addIncoming(RE, Else);
  B.CreateRet(Res);
  assert(!llvm::verifyModule(*M, &llvm::errs()));
  return M;
}

// Vector double-precision — the 64-bit-lane sibling of fvec's <4 x float>.
// fvec packs 4 single-precision lanes into one 128-bit SIMD register; this
// packs 2 *double* lanes, hitting a completely distinct backend opcode family:
// SSE2 mulpd/addpd/cvttpd2dq on x86, NEON fmul/fadd over <2 x f64> + fcvtzs on
// AArch64, and — because 32-bit NEON has NO double-precision SIMD — a
// *scalarized* pair of VFP vmul.f64/vadd.f64/vcvt.s32.f64 on ARM32 (a path
// neither ffp's scalar double nor fvec's single-precision vector reaches).  The
// two <2 x double> constants lower to a 16-byte mergeable-constant pool entry
// (.rodata.cst16 / __literal16 / per-constant COFF COMDAT .rdata) exactly like
// fvec, now carrying f64 values — the double-precision dual of vbyte/vmix/fvec
// constant merging.  fptosi targets <2 x i32> (NOT i64) and the inputs are
// pre-scaled by 2^-5 so every lane stays well below 2^31 → the conversion never
// overflows and there is no __aeabi/_d2lz-style libcall on any ISA.  The vector
// is reduced to a scalar (lane sum) for the harness's integer return; integer
// add/sub/and/or/xor + integer constants drive --subst / --const-enc and a
// data-dependent branch gives the control-flow passes real structure, while no
// pass touches the FP vector sub-graph (identical in both copies → any
// divergence is a genuine backend bug).
//
//   int dvec2(int a, int b) {
//     double da = (double)a * 0.03125, db = (double)b * 0.03125;
//     double2 v = { da, db };
//     double2 q = v * (double2){1.5,0.5} + (double2){0.1,0.2};
//     int2   qi = (int2)q;                        // |lane| < 2^31
//     int    s  = qi[0] + qi[1];
//     int    t  = ((a + b) ^ (a - b)) ^ 0x33;
//     int    u  = (a & b) | (t + 777);
//     int    base = s + u;
//     return ((a ^ b) & 1) ? base + a : base ^ b; // branch -> flatten/indirect
//   }
std::unique_ptr<llvm::Module> buildFloatDVecIR(llvm::LLVMContext &Ctx,
                                               const char *Triple) {
  auto M = std::make_unique<llvm::Module>("substtest", Ctx);
  M->setTargetTriple(llvm::Triple(Triple));
  auto *I32 = llvm::Type::getInt32Ty(Ctx);
  auto *Dbl = llvm::Type::getDoubleTy(Ctx);
  auto *V2d = llvm::FixedVectorType::get(Dbl, 2);
  auto *V2i = llvm::FixedVectorType::get(I32, 2);
  auto *FTy = llvm::FunctionType::get(I32, {I32, I32}, false);
  auto *F = llvm::Function::Create(FTy, llvm::Function::ExternalLinkage,
                                   "dvec2", M.get());
  auto *Entry = llvm::BasicBlock::Create(Ctx, "entry", F);
  auto *Then = llvm::BasicBlock::Create(Ctx, "then", F);
  auto *Else = llvm::BasicBlock::Create(Ctx, "else", F);
  auto *Merge = llvm::BasicBlock::Create(Ctx, "merge", F);
  auto *A = F->getArg(0), *C = F->getArg(1);

  llvm::IRBuilder<> B(Entry);
  // 2^-5 scale keeps every lane below 2^31 so the vector fptosi->i32 never
  // overflows.
  auto *Scale = llvm::ConstantFP::get(Dbl, 0.03125);
  auto *Da = B.CreateFMul(B.CreateSIToFP(A, Dbl), Scale);
  auto *Db = B.CreateFMul(B.CreateSIToFP(C, Dbl), Scale);
  llvm::Value *V = llvm::UndefValue::get(V2d);
  V = B.CreateInsertElement(V, Da, uint64_t(0));
  V = B.CreateInsertElement(V, Db, uint64_t(1));
  // Two <2 x double> constants -> 16-byte pool (.rodata.cst16 / __literal16 /
  // COFF COMDAT .rdata) — the f64 dual of fvec's <4 x float> constant merging.
  double KElems[] = {1.5, 0.5};
  double OffElems[] = {0.1, 0.2};
  auto *K = llvm::ConstantDataVector::get(Ctx, KElems);
  auto *Off = llvm::ConstantDataVector::get(Ctx, OffElems);
  auto *Q = B.CreateFAdd(B.CreateFMul(V, K), Off);
  auto *Qi = B.CreateFPToSI(Q, V2i);
  auto *S = B.CreateAdd(B.CreateExtractElement(Qi, uint64_t(0)),
                        B.CreateExtractElement(Qi, uint64_t(1)));
  auto *T = B.CreateXor(B.CreateXor(B.CreateAdd(A, C), B.CreateSub(A, C)),
                        B.getInt32(0x33));
  auto *U = B.CreateOr(B.CreateAnd(A, C), B.CreateAdd(T, B.getInt32(777)));
  auto *Base = B.CreateAdd(S, U);
  auto *Sel = B.CreateAnd(B.CreateXor(A, C), B.getInt32(1));
  B.CreateCondBr(B.CreateICmpNE(Sel, B.getInt32(0)), Then, Else);

  B.SetInsertPoint(Then);
  auto *RT = B.CreateAdd(Base, A);
  B.CreateBr(Merge);
  B.SetInsertPoint(Else);
  auto *RE = B.CreateXor(Base, C);
  B.CreateBr(Merge);

  B.SetInsertPoint(Merge);
  auto *Res = B.CreatePHI(I32, 2, "res");
  Res->addIncoming(RT, Then);
  Res->addIncoming(RE, Else);
  B.CreateRet(Res);
  assert(!llvm::verifyModule(*M, &llvm::errs()));
  return M;
}

// Atomics — the one instruction class no standing sample exercises: atomicrmw
// (add/sub/and/or/xor/xchg) + cmpxchg on a .data global.  These lower to a
// completely distinct backend path per ISA — a `lock`-prefixed RMW / `lock
// cmpxchg` on x86, an `ldxr/stxr` (AArch64) or `ldrex/strex` (ARM32)
// exclusive-monitor retry loop — every one of which reads a *relocated* global
// address, so the rewrite backend must copy the lock prefix / exclusive pair
// AND fix up the global relocation correctly in one shot.  Single-threaded
// emulation always wins the monitor (status 0 — see
// AllPlatform_ExclusivePairRTTests), so the sequence is deterministic.  i32 is
// naturally 4-aligned, so every atomic lowers inline on all four ISAs — no
// __atomic_* libcall the harness could neither resolve nor execute.
//
// The atomic ops are NOT touched by any IR pass (--subst rewrites plain
// add/sub/and/or/xor, never the atomic instruction class), so the atomic
// sub-graph is byte-identical in both copies — any divergence is a genuine
// rewrite-backend bug.  Their operands and the surrounding integer arithmetic
// ARE substitutable, so --subst / --const-enc fire and visibly change .text; a
// data-dependent branch gives the control-flow passes
// (--flatten/--bogus/--indirect) real structure to transform.  The cmpxchg's
// expected value is the pre-`sub` snapshot, so it succeeds exactly when a==b
// (the input battery carries both a==b and a!=b pairs — both CAS outcomes are
// covered).  The final g_at lands in .data and is byte-compared by the harness,
// so a wrong exclusive-store address or a dropped status is caught there too.
//
//   int g_at = 0x1000;                          // .data
//   int atrmw(int a, int b) {
//     int o0 = __atomic_fetch_add(&g_at, a);
//     int o1 = __atomic_fetch_xor(&g_at, b ^ 0x33);
//     int o2 = __atomic_fetch_and(&g_at, a | 0xFF00);
//     int o3 = __atomic_fetch_or (&g_at, b & 0x0F0F);
//     int o4 = __atomic_fetch_sub(&g_at, a - b);          // exp = this
//     snapshot int o5 = __atomic_exchange (&g_at, (a + b) ^ 0x1234); int exp =
//     o4; bool ok = __atomic_compare_exchange(&g_at, &exp, o0 + o1);  //
//     {old,ok} int t = ((a + b) ^ (a - b)) ^ 0x5A5A; int u = (a & b) | (t +
//     12345); int base = ((o0 ^ o1) + (o2 & o3)) ^ (o4 - o5) ^ exp ^ (ok ? 7 :
//     0)
//                ^ __atomic_load(&g_at) ^ t ^ u;
//     return ((a ^ b) & 1) ? base + a : base ^ b;
//   }
std::unique_ptr<llvm::Module> buildAtomicIR(llvm::LLVMContext &Ctx,
                                            const char *Triple) {
  auto M = std::make_unique<llvm::Module>("substtest", Ctx);
  M->setTargetTriple(llvm::Triple(Triple));
  auto *I32 = llvm::Type::getInt32Ty(Ctx);
  auto *G = new llvm::GlobalVariable(
      *M, I32, false, llvm::GlobalValue::InternalLinkage,
      llvm::ConstantInt::get(I32, 0x1000), "g_at");
  G->setDSOLocal(true);
  G->setAlignment(llvm::Align(4));

  auto *FTy = llvm::FunctionType::get(I32, {I32, I32}, false);
  auto *F = llvm::Function::Create(FTy, llvm::Function::ExternalLinkage,
                                   "atrmw", M.get());
  auto *Entry = llvm::BasicBlock::Create(Ctx, "entry", F);
  auto *Then = llvm::BasicBlock::Create(Ctx, "then", F);
  auto *Else = llvm::BasicBlock::Create(Ctx, "else", F);
  auto *Merge = llvm::BasicBlock::Create(Ctx, "merge", F);
  auto *A = F->getArg(0), *C = F->getArg(1);

  llvm::IRBuilder<> B(Entry);
  const auto Mono = llvm::AtomicOrdering::Monotonic;
  const auto Al = llvm::MaybeAlign(4);
  auto *O0 = B.CreateAtomicRMW(llvm::AtomicRMWInst::Add, G, A, Al, Mono);
  auto *O1 = B.CreateAtomicRMW(llvm::AtomicRMWInst::Xor, G,
                               B.CreateXor(C, B.getInt32(0x33)), Al, Mono);
  auto *O2 = B.CreateAtomicRMW(llvm::AtomicRMWInst::And, G,
                               B.CreateOr(A, B.getInt32(0xFF00)), Al, Mono);
  auto *O3 = B.CreateAtomicRMW(llvm::AtomicRMWInst::Or, G,
                               B.CreateAnd(C, B.getInt32(0x0F0F)), Al, Mono);
  auto *O4 = B.CreateAtomicRMW(llvm::AtomicRMWInst::Sub, G, B.CreateSub(A, C),
                               Al, Mono);
  auto *O5 = B.CreateAtomicRMW(
      llvm::AtomicRMWInst::Xchg, G,
      B.CreateXor(B.CreateAdd(A, C), B.getInt32(0x1234)), Al, Mono);
  // cmpxchg returns { i32 loaded, i1 success }; expected = O4 (pre-sub
  // snapshot)
  // -> success iff the sub left g_at unchanged, i.e. a==b.
  auto *CX = B.CreateAtomicCmpXchg(G, O4, B.CreateAdd(O0, O1), Al, Mono, Mono);
  auto *Old = B.CreateExtractValue(CX, 0);
  auto *Ok = B.CreateExtractValue(CX, 1);
  auto *OkV = B.CreateSelect(Ok, B.getInt32(7), B.getInt32(0));
  auto *Cur = B.CreateLoad(I32, G);
  auto *T = B.CreateXor(B.CreateXor(B.CreateAdd(A, C), B.CreateSub(A, C)),
                        B.getInt32(0x5A5A));
  auto *U = B.CreateOr(B.CreateAnd(A, C), B.CreateAdd(T, B.getInt32(12345)));
  llvm::Value *Base = B.CreateAdd(B.CreateXor(O0, O1), B.CreateAnd(O2, O3));
  Base = B.CreateXor(Base, B.CreateSub(O4, O5));
  Base = B.CreateXor(Base, O4);
  Base = B.CreateXor(Base, OkV);
  Base = B.CreateXor(Base, Old);
  Base = B.CreateXor(Base, Cur);
  Base = B.CreateXor(B.CreateXor(Base, T), U);
  auto *Sel = B.CreateAnd(B.CreateXor(A, C), B.getInt32(1));
  B.CreateCondBr(B.CreateICmpNE(Sel, B.getInt32(0)), Then, Else);

  B.SetInsertPoint(Then);
  auto *RT = B.CreateAdd(Base, A);
  B.CreateBr(Merge);
  B.SetInsertPoint(Else);
  auto *RE = B.CreateXor(Base, C);
  B.CreateBr(Merge);

  B.SetInsertPoint(Merge);
  auto *Res = B.CreatePHI(I32, 2, "res");
  Res->addIncoming(RT, Then);
  Res->addIncoming(RE, Else);
  B.CreateRet(Res);
  assert(!llvm::verifyModule(*M, &llvm::errs()));
  return M;
}

// Atomic min/max RMW (atomicrmw max/min/umax/umin) — the atomic op class atrmw
// (add/sub/and/or/xor/xchg + cmpxchg) never covers.  No target has a plain
// straight-line instruction for atomic min/max on the baseline feature set: x86
// lowers each to a `lock cmpxchg` compare-and-retry loop, AArch64/ARM to an
// ldaxr/cmp/csel/stlxr (LL/SC) retry loop — and, with LSE (Apple silicon
// baseline), to the ldsmax/ldsmin/ldumax/ldumin atomic instructions.  That is a
// compare+select *inside* the atomic loop, a distinct lowering from atrmw's
// straight-line `lock xadd` / LL-SC add (and the LSE min/max ops exercise a
// fork-Unicorn path no other shape reaches).  Single-threaded so deterministic;
// the .data global is compared byte-for-byte.  Zero libcall.  Substitutable
// add/sub/and/or/xor + constants drive --subst / --const-enc; the
// data-dependent diamond + PHI give the control-flow passes real structure.
//
//   int atmnmx(int a, int b) {
//     _Atomic int g = 0x4000;
//     int o0 = atomic_fetch_max(&g, a);
//     int o1 = atomic_fetch_min(&g, a ^ b);
//     unsigned o2 = atomic_fetch_umax(&g, a + b);
//     unsigned o3 = atomic_fetch_umin(&g, a - b);
//     int cur = g;
//     int base = (o0 ^ o1) + (o2 ^ o3) ^ cur ^ ((a+b)^(a-b)^0x5A5A)
//                ^ ((a&b)|(t+12345));
//     return ((a ^ b) & 1) ? base + a : base ^ b;
//   }
std::unique_ptr<llvm::Module> buildAtomicMinMaxIR(llvm::LLVMContext &Ctx,
                                                  const char *Triple) {
  auto M = std::make_unique<llvm::Module>("substtest", Ctx);
  M->setTargetTriple(llvm::Triple(Triple));
  auto *I32 = llvm::Type::getInt32Ty(Ctx);
  auto *G = new llvm::GlobalVariable(
      *M, I32, false, llvm::GlobalValue::InternalLinkage,
      llvm::ConstantInt::get(I32, 0x4000), "g_atmnmx");
  G->setDSOLocal(true);
  G->setAlignment(llvm::Align(4));

  auto *FTy = llvm::FunctionType::get(I32, {I32, I32}, false);
  auto *F = llvm::Function::Create(FTy, llvm::Function::ExternalLinkage,
                                   "atmnmx", M.get());
  auto *Entry = llvm::BasicBlock::Create(Ctx, "entry", F);
  auto *Then = llvm::BasicBlock::Create(Ctx, "then", F);
  auto *Else = llvm::BasicBlock::Create(Ctx, "else", F);
  auto *Merge = llvm::BasicBlock::Create(Ctx, "merge", F);
  auto *A = F->getArg(0), *C = F->getArg(1);

  llvm::IRBuilder<> B(Entry);
  const auto Mono = llvm::AtomicOrdering::Monotonic;
  const auto Al = llvm::MaybeAlign(4);
  auto *O0 = B.CreateAtomicRMW(llvm::AtomicRMWInst::Max, G, A, Al, Mono);
  auto *O1 = B.CreateAtomicRMW(llvm::AtomicRMWInst::Min, G, B.CreateXor(A, C),
                               Al, Mono);
  auto *O2 = B.CreateAtomicRMW(llvm::AtomicRMWInst::UMax, G, B.CreateAdd(A, C),
                               Al, Mono);
  auto *O3 = B.CreateAtomicRMW(llvm::AtomicRMWInst::UMin, G, B.CreateSub(A, C),
                               Al, Mono);
  auto *Cur = B.CreateLoad(I32, G);
  auto *T = B.CreateXor(B.CreateXor(B.CreateAdd(A, C), B.CreateSub(A, C)),
                        B.getInt32(0x5A5A));
  auto *U = B.CreateOr(B.CreateAnd(A, C), B.CreateAdd(T, B.getInt32(12345)));
  llvm::Value *Base = B.CreateAdd(B.CreateXor(O0, O1), B.CreateXor(O2, O3));
  Base = B.CreateXor(Base, Cur);
  Base = B.CreateXor(B.CreateXor(Base, T), U);
  auto *Sel = B.CreateAnd(B.CreateXor(A, C), B.getInt32(1));
  B.CreateCondBr(B.CreateICmpNE(Sel, B.getInt32(0)), Then, Else);

  B.SetInsertPoint(Then);
  auto *RT = B.CreateAdd(Base, A);
  B.CreateBr(Merge);
  B.SetInsertPoint(Else);
  auto *RE = B.CreateXor(Base, C);
  B.CreateBr(Merge);

  B.SetInsertPoint(Merge);
  auto *Res = B.CreatePHI(I32, 2, "res");
  Res->addIncoming(RT, Then);
  Res->addIncoming(RE, Else);
  B.CreateRet(Res);
  assert(!llvm::verifyModule(*M, &llvm::errs()));
  return M;
}

// Atomic NAND — the one atomicrmw op no shape exercised: `atrmw` covers
// add/sub/and/or/xor/xchg + cmpxchg, `atmnmx` covers max/min/umax/umin, but
// `atomicrmw nand` (*p = ~(*p & val)) was never tested.  nand has *no single
// instruction* on any ISA, so it always lowers to a compare-and-swap / LL-SC
// *retry loop* — x86 `lock cmpxchg` loop, AArch64 `ldaxr/and/mvn/stlxr` loop,
// ARM32 `ldrex/and/mvn/strex` loop — distinct from the straight-line
// `lock xadd` / LSE / single-op lowering of every other atomic, with zero
// libcall for aligned i32.  Single-threaded emulation always wins the monitor
// so the sequence is deterministic; the .data global and the return value are
// both compared.  No obfuscation pass touches the atomic op, so orig/obfuscated
// lower byte-identically and any Unicorn mismatch is a real backend / fork-
// Unicorn bug.  add/sub/and/or/xor + 0x5A5A/12345 drive --subst/--const-enc;
// the data-dependent diamond + PHI give the control-flow passes real structure.
//
//   static int g = 0x4000;
//   int atnand(int a, int c) {
//     int o0 = atomic_fetch_nand(&g, a);          // g = ~(g & a)
//     int o1 = atomic_fetch_nand(&g, a ^ c);
//     int o2 = atomic_fetch_nand(&g, a + c);
//     int cur = g, base = ((o0 ^ o1) ^ o2) ^ cur ^ ... ;
//     return ((a ^ c) & 1) ? base + a : base ^ c;
//   }
std::unique_ptr<llvm::Module> buildAtomicNandIR(llvm::LLVMContext &Ctx,
                                                const char *Triple) {
  auto M = std::make_unique<llvm::Module>("substtest", Ctx);
  M->setTargetTriple(llvm::Triple(Triple));
  auto *I32 = llvm::Type::getInt32Ty(Ctx);
  auto *G = new llvm::GlobalVariable(
      *M, I32, false, llvm::GlobalValue::InternalLinkage,
      llvm::ConstantInt::get(I32, 0x4000), "g_atnand");
  G->setDSOLocal(true);
  G->setAlignment(llvm::Align(4));

  auto *FTy = llvm::FunctionType::get(I32, {I32, I32}, false);
  auto *F = llvm::Function::Create(FTy, llvm::Function::ExternalLinkage,
                                   "atnand", M.get());
  auto *Entry = llvm::BasicBlock::Create(Ctx, "entry", F);
  auto *Then = llvm::BasicBlock::Create(Ctx, "then", F);
  auto *Else = llvm::BasicBlock::Create(Ctx, "else", F);
  auto *Merge = llvm::BasicBlock::Create(Ctx, "merge", F);
  auto *A = F->getArg(0), *C = F->getArg(1);

  llvm::IRBuilder<> B(Entry);
  const auto Mono = llvm::AtomicOrdering::Monotonic;
  const auto Al = llvm::MaybeAlign(4);
  auto *O0 = B.CreateAtomicRMW(llvm::AtomicRMWInst::Nand, G, A, Al, Mono);
  auto *O1 = B.CreateAtomicRMW(llvm::AtomicRMWInst::Nand, G, B.CreateXor(A, C),
                               Al, Mono);
  auto *O2 = B.CreateAtomicRMW(llvm::AtomicRMWInst::Nand, G, B.CreateAdd(A, C),
                               Al, Mono);
  auto *Cur = B.CreateLoad(I32, G);
  auto *T = B.CreateXor(B.CreateXor(B.CreateAdd(A, C), B.CreateSub(A, C)),
                        B.getInt32(0x5A5A));
  auto *U = B.CreateOr(B.CreateAnd(A, C), B.CreateAdd(T, B.getInt32(12345)));
  llvm::Value *Base = B.CreateXor(B.CreateXor(O0, O1), O2);
  Base = B.CreateXor(Base, Cur);
  Base = B.CreateXor(B.CreateXor(Base, T), U);
  auto *Sel = B.CreateAnd(B.CreateXor(A, C), B.getInt32(1));
  B.CreateCondBr(B.CreateICmpNE(Sel, B.getInt32(0)), Then, Else);

  B.SetInsertPoint(Then);
  auto *RT = B.CreateAdd(Base, A);
  B.CreateBr(Merge);
  B.SetInsertPoint(Else);
  auto *RE = B.CreateXor(Base, C);
  B.CreateBr(Merge);

  B.SetInsertPoint(Merge);
  auto *Res = B.CreatePHI(I32, 2, "res");
  Res->addIncoming(RT, Then);
  Res->addIncoming(RE, Else);
  B.CreateRet(Res);
  assert(!llvm::verifyModule(*M, &llvm::errs()));
  return M;
}

// Sub-word atomics (i8 / i16 atomicrmw) — every prior atomic shape (atrmw,
// atmnmx, atnand) operates on i32; sub-word atomics lower to a *distinct*
// per-ISA path: x86 `lock` byte/word ops (`lock add byte/word ptr`), AArch64
// byte/halfword exclusives `ldaxrb`/`stlxrb` & `ldaxrh`/`stlxrh` (or LSE
// `ldaddb`/`ldaddh`), ARM32 `ldrexb`/`strexb` & `ldrexh`/`strexh` — all
// lock-free and zero-libcall for naturally-aligned i8/i16.  Two writable
// globals (i8 g_atb @ align 1, i16 g_ath @ align 2) are RMW-ed and both the
// .data section bytes and the return value are compared.  Single-threaded
// emulation is deterministic; no obfuscation pass touches the atomic ops, so
// orig/obfuscated lower byte-identically and any Unicorn mismatch is a real
// backend / fork-Unicorn bug.
//
//   static unsigned char  g8  = 0x5A;
//   static unsigned short g16 = 0x1234;
//   int atbw(int a, int c) {
//     unsigned char  o0 = atomic_fetch_add(&g8,  (char)a);
//     unsigned char  o1 = atomic_fetch_xor(&g8,  (char)c);
//     unsigned short o2 = atomic_fetch_add(&g16, (short)a);
//     unsigned short o3 = atomic_fetch_and(&g16, (short)c);
//     unsigned short o4 = atomic_fetch_or (&g16, (short)(a + c));
//     ... combine zext(o*) + zext(g8) + zext(g16) + mix + diamond ...
//   }
std::unique_ptr<llvm::Module> buildAtomicSubWordIR(llvm::LLVMContext &Ctx,
                                                   const char *Triple) {
  auto M = std::make_unique<llvm::Module>("substtest", Ctx);
  M->setTargetTriple(llvm::Triple(Triple));
  auto *I8 = llvm::Type::getInt8Ty(Ctx);
  auto *I16 = llvm::Type::getInt16Ty(Ctx);
  auto *I32 = llvm::Type::getInt32Ty(Ctx);
  auto *G8 = new llvm::GlobalVariable(
      *M, I8, false, llvm::GlobalValue::InternalLinkage,
      llvm::ConstantInt::get(I8, 0x5A), "g_atb");
  G8->setDSOLocal(true);
  G8->setAlignment(llvm::Align(1));
  auto *G16 = new llvm::GlobalVariable(
      *M, I16, false, llvm::GlobalValue::InternalLinkage,
      llvm::ConstantInt::get(I16, 0x1234), "g_ath");
  G16->setDSOLocal(true);
  G16->setAlignment(llvm::Align(2));

  auto *FTy = llvm::FunctionType::get(I32, {I32, I32}, false);
  auto *F = llvm::Function::Create(FTy, llvm::Function::ExternalLinkage, "atbw",
                                   M.get());
  auto *Entry = llvm::BasicBlock::Create(Ctx, "entry", F);
  auto *Then = llvm::BasicBlock::Create(Ctx, "then", F);
  auto *Else = llvm::BasicBlock::Create(Ctx, "else", F);
  auto *Merge = llvm::BasicBlock::Create(Ctx, "merge", F);
  auto *A = F->getArg(0), *C = F->getArg(1);

  llvm::IRBuilder<> B(Entry);
  const auto Mono = llvm::AtomicOrdering::Monotonic;
  auto *A8 = B.CreateTrunc(A, I8);
  auto *C8 = B.CreateTrunc(C, I8);
  auto *A16 = B.CreateTrunc(A, I16);
  auto *C16 = B.CreateTrunc(C, I16);
  auto *O0 = B.CreateAtomicRMW(llvm::AtomicRMWInst::Add, G8, A8,
                               llvm::MaybeAlign(1), Mono);
  auto *O1 = B.CreateAtomicRMW(llvm::AtomicRMWInst::Xor, G8, C8,
                               llvm::MaybeAlign(1), Mono);
  auto *O2 = B.CreateAtomicRMW(llvm::AtomicRMWInst::Add, G16, A16,
                               llvm::MaybeAlign(2), Mono);
  auto *O3 = B.CreateAtomicRMW(llvm::AtomicRMWInst::And, G16, C16,
                               llvm::MaybeAlign(2), Mono);
  auto *O4 = B.CreateAtomicRMW(llvm::AtomicRMWInst::Or, G16,
                               B.CreateTrunc(B.CreateAdd(A, C), I16),
                               llvm::MaybeAlign(2), Mono);
  auto *Cur8 = B.CreateLoad(I8, G8);
  auto *Cur16 = B.CreateLoad(I16, G16);
  auto *T = B.CreateXor(B.CreateXor(B.CreateAdd(A, C), B.CreateSub(A, C)),
                        B.getInt32(0x5A5A));
  auto *U = B.CreateOr(B.CreateAnd(A, C), B.CreateAdd(T, B.getInt32(12345)));
  llvm::Value *Base = B.CreateXor(B.CreateZExt(O0, I32), B.CreateZExt(O1, I32));
  Base = B.CreateXor(Base, B.CreateZExt(O2, I32));
  Base = B.CreateXor(Base, B.CreateZExt(O3, I32));
  Base = B.CreateXor(Base, B.CreateZExt(O4, I32));
  Base = B.CreateXor(Base, B.CreateZExt(Cur8, I32));
  Base = B.CreateXor(Base, B.CreateZExt(Cur16, I32));
  Base = B.CreateXor(B.CreateXor(Base, T), U);
  auto *Sel = B.CreateAnd(B.CreateXor(A, C), B.getInt32(1));
  B.CreateCondBr(B.CreateICmpNE(Sel, B.getInt32(0)), Then, Else);

  B.SetInsertPoint(Then);
  auto *RT = B.CreateAdd(Base, A);
  B.CreateBr(Merge);
  B.SetInsertPoint(Else);
  auto *RE = B.CreateXor(Base, C);
  B.CreateBr(Merge);

  B.SetInsertPoint(Merge);
  auto *Res = B.CreatePHI(I32, 2, "res");
  Res->addIncoming(RT, Then);
  Res->addIncoming(RE, Else);
  B.CreateRet(Res);
  assert(!llvm::verifyModule(*M, &llvm::errs()));
  return M;
}

// Atomic load / store with explicit memory ordering — every prior atomic shape
// (atrmw/atmnmx/atnand/atbw) is a read-modify-write; atomic *load* and *store*
// with seq_cst / acquire / release ordering lower to a *different* family: the
// ordering inserts fences / acquire-release variants — AArch64 `ldar`/`stlr`,
// x86 plain `mov` load + `xchg` (or `mov`+`mfence`) for the seq_cst store,
// ARM32 `lda`/`stl` or `ldr`/`str` + `dmb` — none of which the RMW loops
// exercise, all lock-free and zero-libcall for aligned i32.  A seq_cst/acquire
// load + a seq_cst/release store sequence on one global; both the .data byte
// and the return value are compared.  No obfuscation pass touches the atomic
// accesses, so orig/obfuscated lower byte-identically and any Unicorn mismatch
// is a real backend / fork-Unicorn bug.
//
//   static int g = 0x7000;
//   int atld(int a, int c) {
//     int v0 = atomic_load(&g, seq_cst);
//     atomic_store(&g, a ^ v0, seq_cst);
//     int v1 = atomic_load(&g, acquire);
//     atomic_store(&g, v1 + c, release);
//     int v2 = atomic_load(&g, seq_cst);
//     ... combine v0^v1^v2 + mix + diamond ...
//   }
std::unique_ptr<llvm::Module> buildAtomicLoadStoreIR(llvm::LLVMContext &Ctx,
                                                     const char *Triple) {
  auto M = std::make_unique<llvm::Module>("substtest", Ctx);
  M->setTargetTriple(llvm::Triple(Triple));
  auto *I32 = llvm::Type::getInt32Ty(Ctx);
  auto *G = new llvm::GlobalVariable(
      *M, I32, false, llvm::GlobalValue::InternalLinkage,
      llvm::ConstantInt::get(I32, 0x7000), "g_atld");
  G->setDSOLocal(true);
  G->setAlignment(llvm::Align(4));

  auto *FTy = llvm::FunctionType::get(I32, {I32, I32}, false);
  auto *F = llvm::Function::Create(FTy, llvm::Function::ExternalLinkage, "atld",
                                   M.get());
  auto *Entry = llvm::BasicBlock::Create(Ctx, "entry", F);
  auto *Then = llvm::BasicBlock::Create(Ctx, "then", F);
  auto *Else = llvm::BasicBlock::Create(Ctx, "else", F);
  auto *Merge = llvm::BasicBlock::Create(Ctx, "merge", F);
  auto *A = F->getArg(0), *C = F->getArg(1);

  llvm::IRBuilder<> B(Entry);
  const auto SC = llvm::AtomicOrdering::SequentiallyConsistent;
  const auto Acq = llvm::AtomicOrdering::Acquire;
  const auto Rel = llvm::AtomicOrdering::Release;
  const llvm::Align Al(4);
  auto atomicLoad = [&](llvm::AtomicOrdering O) -> llvm::Value * {
    auto *L = B.CreateLoad(I32, G);
    L->setAtomic(O);
    L->setAlignment(Al);
    return L;
  };
  auto atomicStore = [&](llvm::Value *V, llvm::AtomicOrdering O) {
    auto *S = B.CreateStore(V, G);
    S->setAtomic(O);
    S->setAlignment(Al);
  };
  auto *V0 = atomicLoad(SC);
  atomicStore(B.CreateXor(A, V0), SC);
  auto *V1 = atomicLoad(Acq);
  atomicStore(B.CreateAdd(V1, C), Rel);
  auto *V2 = atomicLoad(SC);
  auto *T = B.CreateXor(B.CreateXor(B.CreateAdd(A, C), B.CreateSub(A, C)),
                        B.getInt32(0x5A5A));
  auto *U = B.CreateOr(B.CreateAnd(A, C), B.CreateAdd(T, B.getInt32(12345)));
  llvm::Value *Base = B.CreateXor(B.CreateXor(V0, V1), V2);
  Base = B.CreateXor(B.CreateXor(Base, T), U);
  auto *Sel = B.CreateAnd(B.CreateXor(A, C), B.getInt32(1));
  B.CreateCondBr(B.CreateICmpNE(Sel, B.getInt32(0)), Then, Else);

  B.SetInsertPoint(Then);
  auto *RT = B.CreateAdd(Base, A);
  B.CreateBr(Merge);
  B.SetInsertPoint(Else);
  auto *RE = B.CreateXor(Base, C);
  B.CreateBr(Merge);

  B.SetInsertPoint(Merge);
  auto *Res = B.CreatePHI(I32, 2, "res");
  Res->addIncoming(RT, Then);
  Res->addIncoming(RE, Else);
  B.CreateRet(Res);
  assert(!llvm::verifyModule(*M, &llvm::errs()));
  return M;
}

// Floating-point atomic RMW (atomicrmw fadd / fsub on f32) — the most novel
// atomic path: there is no native FP atomic on the baseline ISAs, so LLVM's
// AtomicExpandPass lowers it to an *integer cmpxchg retry loop with an inline
// FP add/sub* — x86 `lock cmpxchg` loop + `addss`/`subss`, AArch64
// `ldaxr`/`fadd`/`stlxr` loop, ARM32 `ldrex`/`vadd.f32`/`strex` loop —
// combining the CAS-loop control flow of atnand with a floating-point op, a
// path no prior atomic (all integer) or FP shape (all non-atomic) reached.  f32
// keeps the cmpxchg at 32 bits (lock-free on every ISA, zero libcall). Operands
// are small exact integers (<256) so every fadd/fsub and the final fptosi are
// exact/deterministic; the .data float global and the return value are both
// compared.  The atomicrmw is a single IR instruction when the obfuscation
// passes run (AtomicExpandPass expands it later during codegen), so no pass
// touches it and orig/obfuscated lower byte-identically — any Unicorn mismatch
// is a real backend / fork-Unicorn bug.
//
//   static float g = 1.0f;
//   int atfp(int a, int c) {
//     float fa = (float)(a & 0xFF), fc = (float)(c & 0xFF);
//     float o0 = atomic_fetch_fadd(&g, fa);   // CAS loop + addss
//     float o1 = atomic_fetch_fsub(&g, fc);   // CAS loop + subss
//     float o2 = atomic_fetch_fadd(&g, fa);
//     int s = (int)(o0 + o1 + o2 + g);
//     ... mix + diamond ...
//   }
std::unique_ptr<llvm::Module> buildAtomicFPIR(llvm::LLVMContext &Ctx,
                                              const char *Triple) {
  auto M = std::make_unique<llvm::Module>("substtest", Ctx);
  M->setTargetTriple(llvm::Triple(Triple));
  auto *I32 = llvm::Type::getInt32Ty(Ctx);
  auto *F32 = llvm::Type::getFloatTy(Ctx);
  auto *G = new llvm::GlobalVariable(*M, F32, false,
                                     llvm::GlobalValue::InternalLinkage,
                                     llvm::ConstantFP::get(F32, 1.0), "g_atfp");
  G->setDSOLocal(true);
  G->setAlignment(llvm::Align(4));

  auto *FTy = llvm::FunctionType::get(I32, {I32, I32}, false);
  auto *F = llvm::Function::Create(FTy, llvm::Function::ExternalLinkage, "atfp",
                                   M.get());
  auto *Entry = llvm::BasicBlock::Create(Ctx, "entry", F);
  auto *Then = llvm::BasicBlock::Create(Ctx, "then", F);
  auto *Else = llvm::BasicBlock::Create(Ctx, "else", F);
  auto *Merge = llvm::BasicBlock::Create(Ctx, "merge", F);
  auto *A = F->getArg(0), *C = F->getArg(1);

  llvm::IRBuilder<> B(Entry);
  const auto Mono = llvm::AtomicOrdering::Monotonic;
  const auto Al = llvm::MaybeAlign(4);
  auto *Fa = B.CreateSIToFP(B.CreateAnd(A, B.getInt32(0xFF)), F32); // [0,255]
  auto *Fc = B.CreateSIToFP(B.CreateAnd(C, B.getInt32(0xFF)), F32); // [0,255]
  auto *O0 = B.CreateAtomicRMW(llvm::AtomicRMWInst::FAdd, G, Fa, Al, Mono);
  auto *O1 = B.CreateAtomicRMW(llvm::AtomicRMWInst::FSub, G, Fc, Al, Mono);
  auto *O2 = B.CreateAtomicRMW(llvm::AtomicRMWInst::FAdd, G, Fa, Al, Mono);
  auto *Cur = B.CreateLoad(F32, G);
  auto *Sum = B.CreateFAdd(B.CreateFAdd(O0, O1), B.CreateFAdd(O2, Cur));
  auto *S = B.CreateFPToSI(Sum, I32); // exact small integer
  auto *T = B.CreateXor(B.CreateXor(B.CreateAdd(A, C), B.CreateSub(A, C)),
                        B.getInt32(0x5A5A));
  auto *U = B.CreateOr(B.CreateAnd(A, C), B.CreateAdd(T, B.getInt32(12345)));
  llvm::Value *Base = B.CreateXor(B.CreateXor(S, T), U);
  auto *Sel = B.CreateAnd(B.CreateXor(A, C), B.getInt32(1));
  B.CreateCondBr(B.CreateICmpNE(Sel, B.getInt32(0)), Then, Else);

  B.SetInsertPoint(Then);
  auto *RT = B.CreateAdd(Base, A);
  B.CreateBr(Merge);
  B.SetInsertPoint(Else);
  auto *RE = B.CreateXor(Base, C);
  B.CreateBr(Merge);

  B.SetInsertPoint(Merge);
  auto *Res = B.CreatePHI(I32, 2, "res");
  Res->addIncoming(RT, Then);
  Res->addIncoming(RE, Else);
  B.CreateRet(Res);
  assert(!llvm::verifyModule(*M, &llvm::errs()));
  return M;
}

// Vector floating-point sign-bit ops (fabs / fneg / copysign on <4 x float>) —
// FloatSign covers only the *scalar* sign ops; the vector forms lower to a
// *different* family of whole-register mask ops: x86 `andps`/`xorps`/`andnps`
// with a 16-byte sign-mask constant pool entry, AArch64 NEON
// `fneg`/`fabs`/`bit` (or `bsl`) over <4 x float>, ARM32 NEON
// `vneg`/`vabs`/`vbsl` — none reached by the scalar FloatSign.  Lanes are exact
// small *signed* integers (incl. negatives, so the sign ops genuinely differ),
// so fneg/fabs/copysign and the final fptosi are all exact/deterministic.  No
// obfuscation pass touches the FP vector sub-graph, so orig/obfuscated lower
// byte-identically and any Unicorn mismatch is a real backend / fork-Unicorn
// bug.  The mask constants also stress the COFF-COMDAT / mergeable-pool
// placement the integer-vector shapes exercise, now for FP sign masks.
//
//   int vfsign(int a, int c) {
//     float fa = (float)(a & 0x3FF) - 512.0f;   // [-512, 511]
//     float fc = (float)(c & 0x3FF) - 512.0f;
//     float4 va = { fa, fa+1, fa+2, fa+3 }, vb = { fc, fc+2, fc+4, fc+6 };
//     float4 r = (-va) + fabs(vb) + copysign(va, vb);   // integer-valued
//     int s = (int)r[0] + r[1] + r[2] + r[3];
//     ... mix + diamond ...
//   }
std::unique_ptr<llvm::Module> buildVecFloatSignIR(llvm::LLVMContext &Ctx,
                                                  const char *Triple) {
  auto M = std::make_unique<llvm::Module>("substtest", Ctx);
  M->setTargetTriple(llvm::Triple(Triple));
  auto *I32 = llvm::Type::getInt32Ty(Ctx);
  auto *Flt = llvm::Type::getFloatTy(Ctx);
  auto *V4f = llvm::FixedVectorType::get(Flt, 4);
  auto *V4i = llvm::FixedVectorType::get(I32, 4);
  auto *FTy = llvm::FunctionType::get(I32, {I32, I32}, false);
  auto *F = llvm::Function::Create(FTy, llvm::Function::ExternalLinkage,
                                   "vfsign", M.get());
  auto *Entry = llvm::BasicBlock::Create(Ctx, "entry", F);
  auto *Then = llvm::BasicBlock::Create(Ctx, "then", F);
  auto *Else = llvm::BasicBlock::Create(Ctx, "else", F);
  auto *Merge = llvm::BasicBlock::Create(Ctx, "merge", F);
  auto *A = F->getArg(0), *C = F->getArg(1);

  llvm::IRBuilder<> B(Entry);
  auto fb = [&](double D) { return llvm::ConstantFP::get(Flt, D); };
  // Signed integer-valued lanes (include negatives so sign ops differ).
  auto *Fa = B.CreateFSub(
      B.CreateSIToFP(B.CreateAnd(A, B.getInt32(0x3FF)), Flt), fb(512.0));
  auto *Fc = B.CreateFSub(
      B.CreateSIToFP(B.CreateAnd(C, B.getInt32(0x3FF)), Flt), fb(512.0));
  llvm::Value *Va = llvm::UndefValue::get(V4f);
  Va = B.CreateInsertElement(Va, Fa, uint64_t(0));
  Va = B.CreateInsertElement(Va, B.CreateFAdd(Fa, fb(1.0)), uint64_t(1));
  Va = B.CreateInsertElement(Va, B.CreateFAdd(Fa, fb(2.0)), uint64_t(2));
  Va = B.CreateInsertElement(Va, B.CreateFAdd(Fa, fb(3.0)), uint64_t(3));
  llvm::Value *Vb = llvm::UndefValue::get(V4f);
  Vb = B.CreateInsertElement(Vb, Fc, uint64_t(0));
  Vb = B.CreateInsertElement(Vb, B.CreateFAdd(Fc, fb(2.0)), uint64_t(1));
  Vb = B.CreateInsertElement(Vb, B.CreateFAdd(Fc, fb(4.0)), uint64_t(2));
  Vb = B.CreateInsertElement(Vb, B.CreateFAdd(Fc, fb(6.0)), uint64_t(3));
  auto *Na = B.CreateFNeg(Va);
  auto *Aa = B.CreateUnaryIntrinsic(llvm::Intrinsic::fabs, Vb);
  auto *Cs = B.CreateBinaryIntrinsic(llvm::Intrinsic::copysign, Va, Vb);
  auto *R = B.CreateFAdd(B.CreateFAdd(Na, Aa), Cs); // integer-valued
  auto *Ri = B.CreateFPToSI(R, V4i);
  auto *S = B.CreateAdd(B.CreateAdd(B.CreateExtractElement(Ri, uint64_t(0)),
                                    B.CreateExtractElement(Ri, uint64_t(1))),
                        B.CreateAdd(B.CreateExtractElement(Ri, uint64_t(2)),
                                    B.CreateExtractElement(Ri, uint64_t(3))));
  auto *T = B.CreateXor(B.CreateXor(B.CreateAdd(A, C), B.CreateSub(A, C)),
                        B.getInt32(0x5A5A));
  auto *U = B.CreateOr(B.CreateAnd(A, C), B.CreateAdd(T, B.getInt32(12345)));
  auto *Base = B.CreateXor(B.CreateXor(S, T), U);
  auto *Sel = B.CreateAnd(B.CreateXor(A, C), B.getInt32(1));
  B.CreateCondBr(B.CreateICmpNE(Sel, B.getInt32(0)), Then, Else);

  B.SetInsertPoint(Then);
  auto *RT = B.CreateAdd(Base, A);
  B.CreateBr(Merge);
  B.SetInsertPoint(Else);
  auto *RE = B.CreateXor(Base, C);
  B.CreateBr(Merge);

  B.SetInsertPoint(Merge);
  auto *Res = B.CreatePHI(I32, 2, "res");
  Res->addIncoming(RT, Then);
  Res->addIncoming(RE, Else);
  B.CreateRet(Res);
  assert(!llvm::verifyModule(*M, &llvm::errs()));
  return M;
}

// Vector i32 saturating arithmetic (sadd/ssub/uadd/usub.sat on <4 x i32>) — the
// existing vsat shape is <8 x i16>, which x86 SSE2 saturates *natively*
// (paddsw/psubsw/paddusw/psubusw); there is NO native i32 vector-saturate on
// x86 (or pre-SVE AArch64 NEON has it via sqadd/uqadd, but x86 does not), so
// the i32 form forces a *completely different* lowering: x86 expands to add/sub
// + overflow-compare + select (blend), while AArch64/ARM NEON use the native
// `sqadd.4s`/`uqadd.4s`/`sqsub.4s`/`uqsub.4s` — a per-ISA divergence vsat's i16
// never reaches.  Lanes include INT_MAX/INT_MIN/UINT_MAX extremes so the clamp
// edges are exercised; all integer, zero libcall.  No obfuscation pass touches
// the saturating intrinsics, so orig/obfuscated lower byte-identically and any
// Unicorn mismatch is a real backend / fork-Unicorn bug.
//
//   int vsat32(int a, int c) {
//     int4 va = { a, a^0x55555555, a+0x40000000, 0x7FFFFFFF };
//     int4 vb = { c, c+0x40000000, 0x10,         c          };
//     int4 sa = sadd_sat(va,vb), ss = ssub_sat(va,vb);
//     int4 ua = uadd_sat(va,vb), us = usub_sat(va,vb);
//     int base = reduce_xor(sa^ss^ua^us) ^ mix; ... diamond ...
//   }
std::unique_ptr<llvm::Module> buildVecSat32IR(llvm::LLVMContext &Ctx,
                                              const char *Triple) {
  auto M = std::make_unique<llvm::Module>("substtest", Ctx);
  M->setTargetTriple(llvm::Triple(Triple));
  auto *I32 = llvm::Type::getInt32Ty(Ctx);
  auto *V4i = llvm::FixedVectorType::get(I32, 4);
  auto *FTy = llvm::FunctionType::get(I32, {I32, I32}, false);
  auto *F = llvm::Function::Create(FTy, llvm::Function::ExternalLinkage,
                                   "vsat32", M.get());
  auto *Entry = llvm::BasicBlock::Create(Ctx, "entry", F);
  auto *Then = llvm::BasicBlock::Create(Ctx, "then", F);
  auto *Else = llvm::BasicBlock::Create(Ctx, "else", F);
  auto *Merge = llvm::BasicBlock::Create(Ctx, "merge", F);
  auto *A = F->getArg(0), *C = F->getArg(1);

  llvm::IRBuilder<> B(Entry);
  auto mkVec = [&](llvm::Value *L0, llvm::Value *L1, llvm::Value *L2,
                   llvm::Value *L3) {
    llvm::Value *V = llvm::UndefValue::get(V4i);
    V = B.CreateInsertElement(V, L0, uint64_t(0));
    V = B.CreateInsertElement(V, L1, uint64_t(1));
    V = B.CreateInsertElement(V, L2, uint64_t(2));
    V = B.CreateInsertElement(V, L3, uint64_t(3));
    return V;
  };
  // Lanes include INT_MAX/large-magnitude values so the saturation edges fire.
  auto *Va =
      mkVec(A, B.CreateXor(A, B.getInt32(0x55555555)),
            B.CreateAdd(A, B.getInt32(0x40000000)), B.getInt32(0x7FFFFFFF));
  auto *Vb =
      mkVec(C, B.CreateAdd(C, B.getInt32(0x40000000)), B.getInt32(0x10), C);
  auto *Sa = B.CreateBinaryIntrinsic(llvm::Intrinsic::sadd_sat, Va, Vb);
  auto *Ss = B.CreateBinaryIntrinsic(llvm::Intrinsic::ssub_sat, Va, Vb);
  auto *Ua = B.CreateBinaryIntrinsic(llvm::Intrinsic::uadd_sat, Va, Vb);
  auto *Us = B.CreateBinaryIntrinsic(llvm::Intrinsic::usub_sat, Va, Vb);
  auto *Vx = B.CreateXor(B.CreateXor(Sa, Ss), B.CreateXor(Ua, Us));
  auto *S = B.CreateXor(B.CreateXor(B.CreateExtractElement(Vx, uint64_t(0)),
                                    B.CreateExtractElement(Vx, uint64_t(1))),
                        B.CreateXor(B.CreateExtractElement(Vx, uint64_t(2)),
                                    B.CreateExtractElement(Vx, uint64_t(3))));
  auto *T = B.CreateXor(B.CreateXor(B.CreateAdd(A, C), B.CreateSub(A, C)),
                        B.getInt32(0x5A5A));
  auto *U = B.CreateOr(B.CreateAnd(A, C), B.CreateAdd(T, B.getInt32(12345)));
  auto *Base = B.CreateXor(B.CreateXor(S, T), U);
  auto *Sel = B.CreateAnd(B.CreateXor(A, C), B.getInt32(1));
  B.CreateCondBr(B.CreateICmpNE(Sel, B.getInt32(0)), Then, Else);

  B.SetInsertPoint(Then);
  auto *RT = B.CreateAdd(Base, A);
  B.CreateBr(Merge);
  B.SetInsertPoint(Else);
  auto *RE = B.CreateXor(Base, C);
  B.CreateBr(Merge);

  B.SetInsertPoint(Merge);
  auto *Res = B.CreatePHI(I32, 2, "res");
  Res->addIncoming(RT, Then);
  Res->addIncoming(RE, Else);
  B.CreateRet(Res);
  assert(!llvm::verifyModule(*M, &llvm::errs()));
  return M;
}

// Vector i64 saturating arithmetic (sadd/ssub/uadd/usub.sat on <2 x i64>) — the
// i64-lane dual of the vsat (<8 x i16>) / vsat8 (<16 x i8>) / vsat32 (<4 x
// i32>) family; the 64-bit vector lane was never covered.  The i64 lane
// diverges the most across ISAs: x86/x86-64 SSE2 has NO native i64 vector
// saturation, so <2 x i64> sadd/ssub/uadd/usub.sat *expand* to add/sub + 64-bit
// overflow- compare + blend (and on 32-bit i386 the illegal <2 x i64> is split
// to scalar i64 register-pair compare/select chains); AArch64 NEON has native
// sqadd.2d / uqadd.2d / sqsub.2d / uqsub.2d and ARM32 NEON vqadd.s64 /
// vqsub.s64 — a per-ISA divergence no narrower vsat lane reaches.  Lanes carry
// near-extreme i64 magnitudes (a large arg-derived value and 0xFFFF...F0 /
// INT64-edge constants) so the signed and unsigned clamp edges actually fire;
// all integer, zero libcall.  No obfuscation pass touches the saturating
// intrinsics, so orig/obfuscated lower byte-identically and any Unicorn
// mismatch is a real rewrite-backend / fork-Unicorn bug.  The two i64 lanes are
// xor-folded then hi^lo-folded to i32; the surrounding add/sub/and/or/xor mix +
// 0x5A5A / 12345 drive --subst / --const-enc and the data-dependent diamond +
// PHI give the control-flow passes structure.
//
//   int vsat64(int a, int c) {
//     i64 a64 = (i64)a, c64 = (i64)c;
//     i64x2 va = { (a64<<31) ^ 0x4000000000000000, 0xFFFFFFFFFFFFFFF0 };
//     i64x2 vb = { (c64<<31) + 0x4000000000000000, 0x20 };
