  B.SetInsertPoint(Merge);
  auto *S = B.CreatePHI(I32, 2, "s");
  S->addIncoming(TS, Then);
  S->addIncoming(TU, Else);
  auto *T = B.CreateXor(B.CreateXor(B.CreateAdd(A, C), B.CreateSub(A, C)),
                        B.getInt32(0x5A5A));
  auto *U = B.CreateOr(B.CreateAnd(A, C), B.CreateAdd(T, B.getInt32(12345)));
  auto *Res = B.CreateXor(B.CreateXor(S, T), U);
  B.CreateRet(Res);
  assert(!llvm::verifyModule(*M, &llvm::errs()));
  return M;
}

// 256-bit word-lane vector saturating arithmetic (sadd/ssub/uadd/usub.sat on
// <8 x i32>) — the 256-bit dual of vsat32 (<4 x i32>) and the first 256-bit
// saturating shape (the 256-bit matrix had arith / shift / min-max but never
// saturation).  No target has a native 256-bit saturating op, so it splits into
// two 128-bit halves; per half x86 SSE2 has NO native i32 saturation (only
// i8/i16 padds*) so each lane expands to add/sub + overflow-compare + blend,
// while AArch64/ARM NEON use sqadd.4s / uqadd.4s / sqsub.4s / uqsub.4s.  Lanes
// carry near-extreme i32 magnitudes (INT_MAX / 0x40000000 / sign-bit derived)
// so the signed and unsigned clamp edges actually fire; all integer, zero
// libcall. No obfuscation pass touches the saturating intrinsics, so
// orig/obfuscated lower byte-identically — any Unicorn mismatch is a real
// rewrite-backend / fork-Unicorn bug.  Multi-block (diamond + PHI); the
// add/sub/and/or/xor mix + 0x5A5A / 12345 drive --subst / --const-enc and the
// control-flow passes.
std::unique_ptr<llvm::Module> buildVecWide256SatIR(llvm::LLVMContext &Ctx,
                                                   const char *Triple) {
  auto M = std::make_unique<llvm::Module>("substtest", Ctx);
  M->setTargetTriple(llvm::Triple(Triple));
  auto *I32 = llvm::Type::getInt32Ty(Ctx);
  auto *V8 = llvm::FixedVectorType::get(I32, 8);
  auto *FTy = llvm::FunctionType::get(I32, {I32, I32}, false);
  auto *F = llvm::Function::Create(FTy, llvm::Function::ExternalLinkage,
                                   "vsat256", M.get());
  auto *Entry = llvm::BasicBlock::Create(Ctx, "entry", F);
  auto *Then = llvm::BasicBlock::Create(Ctx, "then", F);
  auto *Else = llvm::BasicBlock::Create(Ctx, "else", F);
  auto *Merge = llvm::BasicBlock::Create(Ctx, "merge", F);
  auto *A = F->getArg(0), *C = F->getArg(1);

  llvm::IRBuilder<> B(Entry);
  // Lanes mix arg-derived values with near-extreme constants so the signed and
  // unsigned saturation edges fire across the 8 lanes.
  uint32_t BigA[8] = {0u,          0x55555555u, 0x40000000u, 0x7FFFFFFFu,
                      0x80000000u, 0xFFFFFFFFu, 0x7FFFFFF0u, 0x10u};
  uint32_t BigB[8] = {0x40000000u, 0x40000000u, 0x10u,       0x7FFFFFFFu,
                      0x80000000u, 0x1u,        0xFFFFFFF0u, 0x20u};
  auto *BigAV =
      llvm::ConstantDataVector::get(Ctx, llvm::ArrayRef<uint32_t>(BigA, 8));
  auto *BigBV =
      llvm::ConstantDataVector::get(Ctx, llvm::ArrayRef<uint32_t>(BigB, 8));
  auto *Va = B.CreateXor(B.CreateVectorSplat(8, A), BigAV);
  auto *Vb = B.CreateSub(BigBV, B.CreateVectorSplat(8, C));
  auto *Sa = B.CreateBinaryIntrinsic(llvm::Intrinsic::sadd_sat, Va, Vb);
  auto *Ss = B.CreateBinaryIntrinsic(llvm::Intrinsic::ssub_sat, Va, Vb);
  auto *Ua = B.CreateBinaryIntrinsic(llvm::Intrinsic::uadd_sat, Va, Vb);
  auto *Us = B.CreateBinaryIntrinsic(llvm::Intrinsic::usub_sat, Va, Vb);
  auto *Vx = B.CreateXor(B.CreateXor(Sa, Ss), B.CreateXor(Ua, Us));
  auto *S = B.CreateAddReduce(Vx);
  auto *T = B.CreateXor(B.CreateXor(B.CreateAdd(A, C), B.CreateSub(A, C)),
                        B.getInt32(0x5A5A));
  auto *U = B.CreateOr(B.CreateAnd(A, C), B.CreateAdd(T, B.getInt32(12345)));
  auto *Base = B.CreateXor(B.CreateXor(S, T), U);
  auto *Sel = B.CreateAnd(B.CreateXor(A, C), B.getInt32(1));
  B.CreateCondBr(B.CreateICmpNE(Sel, B.getInt32(0)), Then, Else);
  B.SetInsertPoint(Then);
  auto *RT = B.CreateAdd(Base, A);
  B.CreateBr(Merge);
  B.SetInsertPoint(Else);
  auto *RE = B.CreateXor(Base, C);
  B.CreateBr(Merge);
  B.SetInsertPoint(Merge);
  auto *Res = B.CreatePHI(I32, 2, "res");
  Res->addIncoming(RT, Then);
  Res->addIncoming(RE, Else);
  B.CreateRet(Res);
  assert(!llvm::verifyModule(*M, &llvm::errs()));
  return M;
}

// 256-bit word-lane vector funnel shift / rotate (llvm.fshl / fshr on <8 x i32>
// with a splat constant amount) — the 256-bit dual of vfunnel (<4 x i32>) and
// the first 256-bit funnel shape (the 256-bit matrix had arith / shift /
// min-max / saturation but never funnel/rotate).  No target has a native
// 256-bit funnel, so it splits into two 128-bit halves; per half x86 pre-AVX2
// has no per-lane rotate so it lowers to vector shift + or, AArch64/ARM NEON
// use ushl/shl + or. A splat *constant* amount keeps it off the per-lane
// variable-rotate path (vfunnelv covers that for <4 x i32>).  Zero libcall.  No
// obfuscation pass touches fshl/fshr, so orig/obfuscated lower byte-identically
// — any Unicorn mismatch is a real rewrite-backend / fork-Unicorn bug.
std::unique_ptr<llvm::Module> buildVecWide256FunnelIR(llvm::LLVMContext &Ctx,
                                                      const char *Triple) {
  auto M = std::make_unique<llvm::Module>("substtest", Ctx);
  M->setTargetTriple(llvm::Triple(Triple));
  auto *I32 = llvm::Type::getInt32Ty(Ctx);
  auto *V8 = llvm::FixedVectorType::get(I32, 8);
  auto *FTy = llvm::FunctionType::get(I32, {I32, I32}, false);
  auto *F = llvm::Function::Create(FTy, llvm::Function::ExternalLinkage,
                                   "vfunnel256", M.get());
  auto *Entry = llvm::BasicBlock::Create(Ctx, "entry", F);
  auto *Then = llvm::BasicBlock::Create(Ctx, "then", F);
  auto *Else = llvm::BasicBlock::Create(Ctx, "else", F);
  auto *Merge = llvm::BasicBlock::Create(Ctx, "merge", F);
  auto *A = F->getArg(0), *C = F->getArg(1);

  llvm::IRBuilder<> B(Entry);
  llvm::Value *VA = llvm::UndefValue::get(V8), *VB = llvm::UndefValue::get(V8);
  for (unsigned i = 0; i < 8; ++i) {
    VA = B.CreateInsertElement(VA, B.CreateAdd(A, B.getInt32(i * 131 + 7)),
                               B.getInt32(i));
    VB = B.CreateInsertElement(VB, B.CreateXor(C, B.getInt32(i * 37 + 3)),
                               B.getInt32(i));
  }
  auto *Amt7 = B.CreateVectorSplat(8, B.getInt32(7));
  auto *Amt11 = B.CreateVectorSplat(8, B.getInt32(11));
  auto *Fl = B.CreateIntrinsic(llvm::Intrinsic::fshl, {V8}, {VA, VB, Amt7});
  auto *Fr = B.CreateIntrinsic(llvm::Intrinsic::fshr, {V8}, {VA, VB, Amt11});
  auto *Red = B.CreateAddReduce(B.CreateXor(Fl, Fr));
  auto *T = B.CreateXor(B.CreateXor(B.CreateAdd(A, C), B.CreateSub(A, C)),
                        B.getInt32(0x5A5A));
  auto *U = B.CreateOr(B.CreateAnd(A, C), B.CreateAdd(T, B.getInt32(12345)));
  llvm::Value *Base = B.CreateXor(B.CreateXor(Red, T), U);
  auto *Sel = B.CreateAnd(B.CreateXor(A, C), B.getInt32(1));
  B.CreateCondBr(B.CreateICmpNE(Sel, B.getInt32(0)), Then, Else);
  B.SetInsertPoint(Then);
  auto *RT = B.CreateAdd(Base, A);
  B.CreateBr(Merge);
  B.SetInsertPoint(Else);
  auto *RE = B.CreateXor(Base, C);
  B.CreateBr(Merge);
  B.SetInsertPoint(Merge);
  auto *Res = B.CreatePHI(I32, 2, "res");
  Res->addIncoming(RT, Then);
  Res->addIncoming(RE, Else);
  B.CreateRet(Res);
  assert(!llvm::verifyModule(*M, &llvm::errs()));
  return M;
}

// 256-bit i64-lane vector integer min/max (smax/smin/umax/umin on <4 x i64>) —
// the i64-lane dual of vw256mm (<8 x i32>) and vminmax64 (<2 x i64>); the
// 256-bit i64 lane was never covered.  <4 x i64> splits into two 128-bit
// halves; per half x86 SSE2 has no i64 vector compare (pcmpgtq is SSE4.2) so
// min/max expand to a 64-bit compare + blend, AArch64 NEON has no i64-lane
// min/max (only up to .4s) so it compares/selects too, and the 32-bit ISAs
// (i386/ARM32) scalarize each i64 lane to register-pair compare/select — a path
// no narrower min/max reaches. Lanes mix signs (high bit flipped on some lanes)
// so signed != unsigned.  All integer, zero libcall.  No obfuscation pass
// touches min/max intrinsics, so orig/obfuscated lower byte-identically — any
// Unicorn mismatch is a real rewrite-backend / fork-Unicorn bug.
std::unique_ptr<llvm::Module> buildVecWide256MinMax64IR(llvm::LLVMContext &Ctx,
                                                        const char *Triple) {
  auto M = std::make_unique<llvm::Module>("substtest", Ctx);
  M->setTargetTriple(llvm::Triple(Triple));
  auto *I32 = llvm::Type::getInt32Ty(Ctx);
  auto *I64 = llvm::Type::getInt64Ty(Ctx);
  auto *V4 = llvm::FixedVectorType::get(I64, 4);
  auto *FTy = llvm::FunctionType::get(I32, {I32, I32}, false);
  auto *F = llvm::Function::Create(FTy, llvm::Function::ExternalLinkage,
                                   "vmm256_64", M.get());
  auto *Entry = llvm::BasicBlock::Create(Ctx, "entry", F);
  auto *Then = llvm::BasicBlock::Create(Ctx, "then", F);
  auto *Else = llvm::BasicBlock::Create(Ctx, "else", F);
  auto *Merge = llvm::BasicBlock::Create(Ctx, "merge", F);
  auto *A = F->getArg(0), *C = F->getArg(1);

  llvm::IRBuilder<> B(Entry);
  auto *A64 = B.CreateSExt(A, I64), *C64 = B.CreateSExt(C, I64);
  llvm::Value *VA = llvm::UndefValue::get(V4);
  llvm::Value *VB = llvm::UndefValue::get(V4);
  for (unsigned i = 0; i < 4; ++i) {
    auto *La = B.CreateXor(
        B.CreateAdd(B.CreateShl(A64, llvm::ConstantInt::get(I64, 8)),
                    llvm::ConstantInt::get(I64, (uint64_t)i * 0x1111111 + 1)),
        llvm::ConstantInt::get(I64, (i & 1) ? 0x8000000000000000ull : 0ull));
    auto *Lb = B.CreateXor(
        B.CreateSub(llvm::ConstantInt::get(I64, (uint64_t)i * 0x2222222 + 3),
                    B.CreateShl(C64, llvm::ConstantInt::get(I64, 8))),
        llvm::ConstantInt::get(I64, (i & 2) ? 0x8000000000000000ull : 0ull));
    VA = B.CreateInsertElement(VA, La, B.getInt32(i));
    VB = B.CreateInsertElement(VB, Lb, B.getInt32(i));
  }
  auto *Sx = B.CreateIntrinsic(llvm::Intrinsic::smax, {V4}, {VA, VB});
  auto *Sn = B.CreateIntrinsic(llvm::Intrinsic::smin, {V4}, {VA, VB});
  auto *Ux = B.CreateIntrinsic(llvm::Intrinsic::umax, {V4}, {VA, VB});
  auto *Un = B.CreateIntrinsic(llvm::Intrinsic::umin, {V4}, {VA, VB});
  auto fold = [&](llvm::Value *V) -> llvm::Value * {
    llvm::Value *Acc = B.getInt32(0);
    for (unsigned i = 0; i < 4; ++i) {
      auto *L = B.CreateExtractElement(V, B.getInt32(i));
      auto *Lo = B.CreateTrunc(L, I32);
      auto *Hi =
          B.CreateTrunc(B.CreateLShr(L, llvm::ConstantInt::get(I64, 32)), I32);
      Acc = B.CreateXor(Acc, B.CreateXor(Lo, Hi));
    }
    return Acc;
  };
  llvm::Value *Base = B.CreateXor(B.CreateXor(fold(Sx), fold(Sn)),
                                  B.CreateXor(fold(Ux), fold(Un)));
  auto *T = B.CreateXor(B.CreateXor(B.CreateAdd(A, C), B.CreateSub(A, C)),
                        B.getInt32(0x5A5A));
  auto *U = B.CreateOr(B.CreateAnd(A, C), B.CreateAdd(T, B.getInt32(12345)));
  Base = B.CreateXor(B.CreateXor(Base, T), U);
  auto *Sel = B.CreateAnd(B.CreateXor(A, C), B.getInt32(1));
  B.CreateCondBr(B.CreateICmpNE(Sel, B.getInt32(0)), Then, Else);
  B.SetInsertPoint(Then);
  auto *RT = B.CreateAdd(Base, A);
  B.CreateBr(Merge);
  B.SetInsertPoint(Else);
  auto *RE = B.CreateXor(Base, C);
  B.CreateBr(Merge);
  B.SetInsertPoint(Merge);
  auto *Res = B.CreatePHI(I32, 2, "res");
  Res->addIncoming(RT, Then);
  Res->addIncoming(RE, Else);
  B.CreateRet(Res);
  assert(!llvm::verifyModule(*M, &llvm::errs()));
  return M;
}

// Vector saturating shift-left (llvm.sshl.sat / ushl.sat on <4 x i32> and
// <8 x i16>) — the *vector* dual of the scalar sshl.sat/ushl.sat already
// covered by the `oflow` shape (buildOverflowIR); the vector legalization
// (expandShlSat per lane) was never exercised.  x86 SSE2 has NO vector
// saturating shift and no per-lane variable shift pre-AVX2, so each lane
// expands to shift + shift-back-compare overflow detect + clamp to INT_MAX/MIN
// (signed) or UINT_MAX (unsigned) — a dense fixup/const-pool path; AArch64 NEON
// uses native sqshl.4s/uqshl.4s (and .8h), ARM32 NEON vqshl.s32/vqshl.u32.
// Shift amounts are per-lane *constants* in [0,width) so they never go out of
// range (sshl.sat with amount >= bitwidth is poison) and never hit the
// variable-shift libcall; value lanes are arg-derived XOR near-extreme
// constants so the signed and unsigned saturation edges genuinely fire across
// lanes.  Zero libcall.  No obfuscation pass touches sshl.sat/ushl.sat
// (intrinsic, not add/sub/and/or/xor; the vector-constant shift amount is not a
// scalar ICmp/BinOp operand for --const-enc), so orig/obfuscated lower
// byte-identically — any Unicorn mismatch is a real rewrite-backend /
// fork-Unicorn bug.  Multi-block (diamond + PHI) gives the control-flow passes
// real structure.
std::unique_ptr<llvm::Module> buildVecShlSatIR(llvm::LLVMContext &Ctx,
                                               const char *Triple) {
  auto M = std::make_unique<llvm::Module>("substtest", Ctx);
  M->setTargetTriple(llvm::Triple(Triple));
  auto *I16 = llvm::Type::getInt16Ty(Ctx);
  auto *I32 = llvm::Type::getInt32Ty(Ctx);
  auto *FTy = llvm::FunctionType::get(I32, {I32, I32}, false);
  auto *F = llvm::Function::Create(FTy, llvm::Function::ExternalLinkage,
                                   "vshlsat", M.get());
  auto *Entry = llvm::BasicBlock::Create(Ctx, "entry", F);
  auto *Then = llvm::BasicBlock::Create(Ctx, "then", F);
  auto *Else = llvm::BasicBlock::Create(Ctx, "else", F);
  auto *Merge = llvm::BasicBlock::Create(Ctx, "merge", F);
  auto *A = F->getArg(0), *C = F->getArg(1);

  llvm::IRBuilder<> B(Entry);

  // <4 x i32>: value lanes arg-derived XOR near-extreme constants; per-lane
  // constant shift amounts in [0,31] so some lanes saturate, some do not.
  uint32_t BigA[4] = {0x40000000u, 0x7FFFFFFFu, 0x80000000u, 0x00000001u};
  uint32_t Sh32[4] = {3u, 1u, 4u, 2u};
  auto *BigAV =
      llvm::ConstantDataVector::get(Ctx, llvm::ArrayRef<uint32_t>(BigA, 4));
  auto *Sh32V =
      llvm::ConstantDataVector::get(Ctx, llvm::ArrayRef<uint32_t>(Sh32, 4));
  auto *Va = B.CreateXor(B.CreateVectorSplat(4, A), BigAV);
  auto *Ss32 = B.CreateBinaryIntrinsic(llvm::Intrinsic::sshl_sat, Va, Sh32V);
  auto *Us32 = B.CreateBinaryIntrinsic(llvm::Intrinsic::ushl_sat, Va, Sh32V);
  auto *S32 = B.CreateAddReduce(B.CreateXor(Ss32, Us32));

  // <8 x i16>: same, halfword lanes; per-lane constant shift amounts in [0,15].
  auto *Ah = B.CreateTrunc(A, I16);
  uint16_t BigH[8] = {0x4000, 0x7fff, 0x8000, 0x0001,
                      0x7ffe, 0x8001, 0xc000, 0x0002};
  uint16_t Sh16[8] = {3, 1, 4, 2, 5, 1, 6, 2};
  auto *BigHV =
      llvm::ConstantDataVector::get(Ctx, llvm::ArrayRef<uint16_t>(BigH, 8));
  auto *Sh16V =
      llvm::ConstantDataVector::get(Ctx, llvm::ArrayRef<uint16_t>(Sh16, 8));
  auto *Vh = B.CreateXor(B.CreateVectorSplat(8, Ah), BigHV);
  auto *Ss16 = B.CreateBinaryIntrinsic(llvm::Intrinsic::sshl_sat, Vh, Sh16V);
  auto *Us16 = B.CreateBinaryIntrinsic(llvm::Intrinsic::ushl_sat, Vh, Sh16V);
  auto *Vx16 = B.CreateXor(Ss16, Us16);
  llvm::Value *Acc16 = B.getInt16(0);
  for (unsigned i = 0; i < 8; ++i)
    Acc16 = B.CreateXor(Acc16, B.CreateExtractElement(Vx16, B.getInt32(i)));
  auto *S16 = B.CreateZExt(Acc16, I32);

  llvm::Value *S = B.CreateXor(S32, S16);
  auto *T = B.CreateXor(B.CreateXor(B.CreateAdd(A, C), B.CreateSub(A, C)),
                        B.getInt32(0x5A5A));
  auto *U = B.CreateOr(B.CreateAnd(A, C), B.CreateAdd(T, B.getInt32(12345)));
  auto *Base = B.CreateXor(B.CreateXor(S, T), U);
  auto *Sel = B.CreateAnd(B.CreateXor(A, C), B.getInt32(1));
  B.CreateCondBr(B.CreateICmpNE(Sel, B.getInt32(0)), Then, Else);
  B.SetInsertPoint(Then);
  auto *RT = B.CreateAdd(Base, A);
  B.CreateBr(Merge);
  B.SetInsertPoint(Else);
  auto *RE = B.CreateXor(Base, C);
  B.CreateBr(Merge);
  B.SetInsertPoint(Merge);
  auto *Res = B.CreatePHI(I32, 2, "res");
  Res->addIncoming(RT, Then);
  Res->addIncoming(RE, Else);
  B.CreateRet(Res);
  assert(!llvm::verifyModule(*M, &llvm::errs()));
  return M;
}

// Wide (i64) checked-arithmetic intrinsics (llvm.sadd/uadd/ssub/usub.with.
// overflow on i64) — the i64 dual of the scalar i32 .with.overflow already
// covered by the `oflow` shape (buildOverflowIR).  On 32-bit targets
// (i386/ARM32) an i64 add/sub-with-overflow lowers to a multi-word carry/borrow
// chain (ADD+ADC / SUB+SBC) plus overflow-flag extraction — carry-out for the
// unsigned variants, the V flag after the high word for the signed ones — a
// path the i32 oflow shape never reaches; on x86-64/AArch64 it is a single
// ADDS/SUBS with a native flag read.  Operands are built from both args shifted
// into the high word, then pushed to the i64 signed/unsigned boundaries with
// extreme constants (0x7FFF.../0x8000.../0xFFFF...) so signed and unsigned
// overflow genuinely fire for some inputs and stay quiet for others.
// smul/umul.with. overflow on i64 are deliberately excluded: a 64x64 checked
// multiply on a 32-bit target calls __mulodi4/__muloti4 (a libcall,
// unresolvable in the freestanding harness), exactly as vredi64 excludes
// reduce.mul; every add/sub-with-overflow path here is zero-libcall on all four
// ISAs.  The obfuscation passes do not touch the .with.overflow intrinsics
// themselves (the multi-word carry/overflow lowering is identical between orig
// and obfuscated);
// --const-enc may re-encrypt the i64 carrier constants but preserves their
// values, so the two stay semantically equivalent — any Unicorn return/data
// mismatch is a real rewrite-backend / fork-Unicorn bug.  Multi-block (diamond
// + PHI) gives the control-flow passes real structure.
std::unique_ptr<llvm::Module> buildWideOverflowIR(llvm::LLVMContext &Ctx,
                                                  const char *Triple) {
  auto M = std::make_unique<llvm::Module>("substtest", Ctx);
  M->setTargetTriple(llvm::Triple(Triple));
  auto *I32 = llvm::Type::getInt32Ty(Ctx);
  auto *I64 = llvm::Type::getInt64Ty(Ctx);
  auto *FTy = llvm::FunctionType::get(I32, {I32, I32}, false);
  auto *F = llvm::Function::Create(FTy, llvm::Function::ExternalLinkage,
                                   "wovfl", M.get());
  auto *Entry = llvm::BasicBlock::Create(Ctx, "entry", F);
  auto *Then = llvm::BasicBlock::Create(Ctx, "then", F);
  auto *Else = llvm::BasicBlock::Create(Ctx, "else", F);
  auto *Merge = llvm::BasicBlock::Create(Ctx, "merge", F);
  auto *A = F->getArg(0), *C = F->getArg(1);

  llvm::IRBuilder<> B(Entry);
  auto ovPair = [&](unsigned IID, llvm::Value *X, llvm::Value *Y) {
    auto *R = B.CreateIntrinsic(IID, {I64}, {X, Y});
    auto *V = B.CreateExtractValue(R, 0);
    auto *O = B.CreateZExt(B.CreateExtractValue(R, 1), I64);
    return std::pair<llvm::Value *, llvm::Value *>{V, O};
  };
  // Wide operands derived from both args (both 32-bit words vary across inputs)
  // then pushed near the i64 signed/unsigned boundaries.
  auto *Aw = B.CreateZExt(A, I64), *Cw = B.CreateZExt(C, I64);
  auto *Big = B.CreateOr(B.CreateShl(Aw, B.getInt64(32)), Cw);  // (A<<32)|C
  auto *Big2 = B.CreateOr(B.CreateShl(Cw, B.getInt64(32)), Aw); // (C<<32)|A
  auto *PosA = B.CreateXor(Big, B.getInt64(0x7FFFFFFFFFFFFF00ULL));
  auto *PosC = B.CreateOr(Big2, B.getInt64(0x4000000000000000ULL));
  auto *NegA = B.CreateOr(Big, B.getInt64(0x8000000000000000ULL));
  auto *PosD = B.CreateAnd(Big2, B.getInt64(0x7FFFFFFFFFFFFFFFULL));

  auto [Sv, So] = ovPair(llvm::Intrinsic::sadd_with_overflow, PosA, PosC);
  auto [Uv, Uo] = ovPair(llvm::Intrinsic::uadd_with_overflow, NegA, PosC);
  auto [Sdv, Sdo] = ovPair(llvm::Intrinsic::ssub_with_overflow, NegA, PosD);
  auto [Udv, Udo] = ovPair(llvm::Intrinsic::usub_with_overflow, Big, Big2);

  // Fold every i64 value + overflow bit into one accumulator, then collapse to
  // i32 (low XOR high) for the return.
  llvm::Value *Acc = B.CreateXor(Sv, B.CreateShl(So, B.getInt64(1)));
  Acc = B.CreateXor(Acc, B.CreateShl(Uv, B.getInt64(3)));
  Acc = B.CreateXor(Acc, B.CreateShl(Uo, B.getInt64(2)));
  Acc = B.CreateXor(Acc, Sdv);
  Acc = B.CreateXor(Acc, B.CreateShl(Sdo, B.getInt64(4)));
  Acc = B.CreateXor(Acc, Udv);
  Acc = B.CreateXor(Acc, B.CreateShl(Udo, B.getInt64(5)));
  auto *Lo = B.CreateTrunc(Acc, I32);
  auto *Hi = B.CreateTrunc(B.CreateLShr(Acc, B.getInt64(32)), I32);
  auto *S = B.CreateXor(Lo, Hi);

  auto *T = B.CreateXor(B.CreateXor(B.CreateAdd(A, C), B.CreateSub(A, C)),
                        B.getInt32(0x5A5A));
  auto *U = B.CreateOr(B.CreateAnd(A, C), B.CreateAdd(T, B.getInt32(12345)));
  auto *Base = B.CreateXor(B.CreateXor(S, T), U);
  auto *Sel = B.CreateAnd(B.CreateXor(A, C), B.getInt32(1));
  B.CreateCondBr(B.CreateICmpNE(Sel, B.getInt32(0)), Then, Else);

  B.SetInsertPoint(Then);
  auto *RT = B.CreateAdd(Base, A);
  B.CreateBr(Merge);
  B.SetInsertPoint(Else);
  auto *RE = B.CreateXor(Base, C);
  B.CreateBr(Merge);

  B.SetInsertPoint(Merge);
  auto *Res = B.CreatePHI(I32, 2, "res");
  Res->addIncoming(RT, Then);
  Res->addIncoming(RE, Else);
  B.CreateRet(Res);
  assert(!llvm::verifyModule(*M, &llvm::errs()));
  return M;
}

// 256-bit (<8 x i32>) vector 3-way compare (llvm.scmp / llvm.ucmp) -- the
// 256-bit-wide companion of vtcmp (<4 x i32>), vtcmp64 (<2 x i64>), vtcmp8
// (<16 x i8>/<8 x i16>) and vntcmp64 (<8 x i8>/<4 x i16>), completing the
// 3-way-compare lane-width matrix with the 256-bit form.  No target has a
// 256-bit integer register (x86/i386 SSE2 and AArch64/ARM NEON are 128-bit), so
// the <8 x i32> compare legalizes into a 2x128 split, each half lowering the
// already-covered <4 x i32> path (x86 has no native vector 3-way compare so
// each lane is (a sgt b) - (a slt b), unsigned flipping the sign bit first).
// Lanes mix high-bit-set values so signed vs unsigned ordering really diverges.
// Pure compare+select, zero libcall.  No obfuscation pass touches scmp/ucmp, so
// original/obfuscated lower byte-identically -- any Unicorn mismatch is a real
// backend / fork-Unicorn bug.  Multi-block (diamond + PHI); the add/sub/and/or/
// xor mix + 0x5A5A / 12345 drive --subst / --const-enc and the control-flow
// passes.
std::unique_ptr<llvm::Module>
buildVecWide256ThreeWayCmpIR(llvm::LLVMContext &Ctx, const char *Triple) {
  auto M = std::make_unique<llvm::Module>("substtest", Ctx);
  M->setTargetTriple(llvm::Triple(Triple));
  auto *I32 = llvm::Type::getInt32Ty(Ctx);
  auto *V8 = llvm::FixedVectorType::get(I32, 8);
  auto *FTy = llvm::FunctionType::get(I32, {I32, I32}, false);
  auto *F = llvm::Function::Create(FTy, llvm::Function::ExternalLinkage,
                                   "vtcmp256", M.get());
  auto *Entry = llvm::BasicBlock::Create(Ctx, "entry", F);
  auto *Then = llvm::BasicBlock::Create(Ctx, "then", F);
  auto *Else = llvm::BasicBlock::Create(Ctx, "else", F);
  auto *Merge = llvm::BasicBlock::Create(Ctx, "merge", F);
  auto *A = F->getArg(0), *C = F->getArg(1);

  llvm::IRBuilder<> B(Entry);
  llvm::Value *VA = llvm::UndefValue::get(V8);
  llvm::Value *VB = llvm::UndefValue::get(V8);
  for (unsigned i = 0; i < 8; ++i) {
    auto *La = B.CreateXor(B.CreateAdd(A, B.getInt32(i * 7 + 1)),
                           B.getInt32((i & 1) ? 0x80000000U : 0U));
    auto *Lb = B.CreateXor(B.CreateSub(C, B.getInt32(i * 5 + 2)),
                           B.getInt32((i & 1) ? 0x40000000U : 0U));
    VA = B.CreateInsertElement(VA, La, B.getInt32(i));
    VB = B.CreateInsertElement(VB, Lb, B.getInt32(i));
  }
  auto *Sx = B.CreateIntrinsic(llvm::Intrinsic::scmp, {V8, V8}, {VA, VB});
  auto *Ux = B.CreateIntrinsic(llvm::Intrinsic::ucmp, {V8, V8}, {VA, VB});
  llvm::Value *Base = B.getInt32(0);
  for (unsigned i = 0; i < 8; ++i) {
    auto *Sl = B.CreateExtractElement(Sx, B.getInt32(i));
    auto *Ul = B.CreateExtractElement(Ux, B.getInt32(i));
    Base = B.CreateAdd(Base, B.CreateShl(Sl, B.getInt32((i * 4 + 1) & 31)));
    Base = B.CreateXor(Base, B.CreateShl(Ul, B.getInt32((i * 5 + 2) & 31)));
  }
  auto *T = B.CreateXor(B.CreateXor(B.CreateAdd(A, C), B.CreateSub(A, C)),
                        B.getInt32(0x5A5A));
  auto *U = B.CreateOr(B.CreateAnd(A, C), B.CreateAdd(T, B.getInt32(12345)));
  Base = B.CreateXor(B.CreateXor(Base, T), U);
  auto *Sel = B.CreateAnd(B.CreateXor(A, C), B.getInt32(1));
  B.CreateCondBr(B.CreateICmpNE(Sel, B.getInt32(0)), Then, Else);
  B.SetInsertPoint(Then);
  auto *RT = B.CreateAdd(Base, A);
  B.CreateBr(Merge);
  B.SetInsertPoint(Else);
  auto *RE = B.CreateXor(Base, C);
  B.CreateBr(Merge);
  B.SetInsertPoint(Merge);
  auto *Res = B.CreatePHI(I32, 2, "res");
  Res->addIncoming(RT, Then);
  Res->addIncoming(RE, Else);
  B.CreateRet(Res);
  assert(!llvm::verifyModule(*M, &llvm::errs()));
  return M;
}

// 256-bit byte/halfword-lane vector integer min/max (llvm.smax/smin/umax/umin
// on <32 x i8> and <16 x i16>) -- the 256-bit narrow-lane companion of vminmax8
// (<16 x i8>/<8 x i16> 128-bit) and vw256mm (<8 x i32> 256-bit), completing the
// 256-bit min/max coverage for byte/halfword lanes.  No target has a 256-bit
// integer register so each splits into 2x128 halves; per half x86 SSE2 has the
// asymmetric native/emulated mix (pminub/pmaxub native for unsigned i8 but
// signed i8 is SSE4.1 -> pcmpgtb+blend; pminsw/pmaxsw native for signed i16 but
// unsigned i16 is SSE4.1 -> bias-xor+pcmpgtw+blend), AArch64/ARM NEON have all
// four native on .16b/.8h.  Lanes mix near-extreme constants (0x7f/0x80/0xff
// bytes, 0x7fff/0x8000 halfwords) so the signed and unsigned orderings really
// diverge.  All integer, zero libcall.  No obfuscation pass touches min/max
// intrinsics, so orig/obfuscated lower byte-identically -- any Unicorn mismatch
// is a real backend / fork-Unicorn bug.
std::unique_ptr<llvm::Module> buildVecWide256MinMax8IR(llvm::LLVMContext &Ctx,
                                                       const char *Triple) {
  auto M = std::make_unique<llvm::Module>("substtest", Ctx);
  M->setTargetTriple(llvm::Triple(Triple));
  auto *I8 = llvm::Type::getInt8Ty(Ctx);
  auto *I16 = llvm::Type::getInt16Ty(Ctx);
  auto *I32 = llvm::Type::getInt32Ty(Ctx);
  auto *V32 = llvm::FixedVectorType::get(I8, 32);
  auto *V16 = llvm::FixedVectorType::get(I16, 16);
  auto *FTy = llvm::FunctionType::get(I32, {I32, I32}, false);
  auto *F = llvm::Function::Create(FTy, llvm::Function::ExternalLinkage,
                                   "vw256mm8", M.get());
  auto *Entry = llvm::BasicBlock::Create(Ctx, "entry", F);
  auto *Then = llvm::BasicBlock::Create(Ctx, "then", F);
  auto *Else = llvm::BasicBlock::Create(Ctx, "else", F);
  auto *Merge = llvm::BasicBlock::Create(Ctx, "merge", F);
  auto *A = F->getArg(0), *C = F->getArg(1);

  llvm::IRBuilder<> B(Entry);

  // <32 x i8>: arg-derived lanes vs near-extreme byte constants.
  auto *Ab = B.CreateTrunc(A, I8), *Cb = B.CreateTrunc(C, I8);
  uint8_t BigB[32] = {0x7f, 0x80, 0xff, 0x01, 0x40, 0xc0, 0x7e, 0x81,
                      0x10, 0xf0, 0x33, 0xcc, 0x55, 0xaa, 0x08, 0x7f,
                      0x00, 0x80, 0x7f, 0xfe, 0x02, 0xbf, 0x41, 0x90,
                      0x6f, 0x11, 0xee, 0x44, 0x99, 0x5a, 0xa5, 0x80};
  auto *BigBV =
      llvm::ConstantDataVector::get(Ctx, llvm::ArrayRef<uint8_t>(BigB, 32));
  llvm::Value *VA8 = llvm::UndefValue::get(V32);
  for (unsigned i = 0; i < 32; ++i)
    VA8 = B.CreateInsertElement(
        VA8, B.CreateAdd(Ab, B.getInt8((uint8_t)(i * 7 + 1))), B.getInt32(i));
  auto *VB8 = B.CreateXor(B.CreateVectorSplat(32, Cb), BigBV);
  auto *Sx8 = B.CreateIntrinsic(llvm::Intrinsic::smax, {V32}, {VA8, VB8});
  auto *Sn8 = B.CreateIntrinsic(llvm::Intrinsic::smin, {V32}, {VA8, VB8});
  auto *Ux8 = B.CreateIntrinsic(llvm::Intrinsic::umax, {V32}, {VA8, VB8});
  auto *Un8 = B.CreateIntrinsic(llvm::Intrinsic::umin, {V32}, {VA8, VB8});
  auto Red8 = [&](llvm::Value *V) -> llvm::Value * {
    llvm::Value *Acc = B.getInt8(0);
    for (unsigned i = 0; i < 32; ++i)
      Acc = B.CreateXor(Acc, B.CreateExtractElement(V, B.getInt32(i)));
    return B.CreateZExt(Acc, I32);
  };

  // <16 x i16>: arg-derived lanes vs near-extreme halfword constants.
  auto *Ah = B.CreateTrunc(A, I16), *Ch = B.CreateTrunc(C, I16);
  uint16_t BigH[16] = {0x7fff, 0x8000, 0xffff, 0x0001, 0x4000, 0xc000,
                       0x7ffe, 0x8001, 0x0000, 0x00ff, 0x7f00, 0x9abc,
                       0x1234, 0xfedc, 0x5a5a, 0x8000};
  auto *BigHV =
      llvm::ConstantDataVector::get(Ctx, llvm::ArrayRef<uint16_t>(BigH, 16));
  llvm::Value *VA16 = llvm::UndefValue::get(V16);
  for (unsigned i = 0; i < 16; ++i)
    VA16 = B.CreateInsertElement(
        VA16, B.CreateAdd(Ah, B.getInt16((uint16_t)(i * 131 + 7))),
        B.getInt32(i));
  auto *VB16 = B.CreateXor(B.CreateVectorSplat(16, Ch), BigHV);
  auto *Sx16 = B.CreateIntrinsic(llvm::Intrinsic::smax, {V16}, {VA16, VB16});
  auto *Sn16 = B.CreateIntrinsic(llvm::Intrinsic::smin, {V16}, {VA16, VB16});
  auto *Ux16 = B.CreateIntrinsic(llvm::Intrinsic::umax, {V16}, {VA16, VB16});
  auto *Un16 = B.CreateIntrinsic(llvm::Intrinsic::umin, {V16}, {VA16, VB16});
  auto Red16 = [&](llvm::Value *V) -> llvm::Value * {
    llvm::Value *Acc = B.getInt16(0);
    for (unsigned i = 0; i < 16; ++i)
      Acc = B.CreateXor(Acc, B.CreateExtractElement(V, B.getInt32(i)));
    return B.CreateZExt(Acc, I32);
  };

  llvm::Value *S8 =
      B.CreateXor(B.CreateXor(Red8(Sx8), B.CreateShl(Red8(Sn8), B.getInt32(1))),
                  B.CreateXor(Red8(Ux8), Red8(Un8)));
  llvm::Value *S16 = B.CreateXor(
      B.CreateXor(Red16(Sx16), B.CreateShl(Red16(Sn16), B.getInt32(1))),
      B.CreateXor(Red16(Ux16), Red16(Un16)));
  llvm::Value *S = B.CreateXor(S8, S16);

  auto *T = B.CreateXor(B.CreateXor(B.CreateAdd(A, C), B.CreateSub(A, C)),
                        B.getInt32(0x5A5A));
  auto *U = B.CreateOr(B.CreateAnd(A, C), B.CreateAdd(T, B.getInt32(12345)));
  llvm::Value *Base = B.CreateXor(B.CreateXor(S, T), U);
  auto *Sel = B.CreateAnd(B.CreateXor(A, C), B.getInt32(1));
  B.CreateCondBr(B.CreateICmpNE(Sel, B.getInt32(0)), Then, Else);

  B.SetInsertPoint(Then);
  auto *RT = B.CreateAdd(Base, A);
  B.CreateBr(Merge);
  B.SetInsertPoint(Else);
  auto *RE = B.CreateXor(Base, C);
  B.CreateBr(Merge);

  B.SetInsertPoint(Merge);
  auto *Res = B.CreatePHI(I32, 2, "res");
  Res->addIncoming(RT, Then);
  Res->addIncoming(RE, Else);
  B.CreateRet(Res);
  assert(!llvm::verifyModule(*M, &llvm::errs()));
  return M;
}

// 256-bit (<8 x i32>) vector byte-swap + bit-reverse (llvm.bswap /
// llvm.bitreverse) -- the 256-bit-wide companion of vbswap (<8 x i16>/<4 x
// i32>/ <2 x i64>) and VecBitRev (<16 x i8>/<8 x i16>/<4 x i32>), neither of
// which reached 256-bit.  No target has a 256-bit integer register so each
// splits into 2x128 halves; per <4 x i32> half AArch64 NEON uses rev32.16b
// (bswap) / rbit.16b+rev32 (bitreverse), x86 SSE2 has no vector
// bswap/bitreverse so each expands to shift/mask SWAR.  All integer, zero
// libcall.  No obfuscation pass touches bswap/bitreverse, so orig/obfuscated
// lower byte-identically -- any Unicorn mismatch is a real backend /
// fork-Unicorn bug.
std::unique_ptr<llvm::Module> buildVecWide256RevIR(llvm::LLVMContext &Ctx,
                                                   const char *Triple) {
  auto M = std::make_unique<llvm::Module>("substtest", Ctx);
  M->setTargetTriple(llvm::Triple(Triple));
  auto *I32 = llvm::Type::getInt32Ty(Ctx);
  auto *V8 = llvm::FixedVectorType::get(I32, 8);
  auto *FTy = llvm::FunctionType::get(I32, {I32, I32}, false);
  auto *F = llvm::Function::Create(FTy, llvm::Function::ExternalLinkage,
                                   "vw256rev", M.get());
  auto *Entry = llvm::BasicBlock::Create(Ctx, "entry", F);
  auto *Then = llvm::BasicBlock::Create(Ctx, "then", F);
  auto *Else = llvm::BasicBlock::Create(Ctx, "else", F);
  auto *Merge = llvm::BasicBlock::Create(Ctx, "merge", F);
  auto *A = F->getArg(0), *C = F->getArg(1);

  llvm::IRBuilder<> B(Entry);
  llvm::Value *VW = llvm::UndefValue::get(V8);
  for (unsigned i = 0; i < 8; ++i)
    VW = B.CreateInsertElement(
        VW,
        B.CreateAdd(B.CreateXor(A, B.CreateShl(C, B.getInt32(i & 31))),
                    B.getInt32(0x01020304 + i * 0x11111111)),
        B.getInt32(i));
  auto *Sw = B.CreateIntrinsic(llvm::Intrinsic::bswap, {V8}, {VW});
  auto *Br = B.CreateIntrinsic(llvm::Intrinsic::bitreverse, {V8}, {VW});
  llvm::Value *Base = B.getInt32(0);
  for (unsigned i = 0; i < 8; ++i) {
    Base = B.CreateXor(Base, B.CreateExtractElement(Sw, B.getInt32(i)));
    Base = B.CreateAdd(Base, B.CreateExtractElement(Br, B.getInt32(i)));
  }
  auto *T = B.CreateXor(B.CreateXor(B.CreateAdd(A, C), B.CreateSub(A, C)),
                        B.getInt32(0x5A5A));
  auto *U = B.CreateOr(B.CreateAnd(A, C), B.CreateAdd(T, B.getInt32(12345)));
  Base = B.CreateXor(B.CreateXor(Base, T), U);
  auto *Sel = B.CreateAnd(B.CreateXor(A, C), B.getInt32(1));
  B.CreateCondBr(B.CreateICmpNE(Sel, B.getInt32(0)), Then, Else);
  B.SetInsertPoint(Then);
  auto *RT = B.CreateAdd(Base, A);
  B.CreateBr(Merge);
  B.SetInsertPoint(Else);
  auto *RE = B.CreateXor(Base, C);
  B.CreateBr(Merge);
  B.SetInsertPoint(Merge);
  auto *Res = B.CreatePHI(I32, 2, "res");
  Res->addIncoming(RT, Then);
  Res->addIncoming(RE, Else);
  B.CreateRet(Res);
  assert(!llvm::verifyModule(*M, &llvm::errs()));
  return M;
}

// Hardware CRC32C (Castagnoli) accumulate — the first patch-full coverage of the
// CRC checksum instruction family.  x86/x86-64 emit SSE4.2 `crc32` (via
// llvm.x86.sse42.crc32.*; the "sse42.crc32" substring makes
// detectTargetFeaturesX86 add +sse4.2,+crc32); AArch64 emits `crc32c{b,h,w,x}`
// (llvm.aarch64.crc32c*, +crc); ARM32 emits ARMv8 AArch32 `crc32c{b,h,w}`
// (llvm.arm.crc32c*, +v8,+fp-armv8,+crc).  crc32 is not a plain ALU op: it
// threads a running 32-bit accumulator through byte/half/word (and, on 64-bit
// ISAs, qword) updates — a distinct per-ISA hardware path no other shape reaches,
// and one every requested ISA implements natively.  checkEquiv compares the
// original against the obfuscated copy *within* each cell (never across ISAs), so
// the differing CRC32C results across ISAs are irrelevant; each cell only needs
// its own crc instructions to decode and the obfuscation to preserve them.  The
// accumulator folds into the usual data-dependent diamond + PHI with non-folding
// constants (0x5C5C/33203) so the subst / const-enc / opaque / flatten / bogus /
// indirect passes have integer arithmetic (and a branch) to transform, while the
// crc intrinsics themselves are untouched — the original and obfuscated copies
// stay byte-identical over the crc sub-graph, an undecoded crc32/crc32c faults
// the Unicorn baseline (UC_ERR_INSN_INVALID), and any value divergence is a
// genuine backend / fork-Unicorn bug.
std::unique_ptr<llvm::Module> buildScalarCrc32IR(llvm::LLVMContext &Ctx,
                                                 const char *Triple) {
  auto M = std::make_unique<llvm::Module>("substtest", Ctx);
  M->setTargetTriple(llvm::Triple(Triple));
  llvm::Triple TT(Triple);
  llvm::Triple::ArchType ArchK = TT.getArch();
  bool IsX86 = ArchK == llvm::Triple::x86 || ArchK == llvm::Triple::x86_64;
  bool IsA64 = ArchK == llvm::Triple::aarch64;
  bool Is64 = TT.isArch64Bit();

  auto *I8 = llvm::Type::getInt8Ty(Ctx);
  auto *I16 = llvm::Type::getInt16Ty(Ctx);
  auto *I32 = llvm::Type::getInt32Ty(Ctx);
  auto *I64 = llvm::Type::getInt64Ty(Ctx);

  auto *FTy = llvm::FunctionType::get(I32, {I32, I32}, false);
  auto *F = llvm::Function::Create(FTy, llvm::Function::ExternalLinkage,
                                   "crc32acc", M.get());
  auto *Entry = llvm::BasicBlock::Create(Ctx, "entry", F);
  auto *Then = llvm::BasicBlock::Create(Ctx, "then", F);
  auto *Else = llvm::BasicBlock::Create(Ctx, "else", F);
  auto *Merge = llvm::BasicBlock::Create(Ctx, "merge", F);
  auto *A = F->getArg(0), *C = F->getArg(1);

  llvm::IRBuilder<> B(Entry);

  // Per-ISA hardware CRC32C update helpers over the running accumulator.
  auto crcByte = [&](llvm::Value *Crc, llvm::Value *D) -> llvm::Value * {
    if (IsX86)
      return B.CreateIntrinsic(llvm::Intrinsic::x86_sse42_crc32_32_8, {},
                               {Crc, B.CreateTrunc(D, I8)});
    return B.CreateIntrinsic(
        IsA64 ? static_cast<llvm::Intrinsic::ID>(llvm::Intrinsic::aarch64_crc32cb)
              : static_cast<llvm::Intrinsic::ID>(llvm::Intrinsic::arm_crc32cb),
        {}, {Crc, D});
  };
  auto crcHalf = [&](llvm::Value *Crc, llvm::Value *D) -> llvm::Value * {
    if (IsX86)
      return B.CreateIntrinsic(llvm::Intrinsic::x86_sse42_crc32_32_16, {},
                               {Crc, B.CreateTrunc(D, I16)});
    return B.CreateIntrinsic(
        IsA64 ? static_cast<llvm::Intrinsic::ID>(llvm::Intrinsic::aarch64_crc32ch)
              : static_cast<llvm::Intrinsic::ID>(llvm::Intrinsic::arm_crc32ch),
        {}, {Crc, D});
  };
  auto crcWord = [&](llvm::Value *Crc, llvm::Value *D) -> llvm::Value * {
    if (IsX86)
      return B.CreateIntrinsic(llvm::Intrinsic::x86_sse42_crc32_32_32, {},
                               {Crc, D});
    return B.CreateIntrinsic(
        IsA64 ? static_cast<llvm::Intrinsic::ID>(llvm::Intrinsic::aarch64_crc32cw)
              : static_cast<llvm::Intrinsic::ID>(llvm::Intrinsic::arm_crc32cw),
        {}, {Crc, D});
  };

  // Seed from arg0, thread through byte -> half -> word updates whose data is
  // derived from both args so nothing folds to a constant.
  llvm::Value *Crc = A;
  Crc = crcByte(Crc, B.CreateXor(A, C));
  Crc = crcHalf(Crc, B.CreateAdd(A, C));
  Crc = crcWord(Crc, B.CreateSub(A, C));

  // 64-bit ISAs also exercise the qword update (x86 `crc32 r64, r/m64` /
  // AArch64 `crc32cx`); the i64 result folds back into the 32-bit accumulator.
  if (Is64) {
    auto *D64 = B.CreateOr(B.CreateZExt(A, I64),
                           B.CreateShl(B.CreateZExt(C, I64), B.getInt64(32)));
    if (IsX86) {
      auto *Q = B.CreateIntrinsic(llvm::Intrinsic::x86_sse42_crc32_64_64, {},
                                  {B.CreateZExt(Crc, I64), D64});
      Crc = B.CreateTrunc(Q, I32);
    } else if (IsA64) {
      Crc = B.CreateIntrinsic(llvm::Intrinsic::aarch64_crc32cx, {}, {Crc, D64});
    }
  }

  // Fold the CRC into the usual data-dependent diamond + PHI so the L1 passes
  // have integer arithmetic (and a branch) to transform.
  auto *T = B.CreateXor(B.CreateXor(B.CreateAdd(A, C), B.CreateSub(A, C)),
                        B.getInt32(0x5C5C));
  auto *U = B.CreateOr(B.CreateAnd(Crc, C), B.CreateAdd(T, B.getInt32(33203)));
  auto *BaseV = B.CreateAdd(Crc, U);
  B.CreateCondBr(B.CreateICmpNE(B.CreateAnd(B.CreateXor(A, C), B.getInt32(1)),
                                B.getInt32(0)),
                 Then, Else);

  B.SetInsertPoint(Then);
  auto *R1 = B.CreateAdd(BaseV, A);
  B.CreateBr(Merge);

  B.SetInsertPoint(Else);
  auto *R2 = B.CreateXor(BaseV, C);
  B.CreateBr(Merge);

  B.SetInsertPoint(Merge);
  auto *Pc = B.CreatePHI(I32, 2);
  Pc->addIncoming(R1, Then);
  Pc->addIncoming(R2, Else);
  B.CreateRet(Pc);
  assert(!llvm::verifyModule(*M, &llvm::errs()));
  return M;
}

// Hardware carry-less / polynomial multiply (GF(2)[x]) — the first patch-full
// coverage of the polynomial-multiply instruction family, the checksum/crypto
// sibling of CRC32.  x86/x86-64 emit SSE `pclmulqdq` (via llvm.x86.pclmulqdq;
// the "pclmulqdq" substring makes detectTargetFeaturesX86 add +pclmul); AArch64
// emits NEON `pmul v.16b` (llvm.aarch64.neon.pmul) and ARM32 emits NEON
// `vmul.p8 q` (llvm.arm.neon.vmulp) — both base NEON, no crypto extension
// required.  A polynomial multiply is a distinct hardware path from an ordinary
// integer multiply (a carry-less GF(2) product: byte 0x53*0x53 = 0x05 poly vs
// 0x69 integer) that no other shape reaches, and one every requested ISA
// implements natively.  checkEquiv compares the original against the obfuscated
// copy *within* each cell (never across ISAs), so the differing poly products
// across ISAs are irrelevant; each cell only needs its own pclmulqdq/pmul to
// decode and the obfuscation to preserve it.  The reduced product folds into the
// usual data-dependent diamond + PHI with non-folding constants (0x5C5C/33203)
// so the subst / const-enc / opaque / flatten / bogus / indirect passes have
// integer arithmetic (and a branch) to transform, while the poly-multiply
// intrinsic (and its x86 imm-arg) is left untouched — the original and
// obfuscated copies stay byte-identical over the poly sub-graph, an undecoded
// pclmulqdq/pmul faults the Unicorn baseline (UC_ERR_INSN_INVALID), and any
// value divergence is a genuine backend / fork-Unicorn bug.
std::unique_ptr<llvm::Module> buildPolyMulIR(llvm::LLVMContext &Ctx,
                                             const char *Triple) {
  auto M = std::make_unique<llvm::Module>("substtest", Ctx);
  M->setTargetTriple(llvm::Triple(Triple));
  llvm::Triple TT(Triple);
  llvm::Triple::ArchType ArchK = TT.getArch();
  bool IsX86 = ArchK == llvm::Triple::x86 || ArchK == llvm::Triple::x86_64;
  bool IsA64 = ArchK == llvm::Triple::aarch64;

  auto *I8 = llvm::Type::getInt8Ty(Ctx);
  auto *I32 = llvm::Type::getInt32Ty(Ctx);
  auto *I64 = llvm::Type::getInt64Ty(Ctx);

  auto *FTy = llvm::FunctionType::get(I32, {I32, I32}, false);
  auto *F = llvm::Function::Create(FTy, llvm::Function::ExternalLinkage,
                                   "polymul", M.get());
  auto *Entry = llvm::BasicBlock::Create(Ctx, "entry", F);
  auto *Then = llvm::BasicBlock::Create(Ctx, "then", F);
  auto *Else = llvm::BasicBlock::Create(Ctx, "else", F);
  auto *Merge = llvm::BasicBlock::Create(Ctx, "merge", F);
  auto *A = F->getArg(0), *C = F->getArg(1);

  llvm::IRBuilder<> B(Entry);

  // Per-ISA hardware polynomial multiply, reduced to a 32-bit accumulator.
  llvm::Value *Pv = nullptr;
  if (IsX86) {
    // 64x64 -> 128 carry-less multiply; imm 0 selects the low 64-bit lanes.
    auto *V2I64 = llvm::FixedVectorType::get(I64, 2);
    llvm::Value *VA = llvm::UndefValue::get(V2I64);
    VA = B.CreateInsertElement(VA, B.CreateZExt(A, I64), B.getInt32(0));
    VA = B.CreateInsertElement(VA, B.CreateZExt(B.CreateAdd(A, C), I64),
                               B.getInt32(1));
    llvm::Value *VB = llvm::UndefValue::get(V2I64);
    VB = B.CreateInsertElement(VB, B.CreateZExt(B.CreateXor(A, C), I64),
                               B.getInt32(0));
    VB = B.CreateInsertElement(VB, B.CreateZExt(B.CreateSub(A, C), I64),
                               B.getInt32(1));
    auto *R = B.CreateIntrinsic(llvm::Intrinsic::x86_pclmulqdq, {},
                                {VA, VB, B.getInt8(0)});
    auto *Lo = B.CreateExtractElement(R, B.getInt32(0));
    auto *Hi = B.CreateExtractElement(R, B.getInt32(1));
    Pv = B.CreateTrunc(B.CreateXor(Lo, B.CreateMul(Hi, B.getInt64(131))), I32);
  } else {
    // Same-width per-byte polynomial multiply over 16 byte lanes.
    const unsigned W = 16;
    auto *V16 = llvm::FixedVectorType::get(I8, W);
    auto *V4I32 = llvm::FixedVectorType::get(I32, 4);
    llvm::SmallVector<llvm::Constant *, 16> IotaElems;
    for (unsigned i = 0; i < W; ++i)
      IotaElems.push_back(llvm::ConstantInt::get(I8, i * 7 + 1));
    auto *Iota = llvm::ConstantVector::get(IotaElems);
    auto *Ab = B.CreateTrunc(A, I8);
    auto *Cb = B.CreateTrunc(C, I8);
    auto *VA = B.CreateAdd(B.CreateVectorSplat(W, Ab), Iota);
    auto *VB = B.CreateXor(B.CreateVectorSplat(W, Cb), Iota);
    auto ID = IsA64 ? static_cast<llvm::Intrinsic::ID>(
                          llvm::Intrinsic::aarch64_neon_pmul)
                    : static_cast<llvm::Intrinsic::ID>(
                          llvm::Intrinsic::arm_neon_vmulp);
    auto *R = B.CreateIntrinsic(ID, {V16}, {VA, VB});
    auto *R4 = B.CreateBitCast(R, V4I32);
    llvm::Value *Acc = B.CreateExtractElement(R4, B.getInt32(0));
    for (unsigned i = 1; i < 4; ++i)
      Acc = B.CreateXor(Acc, B.CreateExtractElement(R4, B.getInt32(i)));
    Pv = Acc;
  }

  // Fold the poly product into the usual data-dependent diamond + PHI so the L1
  // passes have integer arithmetic (and a branch) to transform.
  auto *T = B.CreateXor(B.CreateXor(B.CreateAdd(A, C), B.CreateSub(A, C)),
                        B.getInt32(0x5C5C));
  auto *U = B.CreateOr(B.CreateAnd(Pv, C), B.CreateAdd(T, B.getInt32(33203)));
  auto *BaseV = B.CreateAdd(Pv, U);
  B.CreateCondBr(B.CreateICmpNE(B.CreateAnd(B.CreateXor(A, C), B.getInt32(1)),
                                B.getInt32(0)),
                 Then, Else);

  B.SetInsertPoint(Then);
  auto *R1 = B.CreateAdd(BaseV, A);
  B.CreateBr(Merge);

  B.SetInsertPoint(Else);
  auto *R2 = B.CreateXor(BaseV, C);
  B.CreateBr(Merge);

  B.SetInsertPoint(Merge);
  auto *Pc = B.CreatePHI(I32, 2);
  Pc->addIncoming(R1, Then);
  Pc->addIncoming(R2, Else);
  B.CreateRet(Pc);
  assert(!llvm::verifyModule(*M, &llvm::errs()));
  return M;
}

// Hardware reciprocal / reciprocal-square-root *estimate* on 256-bit vectors —
// the first patch-full coverage of the low-precision FP estimate instruction
// family.  Unlike the correctly-rounded vector fdiv/fsqrt shapes (vfdiv* /
// vdivsqrt256) these are architecturally-defined *approximations* (well under
// full precision): a distinct per-ISA hardware path no other shape reaches, and
// one every requested ISA implements natively.  x86/x86-64 emit AVX
// `vrcpps`/`vrsqrtps ymm` (llvm.x86.avx.rcp.ps.256 / rsqrt.ps.256; the "avx"
// substring makes detectTargetFeaturesX86 add +avx); AArch64 emits NEON
// `frecpe`/`frsqrte` and ARM32 emits NEON `vrecpe.f32`/`vrsqrte.f32`
// (llvm.aarch64.neon.frecpe/frsqrte, llvm.arm.neon.vrecpe/vrsqrte), applied to
// each 128-bit half so the native <4 x float> estimate selects directly (no
// reliance on <8 x float> intrinsic legalization).  The estimate's exact low
// bits differ across ISAs (and from a true reciprocal), but checkEquiv compares
// the original against the obfuscated copy *within* each cell (never across
// ISAs) and neither copy touches the estimate sub-graph, so both emit
// byte-identical estimate instructions and observe identical results; each cell
// only needs its own vrcpps/frecpe to decode and the obfuscation to preserve it.
// Every lane input is forced >= 1.0 so the estimate is finite and positive (no
// NaN/inf/zero) and lands in (0, ~1.01]; scaling by 2^20 keeps every fptosi lane
// within i32 range.  The reduced estimate folds into the usual data-dependent
// diamond + PHI with non-folding constants (0x5C5C/33203) so the subst /
// const-enc / opaque / flatten / bogus / indirect passes have integer
// arithmetic (and a branch) to transform, while the estimate intrinsics
// themselves are left untouched — an undecoded vrcpps/vrsqrtps faults the
// Unicorn baseline (UC_ERR_INSN_INVALID) and any value divergence is a genuine
// backend / fork-Unicorn bug.
std::unique_ptr<llvm::Module> buildVecAvxRcpRsqrt256IR(llvm::LLVMContext &Ctx,
                                                       const char *Triple) {
  auto M = std::make_unique<llvm::Module>("substtest", Ctx);
  M->setTargetTriple(llvm::Triple(Triple));
  llvm::Triple TT(Triple);
  llvm::Triple::ArchType ArchK = TT.getArch();
  bool IsX86 = ArchK == llvm::Triple::x86 || ArchK == llvm::Triple::x86_64;
  bool IsA64 = ArchK == llvm::Triple::aarch64;

  auto *I32 = llvm::Type::getInt32Ty(Ctx);
  auto *Flt = llvm::Type::getFloatTy(Ctx);
  auto *V4f = llvm::FixedVectorType::get(Flt, 4);
  auto *V8f = llvm::FixedVectorType::get(Flt, 8);
  auto *V8i = llvm::FixedVectorType::get(I32, 8);

  auto *FTy = llvm::FunctionType::get(I32, {I32, I32}, false);
  auto *F = llvm::Function::Create(FTy, llvm::Function::ExternalLinkage,
                                   "vrcprsqrt256", M.get());
  F->addFnAttr("min-legal-vector-width", "256");
  auto *Entry = llvm::BasicBlock::Create(Ctx, "entry", F);
  auto *Then = llvm::BasicBlock::Create(Ctx, "then", F);
  auto *Else = llvm::BasicBlock::Create(Ctx, "else", F);
  auto *Merge = llvm::BasicBlock::Create(Ctx, "merge", F);
  auto *A = F->getArg(0), *C = F->getArg(1);

  llvm::IRBuilder<> B(Entry);

  // Native per-ISA reciprocal / reciprocal-sqrt estimate over a <8 x float>.
  // x86 pins the AVX 256-bit intrinsic (both i386 and x86-64); AArch64/ARM apply
  // the native <4 x float> NEON estimate to each 128-bit half and reassemble.
  auto *Poison = llvm::PoisonValue::get(V8f);
  auto estimate = [&](llvm::Value *X, bool Rsqrt) -> llvm::Value * {
    if (IsX86)
      return B.CreateIntrinsic(Rsqrt ? llvm::Intrinsic::x86_avx_rsqrt_ps_256
                                     : llvm::Intrinsic::x86_avx_rcp_ps_256,
                               {}, {X});
    llvm::Intrinsic::ID IID;
    if (IsA64)
      IID = Rsqrt ? llvm::Intrinsic::aarch64_neon_frsqrte
                  : llvm::Intrinsic::aarch64_neon_frecpe;
    else
      IID = Rsqrt ? llvm::Intrinsic::arm_neon_vrsqrte
                  : llvm::Intrinsic::arm_neon_vrecpe;
    auto *Lo = B.CreateShuffleVector(X, Poison, {0, 1, 2, 3});
    auto *Hi = B.CreateShuffleVector(X, Poison, {4, 5, 6, 7});
    auto *RLo = B.CreateIntrinsic(IID, {V4f}, {Lo});
    auto *RHi = B.CreateIntrinsic(IID, {V4f}, {Hi});
    return B.CreateShuffleVector(RLo, RHi, {0, 1, 2, 3, 4, 5, 6, 7});
  };

  // Two <8 x float> inputs, every lane forced >= 1.0 (positive, nonzero) so the
  // estimate is finite and lands in (0, ~1.01].
  auto *Alo = B.CreateAnd(A, B.getInt32(1023));
  auto *Clo = B.CreateAnd(C, B.getInt32(1023));
  llvm::Value *VA = llvm::UndefValue::get(V8f);
  llvm::Value *VC = llvm::UndefValue::get(V8f);
  for (unsigned I = 0; I < 8; ++I) {
    VA = B.CreateInsertElement(
        VA, B.CreateSIToFP(B.CreateAdd(Alo, B.getInt32(I + 1)), Flt),
        uint64_t(I));
    VC = B.CreateInsertElement(
        VC, B.CreateSIToFP(B.CreateAdd(Clo, B.getInt32(I * 2 + 1)), Flt),
        uint64_t(I));
  }

  // Native reciprocal estimate of VA, reciprocal-sqrt estimate of VC; scale each
  // lane by 2^20 and truncate to i32 (positive, in range).
  auto *Scale = B.CreateVectorSplat(8, llvm::ConstantFP::get(Flt, 1048576.0));
  auto *Ri = B.CreateFPToSI(B.CreateFMul(estimate(VA, false), Scale), V8i);
  auto *Qi = B.CreateFPToSI(B.CreateFMul(estimate(VC, true), Scale), V8i);

  // Reduce both lane vectors to a scalar with distinct per-lane weights.
  llvm::Value *S = B.getInt32(0);
  for (unsigned L = 0; L < 8; ++L) {
    S = B.CreateAdd(S, B.CreateMul(B.CreateExtractElement(Ri, uint64_t(L)),
                                   B.getInt32(L + 1)));
    S = B.CreateAdd(S, B.CreateMul(B.CreateExtractElement(Qi, uint64_t(L)),
                                   B.getInt32(8 - L)));
  }

  // Fold into the usual data-dependent diamond + PHI so the L1 passes have
  // integer arithmetic (and a branch) to transform.
  auto *T = B.CreateXor(B.CreateXor(B.CreateAdd(A, C), B.CreateSub(A, C)),
                        B.getInt32(0x5C5C));
  auto *U = B.CreateOr(B.CreateAnd(S, C), B.CreateAdd(T, B.getInt32(33203)));
  auto *BaseV = B.CreateAdd(S, U);
  B.CreateCondBr(B.CreateICmpNE(B.CreateAnd(B.CreateXor(A, C), B.getInt32(1)),
                                B.getInt32(0)),
                 Then, Else);

  B.SetInsertPoint(Then);
  auto *RT = B.CreateAdd(BaseV, A);
  B.CreateBr(Merge);

  B.SetInsertPoint(Else);
  auto *RE = B.CreateXor(BaseV, C);
  B.CreateBr(Merge);

  B.SetInsertPoint(Merge);
  auto *Pc = B.CreatePHI(I32, 2);
  Pc->addIncoming(RT, Then);
  Pc->addIncoming(RE, Else);
  B.CreateRet(Pc);
  assert(!llvm::verifyModule(*M, &llvm::errs()));
  return M;
}

// One hardware AES block-cipher *encrypt round* on a 128-bit state — the first
// patch-full coverage of the AES cryptographic instruction family, the natural
// sibling to the already-covered CRC checksum (crc32acc) and carry-less/
// polynomial multiply (polymul, pclmulqdq) families.  AES is a distinct per-ISA
// hardware crypto path no other shape reaches, and one every requested ISA
// implements natively: x86/x86-64 emit AES-NI `aesenc`
// (llvm.x86.aesni.aesenc — the "aesni" substring makes detectTargetFeaturesX86
// add +aes; a single instruction that does ShiftRows∘SubBytes∘MixColumns then
// XORs the round key), while AArch64 and ARM32 use the ARMv8 crypto extension's
// split idiom `aese` (AddRoundKey∘ShiftRows∘SubBytes) followed by `aesmc`
// (MixColumns) over <16 x i8> (llvm.aarch64.crypto.aese/aesmc — "aarch64.crypto
// .aes" adds +aes; llvm.arm.neon.aese/aesmc — "arm.neon.aes" adds
// +v8,+fp-armv8,+aes).  The round result differs across ISAs (x86 fuses
// MixColumns into aesenc, ARM splits it; the byte orders differ too), but
// checkEquiv compares the original against the obfuscated copy *within* each cell
// (never across ISAs) and neither copy touches the AES sub-graph, so both emit
// byte-identical AES instructions and observe identical results; each cell only
// needs its own aesenc/aese+aesmc to decode and the obfuscation to preserve it.
// fork-Unicorn already decodes all three: the default x86 CPU model is Haswell
// (cpu.c: FEAT_1_ECX has CPUID_EXT_AES), so the AESNI_OP decode gate
// (cpuid_ext_features & CPUID_EXT_AES) passes for both i386 and x86-64; AArch64/
// ARM32 crypto decode on UC_CPU_ARM64_MAX / UC_CPU_ARM_MAX (already exercised by
// AArch64_CryptoRTTests / ARM32_CryptoRTTests).  Both the 128-bit state and the
// round key are derived from the two runtime args (each lane mixes both args;
// the key XORs a distinct non-folding constant into each lane) so the backend
// cannot fold the round to a constant.  The 128-bit result is folded down to a
// scalar (xor the two 64-bit lanes, then xor-fold the halves) and merged into
// the usual data-dependent diamond + PHI with non-folding constants (0x5C5C/
// 33203) so the subst / const-enc / opaque / flatten / bogus / indirect passes
// have integer arithmetic (and a branch) to transform, while the AES intrinsics
// themselves are left untouched — an undecoded aesenc/aese faults the Unicorn
// baseline (UC_ERR_INSN_INVALID) and any value divergence is a genuine backend /
// fork-Unicorn bug.
std::unique_ptr<llvm::Module> buildVecAesEnc128IR(llvm::LLVMContext &Ctx,
                                                  const char *Triple) {
  auto M = std::make_unique<llvm::Module>("substtest", Ctx);
  M->setTargetTriple(llvm::Triple(Triple));
  llvm::Triple TT(Triple);
  llvm::Triple::ArchType ArchK = TT.getArch();
  bool IsX86 = ArchK == llvm::Triple::x86 || ArchK == llvm::Triple::x86_64;
  bool IsA64 = ArchK == llvm::Triple::aarch64;

  auto *I32 = llvm::Type::getInt32Ty(Ctx);
  auto *I64 = llvm::Type::getInt64Ty(Ctx);
  auto *I8 = llvm::Type::getInt8Ty(Ctx);
  auto *V2i64 = llvm::FixedVectorType::get(I64, 2);
  auto *V16i8 = llvm::FixedVectorType::get(I8, 16);

  auto *FTy = llvm::FunctionType::get(I32, {I32, I32}, false);
  auto *F = llvm::Function::Create(FTy, llvm::Function::ExternalLinkage,
                                   "vaesenc128", M.get());
  F->addFnAttr("min-legal-vector-width", "128");
  auto *Entry = llvm::BasicBlock::Create(Ctx, "entry", F);
  auto *Then = llvm::BasicBlock::Create(Ctx, "then", F);
  auto *Else = llvm::BasicBlock::Create(Ctx, "else", F);
  auto *Merge = llvm::BasicBlock::Create(Ctx, "merge", F);
  auto *A = F->getArg(0), *C = F->getArg(1);

  llvm::IRBuilder<> B(Entry);

  // Build a 128-bit state and round key, both derived from the two args (each
  // lane mixes both, so no lane is a foldable constant), then run one native AES
  // encrypt round: x86 pins the fused AES-NI aesenc, AArch64/ARM apply the split
  // aese (AddRoundKey∘ShiftRows∘SubBytes) + aesmc (MixColumns) idiom.
  auto *A64 = B.CreateZExt(A, I64);
  auto *C64 = B.CreateZExt(C, I64);
  auto *Lane0 = B.CreateOr(A64, B.CreateShl(C64, B.getInt64(32)));
  auto *Lane1 = B.CreateOr(C64, B.CreateShl(A64, B.getInt64(32)));
  llvm::Value *St = llvm::UndefValue::get(V2i64);
  St = B.CreateInsertElement(St, Lane0, uint64_t(0));
  St = B.CreateInsertElement(St, Lane1, uint64_t(1));
  llvm::Value *Key = llvm::UndefValue::get(V2i64);
  Key = B.CreateInsertElement(
      Key, B.CreateXor(Lane0, B.getInt64(0x9E3779B97F4A7C15ULL)), uint64_t(0));
  Key = B.CreateInsertElement(
      Key, B.CreateXor(Lane1, B.getInt64(0xC2B2AE3D27D4EB4FULL)), uint64_t(1));

  auto aesRound = [&](llvm::Value *Stv, llvm::Value *Keyv) -> llvm::Value * {
    if (IsX86)
      return B.CreateIntrinsic(llvm::Intrinsic::x86_aesni_aesenc, {},
                               {Stv, Keyv});
    auto *D = B.CreateBitCast(Stv, V16i8);
    auto *K = B.CreateBitCast(Keyv, V16i8);
    // Keep AArch64 and ARM intrinsic IDs out of a single ?: — they are distinct
    // enum types and mixing them in one conditional is a deprecated conversion.
    llvm::Intrinsic::ID EseID, McID;
    if (IsA64) {
      EseID = llvm::Intrinsic::aarch64_crypto_aese;
      McID = llvm::Intrinsic::aarch64_crypto_aesmc;
    } else {
      EseID = llvm::Intrinsic::arm_neon_aese;
      McID = llvm::Intrinsic::arm_neon_aesmc;
    }
    auto *E = B.CreateIntrinsic(EseID, {}, {D, K});
    // aesmc takes a single operand; use the (ID, Args) overload — the empty
    // `{}` type list of the 3-arg form is ambiguous against ArrayRef<Value*>.
    auto *Mc = B.CreateIntrinsic(McID, {E});
    return B.CreateBitCast(Mc, V2i64);
  };

  // Reduce the 128-bit round result to a scalar: xor the two 64-bit lanes, then
  // xor-fold the halves into i32.
  auto *R = aesRound(St, Key);
  auto *Mix = B.CreateXor(B.CreateExtractElement(R, uint64_t(0)),
                          B.CreateExtractElement(R, uint64_t(1)));
  auto *S = B.CreateTrunc(B.CreateXor(Mix, B.CreateLShr(Mix, B.getInt64(32))),
                          I32);

  // Fold into the usual data-dependent diamond + PHI so the L1 passes have
  // integer arithmetic (and a branch) to transform.
  auto *T = B.CreateXor(B.CreateXor(B.CreateAdd(A, C), B.CreateSub(A, C)),
                        B.getInt32(0x5C5C));
  auto *U = B.CreateOr(B.CreateAnd(S, C), B.CreateAdd(T, B.getInt32(33203)));
  auto *BaseV = B.CreateAdd(S, U);
  B.CreateCondBr(B.CreateICmpNE(B.CreateAnd(B.CreateXor(A, C), B.getInt32(1)),
                                B.getInt32(0)),
                 Then, Else);

  B.SetInsertPoint(Then);
  auto *RT = B.CreateAdd(BaseV, A);
  B.CreateBr(Merge);

  B.SetInsertPoint(Else);
  auto *RE = B.CreateXor(BaseV, C);
  B.CreateBr(Merge);

  B.SetInsertPoint(Merge);
  auto *Pc = B.CreatePHI(I32, 2);
  Pc->addIncoming(RT, Then);
  Pc->addIncoming(RE, Else);
  B.CreateRet(Pc);
  assert(!llvm::verifyModule(*M, &llvm::errs()));
  return M;
}

// One hardware AES block-cipher *decrypt round* on a 128-bit state — the direct
// sibling of the just-added encrypt round (vaesenc128) that completes the AES
// cryptographic instruction family (crc32acc / polymul / aesenc → aesdec).  The
// decrypt round is a *distinct hardware instruction* from encrypt — a separate
// per-ISA opcode with its own fork-Unicorn decode arm and its own backend
// intrinsic lowering, not a re-run of the aesenc path: x86/x86-64 emit AES-NI
// `aesdec` (llvm.x86.aesni.aesdec, opcode 66 0F38 DE — distinct from aesenc's
// DC; the "aesni" substring makes detectTargetFeaturesX86 add +aes; a single
// instruction that does InvShiftRows∘InvSubBytes∘InvMixColumns then XORs the
// round key), while AArch64 and ARM32 use the ARMv8 crypto extension's split
// decrypt idiom `aesd` (AddRoundKey∘InvShiftRows∘InvSubBytes) followed by
// `aesimc` (InvMixColumns) over <16 x i8> (llvm.aarch64.crypto.aesd/aesimc —
// "aarch64.crypto.aes" adds +aes; llvm.arm.neon.aesd/aesimc — "arm.neon.aes"
// adds +v8,+fp-armv8,+aes).  The round result differs across ISAs (x86 fuses
// InvMixColumns into aesdec, ARM splits it; the byte orders differ too), but
// checkEquiv compares the original against the obfuscated copy *within* each cell
// (never across ISAs) and neither copy touches the AES sub-graph, so both emit
// byte-identical AES instructions and observe identical results; each cell only
// needs its own aesdec/aesd+aesimc to decode and the obfuscation to preserve it.
// fork-Unicorn already decodes all three: the default x86 CPU model is Haswell
// (cpu.c: FEAT_1_ECX has CPUID_EXT_AES), so the AESNI_OP decode gate
// (cpuid_ext_features & CPUID_EXT_AES) passes the aesdec (DE) arm for both i386
// and x86-64 exactly as it already does for aesenc (DC); AArch64/ARM32 crypto
// decode on UC_CPU_ARM64_MAX / UC_CPU_ARM_MAX (already exercised by
// AArch64_CryptoRTTests / ARM32_CryptoRTTests).  Both the 128-bit state and the
// round key are derived from the two runtime args (each lane mixes both args;
// the key XORs a distinct non-folding constant into each lane) so the backend
// cannot fold the round to a constant.  The 128-bit result is folded down to a
// scalar (xor the two 64-bit lanes, then xor-fold the halves) and merged into
// the usual data-dependent diamond + PHI with non-folding constants (0x5C5C/
// 33203) so the subst / const-enc / opaque / flatten / bogus / indirect passes
// have integer arithmetic (and a branch) to transform, while the AES intrinsics
// themselves are left untouched — an undecoded aesdec/aesd faults the Unicorn
// baseline (UC_ERR_INSN_INVALID) and any value divergence is a genuine backend /
// fork-Unicorn bug.
std::unique_ptr<llvm::Module> buildVecAesDec128IR(llvm::LLVMContext &Ctx,
                                                  const char *Triple) {
  auto M = std::make_unique<llvm::Module>("substtest", Ctx);
  M->setTargetTriple(llvm::Triple(Triple));
  llvm::Triple TT(Triple);
  llvm::Triple::ArchType ArchK = TT.getArch();
  bool IsX86 = ArchK == llvm::Triple::x86 || ArchK == llvm::Triple::x86_64;
  bool IsA64 = ArchK == llvm::Triple::aarch64;

  auto *I32 = llvm::Type::getInt32Ty(Ctx);
  auto *I64 = llvm::Type::getInt64Ty(Ctx);
  auto *I8 = llvm::Type::getInt8Ty(Ctx);
  auto *V2i64 = llvm::FixedVectorType::get(I64, 2);
  auto *V16i8 = llvm::FixedVectorType::get(I8, 16);

  auto *FTy = llvm::FunctionType::get(I32, {I32, I32}, false);
  auto *F = llvm::Function::Create(FTy, llvm::Function::ExternalLinkage,
                                   "vaesdec128", M.get());
  F->addFnAttr("min-legal-vector-width", "128");
  auto *Entry = llvm::BasicBlock::Create(Ctx, "entry", F);
  auto *Then = llvm::BasicBlock::Create(Ctx, "then", F);
  auto *Else = llvm::BasicBlock::Create(Ctx, "else", F);
  auto *Merge = llvm::BasicBlock::Create(Ctx, "merge", F);
  auto *A = F->getArg(0), *C = F->getArg(1);

  llvm::IRBuilder<> B(Entry);

  // Build a 128-bit state and round key, both derived from the two args (each
  // lane mixes both, so no lane is a foldable constant), then run one native AES
  // decrypt round: x86 pins the fused AES-NI aesdec, AArch64/ARM apply the split
  // aesd (AddRoundKey∘InvShiftRows∘InvSubBytes) + aesimc (InvMixColumns) idiom.
  auto *A64 = B.CreateZExt(A, I64);
  auto *C64 = B.CreateZExt(C, I64);
  auto *Lane0 = B.CreateOr(A64, B.CreateShl(C64, B.getInt64(32)));
  auto *Lane1 = B.CreateOr(C64, B.CreateShl(A64, B.getInt64(32)));
  llvm::Value *St = llvm::UndefValue::get(V2i64);
  St = B.CreateInsertElement(St, Lane0, uint64_t(0));
  St = B.CreateInsertElement(St, Lane1, uint64_t(1));
  llvm::Value *Key = llvm::UndefValue::get(V2i64);
  Key = B.CreateInsertElement(
      Key, B.CreateXor(Lane0, B.getInt64(0x9E3779B97F4A7C15ULL)), uint64_t(0));
  Key = B.CreateInsertElement(
      Key, B.CreateXor(Lane1, B.getInt64(0xC2B2AE3D27D4EB4FULL)), uint64_t(1));

  auto aesRound = [&](llvm::Value *Stv, llvm::Value *Keyv) -> llvm::Value * {
    if (IsX86)
      return B.CreateIntrinsic(llvm::Intrinsic::x86_aesni_aesdec, {},
                               {Stv, Keyv});
    auto *D = B.CreateBitCast(Stv, V16i8);
    auto *K = B.CreateBitCast(Keyv, V16i8);
    // Keep AArch64 and ARM intrinsic IDs out of a single ?: — they are distinct
    // enum types and mixing them in one conditional is a deprecated conversion.
    llvm::Intrinsic::ID EsdID, ImcID;
    if (IsA64) {
      EsdID = llvm::Intrinsic::aarch64_crypto_aesd;
      ImcID = llvm::Intrinsic::aarch64_crypto_aesimc;
    } else {
      EsdID = llvm::Intrinsic::arm_neon_aesd;
      ImcID = llvm::Intrinsic::arm_neon_aesimc;
    }
    auto *E = B.CreateIntrinsic(EsdID, {}, {D, K});
    // aesimc takes a single operand; use the (ID, Args) overload — the empty
    // `{}` type list of the 3-arg form is ambiguous against ArrayRef<Value*>.
    auto *Imc = B.CreateIntrinsic(ImcID, {E});
    return B.CreateBitCast(Imc, V2i64);
  };

  // Reduce the 128-bit round result to a scalar: xor the two 64-bit lanes, then
  // xor-fold the halves into i32.
  auto *R = aesRound(St, Key);
  auto *Mix = B.CreateXor(B.CreateExtractElement(R, uint64_t(0)),
                          B.CreateExtractElement(R, uint64_t(1)));
  auto *S = B.CreateTrunc(B.CreateXor(Mix, B.CreateLShr(Mix, B.getInt64(32))),
                          I32);

  // Fold into the usual data-dependent diamond + PHI so the L1 passes have
  // integer arithmetic (and a branch) to transform.
  auto *T = B.CreateXor(B.CreateXor(B.CreateAdd(A, C), B.CreateSub(A, C)),
                        B.getInt32(0x5C5C));
  auto *U = B.CreateOr(B.CreateAnd(S, C), B.CreateAdd(T, B.getInt32(33203)));
  auto *BaseV = B.CreateAdd(S, U);
  B.CreateCondBr(B.CreateICmpNE(B.CreateAnd(B.CreateXor(A, C), B.getInt32(1)),
                                B.getInt32(0)),
                 Then, Else);

  B.SetInsertPoint(Then);
  auto *RT = B.CreateAdd(BaseV, A);
  B.CreateBr(Merge);

  B.SetInsertPoint(Else);
  auto *RE = B.CreateXor(BaseV, C);
  B.CreateBr(Merge);

  B.SetInsertPoint(Merge);
  auto *Pc = B.CreatePHI(I32, 2);
  Pc->addIncoming(RT, Then);
  Pc->addIncoming(RE, Else);
  B.CreateRet(Pc);
  assert(!llvm::verifyModule(*M, &llvm::errs()));
  return M;
}

// One standalone AES *InvMixColumns* (AESIMC) over a 128-bit state — the first
// patch-full coverage of the standalone AESIMC instruction, completing the
// AES-NI family beyond the encrypt/decrypt rounds (vaesenc128 / vaesdec128).
// AESIMC is a *distinct* hardware opcode from the round instructions: x86/x86-64
// emit the standalone AES-NI `aesimc` (llvm.x86.aesni.aesimc, 66 0F38 DB — the
// "aesni" substring makes detectTargetFeaturesX86 add +aes; a single unary
// instruction applying the AES InvMixColumns transform, with no round key),
// distinct from aesenc's DC / aesdec's DE which fuse (Inv)MixColumns into the
// round.  AArch64 and ARM32 apply the native single-operand `aesimc`
// (llvm.aarch64.crypto.aesimc — "aarch64.crypto.aes" adds +aes; llvm.arm.neon
// .aesimc — "arm.neon.aes" adds +v8,+fp-armv8,+aes).  The transform result
// differs across ISAs (byte orders differ), but checkEquiv compares the original
// against the obfuscated copy *within* each cell (never across ISAs) and neither
// copy touches the AES sub-graph, so both emit byte-identical AESIMC and observe
// identical results; each cell only needs its own aesimc to decode and the
// obfuscation to preserve it.  fork-Unicorn already decodes it: the default x86
// CPU model is Haswell (cpu.c: FEAT_1_ECX has CPUID_EXT_AES), so the AESNI_OP
// decode gate ([0xdb] = AESNI_OP(aesimc)) passes for both i386 and x86-64;
// AArch64/ARM32 crypto decode on UC_CPU_ARM64_MAX / UC_CPU_ARM_MAX.  The 128-bit
// state is derived from the two runtime args (each lane mixes both, xored with a
// distinct non-folding constant per lane) so the backend cannot fold the
// transform to a constant.  The 128-bit result is folded to a scalar (xor the
// two 64-bit lanes, then xor-fold the halves) and merged into the usual
// data-dependent diamond + PHI with non-folding constants (0x5C5C / 33203) so
// the subst / const-enc / opaque / flatten / bogus / indirect passes have
// integer arithmetic (and a branch) to transform, while the AESIMC intrinsic
// itself is left untouched — an undecoded aesimc faults the Unicorn baseline
// (UC_ERR_INSN_INVALID) and any value divergence is a genuine backend /
// fork-Unicorn bug.
std::unique_ptr<llvm::Module> buildVecAesImc128IR(llvm::LLVMContext &Ctx,
                                                  const char *Triple) {
  auto M = std::make_unique<llvm::Module>("substtest", Ctx);
  M->setTargetTriple(llvm::Triple(Triple));
  llvm::Triple TT(Triple);
  llvm::Triple::ArchType ArchK = TT.getArch();
  bool IsX86 = ArchK == llvm::Triple::x86 || ArchK == llvm::Triple::x86_64;
  bool IsA64 = ArchK == llvm::Triple::aarch64;

  auto *I32 = llvm::Type::getInt32Ty(Ctx);
  auto *I64 = llvm::Type::getInt64Ty(Ctx);
  auto *I8 = llvm::Type::getInt8Ty(Ctx);
  auto *V2i64 = llvm::FixedVectorType::get(I64, 2);
  auto *V16i8 = llvm::FixedVectorType::get(I8, 16);

  auto *FTy = llvm::FunctionType::get(I32, {I32, I32}, false);
  auto *F = llvm::Function::Create(FTy, llvm::Function::ExternalLinkage,
                                   "vaesimc128", M.get());
  F->addFnAttr("min-legal-vector-width", "128");
  auto *Entry = llvm::BasicBlock::Create(Ctx, "entry", F);
  auto *Then = llvm::BasicBlock::Create(Ctx, "then", F);
  auto *Else = llvm::BasicBlock::Create(Ctx, "else", F);
  auto *Merge = llvm::BasicBlock::Create(Ctx, "merge", F);
  auto *A = F->getArg(0), *C = F->getArg(1);

  llvm::IRBuilder<> B(Entry);

  // Build a 128-bit state derived from the two args (each lane mixes both and
  // xors a distinct non-folding constant, so no lane is a foldable constant),
  // then run one native standalone AES InvMixColumns: x86 pins the AES-NI
  // aesimc, AArch64/ARM apply the native single-operand aesimc.
  auto *A64 = B.CreateZExt(A, I64);
  auto *C64 = B.CreateZExt(C, I64);
  auto *Lane0 = B.CreateXor(B.CreateOr(A64, B.CreateShl(C64, B.getInt64(32))),
                            B.getInt64(0x9E3779B97F4A7C15ULL));
  auto *Lane1 = B.CreateXor(B.CreateOr(C64, B.CreateShl(A64, B.getInt64(32))),
                            B.getInt64(0xC2B2AE3D27D4EB4FULL));
  llvm::Value *St = llvm::UndefValue::get(V2i64);
  St = B.CreateInsertElement(St, Lane0, uint64_t(0));
  St = B.CreateInsertElement(St, Lane1, uint64_t(1));

  auto aesImc = [&](llvm::Value *Stv) -> llvm::Value * {
    if (IsX86)
      return B.CreateIntrinsic(llvm::Intrinsic::x86_aesni_aesimc, {}, {Stv});
    auto *D = B.CreateBitCast(Stv, V16i8);
    // Keep the AArch64 and ARM intrinsic IDs out of a single ?: — they are
    // distinct enum values and mixing them in one conditional is a deprecated
    // conversion.
    llvm::Intrinsic::ID ImcID;
    if (IsA64)
      ImcID = llvm::Intrinsic::aarch64_crypto_aesimc;
    else
      ImcID = llvm::Intrinsic::arm_neon_aesimc;
    // aesimc takes a single operand; use the (ID, Args) overload — the empty
    // `{}` type list of the 3-arg form is ambiguous against ArrayRef<Value*>.
    auto *Imc = B.CreateIntrinsic(ImcID, {D});
    return B.CreateBitCast(Imc, V2i64);
  };

  // Reduce the 128-bit result to a scalar: xor the two 64-bit lanes, then
  // xor-fold the halves into i32.
  auto *R = aesImc(St);
  auto *Mix = B.CreateXor(B.CreateExtractElement(R, uint64_t(0)),
                          B.CreateExtractElement(R, uint64_t(1)));
  auto *S = B.CreateTrunc(B.CreateXor(Mix, B.CreateLShr(Mix, B.getInt64(32))),
                          I32);

  // Fold into the usual data-dependent diamond + PHI so the L1 passes have
  // integer arithmetic (and a branch) to transform.
  auto *T = B.CreateXor(B.CreateXor(B.CreateAdd(A, C), B.CreateSub(A, C)),
                        B.getInt32(0x5C5C));
  auto *U = B.CreateOr(B.CreateAnd(S, C), B.CreateAdd(T, B.getInt32(33203)));
  auto *BaseV = B.CreateAdd(S, U);
  B.CreateCondBr(B.CreateICmpNE(B.CreateAnd(B.CreateXor(A, C), B.getInt32(1)),
                                B.getInt32(0)),
                 Then, Else);

  B.SetInsertPoint(Then);
  auto *RT = B.CreateAdd(BaseV, A);
  B.CreateBr(Merge);

  B.SetInsertPoint(Else);
  auto *RE = B.CreateXor(BaseV, C);
  B.CreateBr(Merge);

  B.SetInsertPoint(Merge);
  auto *Pc = B.CreatePHI(I32, 2);
  Pc->addIncoming(RT, Then);
  Pc->addIncoming(RE, Else);
  B.CreateRet(Pc);
  assert(!llvm::verifyModule(*M, &llvm::errs()));
  return M;
}

// One hardware AES *last-round* pair (AESENCLAST + AESDECLAST) on a 128-bit
// state — extends the AES-NI family beyond the full rounds (vaesenc128 /
// vaesdec128) and the standalone InvMixColumns (vaesimc128) to the *last-round*
// variants, which omit (Inv)MixColumns and are distinct hardware opcodes: x86/
// x86-64 emit AES-NI `aesenclast` (llvm.x86.aesni.aesenclast, 66 0F38 DD) and
// `aesdeclast` (llvm.x86.aesni.aesdeclast, 66 0F38 DF) — separate opcodes from
// aesenc's DC / aesdec's DE, never reached before; the "aesni" substring makes
// detectTargetFeaturesX86 add +aes.  AArch64/ARM32 emit the ARMv8 crypto `aese`
// / `aesd` (llvm.aarch64.crypto.aese/aesd — "aarch64.crypto.aes" adds +aes;
// llvm.arm.neon.aese/aesd — "arm.neon.aes" adds +v8,+fp-armv8,+aes) as the
// last-round equivalents (AddRoundKey∘ShiftRows∘SubBytes without the following
// aesmc/aesimc).  The result differs across ISAs (x86 XORs the key last, ARM
// first; byte orders differ), but checkEquiv compares the original against the
// obfuscated copy *within* each cell (never across ISAs) and neither copy
// touches the AES sub-graph, so both emit byte-identical AES instructions and
// observe identical results; each cell only needs its own aesenclast/aesdeclast
// (or aese/aesd) to decode and the obfuscation to preserve it.  fork-Unicorn
// already decodes all of them: the default x86 CPU model is Haswell (cpu.c:
// FEAT_1_ECX has CPUID_EXT_AES), so the AESNI_OP decode gate ([0xdd] =
// AESNI_OP(aesenclast), [0xdf] = AESNI_OP(aesdeclast)) passes for both i386 and
// x86-64; AArch64/ARM32 crypto decode on UC_CPU_ARM64_MAX / UC_CPU_ARM_MAX.
// Both the 128-bit state and the two round keys are derived from the two runtime
// args (each lane mixes both args; each key XORs a distinct non-folding constant
// into each lane) so the backend cannot fold the rounds to constants.  The two
// 128-bit results are XORed together, then folded to a scalar (xor the two
// 64-bit lanes, then xor-fold the halves) and merged into the usual
// data-dependent diamond + PHI with non-folding constants (0x5C5C / 33203) so
// the subst / const-enc / opaque / flatten / bogus / indirect passes have
// integer arithmetic (and a branch) to transform, while the AES intrinsics
// themselves are left untouched — an undecoded aesenclast/aesdeclast faults the
// Unicorn baseline (UC_ERR_INSN_INVALID) and any value divergence is a genuine
// backend / fork-Unicorn bug.
std::unique_ptr<llvm::Module> buildVecAesLast128IR(llvm::LLVMContext &Ctx,
                                                   const char *Triple) {
  auto M = std::make_unique<llvm::Module>("substtest", Ctx);
  M->setTargetTriple(llvm::Triple(Triple));
  llvm::Triple TT(Triple);
  llvm::Triple::ArchType ArchK = TT.getArch();
  bool IsX86 = ArchK == llvm::Triple::x86 || ArchK == llvm::Triple::x86_64;
  bool IsA64 = ArchK == llvm::Triple::aarch64;

  auto *I32 = llvm::Type::getInt32Ty(Ctx);
  auto *I64 = llvm::Type::getInt64Ty(Ctx);
  auto *I8 = llvm::Type::getInt8Ty(Ctx);
  auto *V2i64 = llvm::FixedVectorType::get(I64, 2);
  auto *V16i8 = llvm::FixedVectorType::get(I8, 16);

  auto *FTy = llvm::FunctionType::get(I32, {I32, I32}, false);
  auto *F = llvm::Function::Create(FTy, llvm::Function::ExternalLinkage,
                                   "vaeslast128", M.get());
  F->addFnAttr("min-legal-vector-width", "128");
  auto *Entry = llvm::BasicBlock::Create(Ctx, "entry", F);
  auto *Then = llvm::BasicBlock::Create(Ctx, "then", F);
  auto *Else = llvm::BasicBlock::Create(Ctx, "else", F);
  auto *Merge = llvm::BasicBlock::Create(Ctx, "merge", F);
  auto *A = F->getArg(0), *C = F->getArg(1);

  llvm::IRBuilder<> B(Entry);

  // Build a 128-bit state and two round keys, all derived from the two args
  // (each lane mixes both, so no lane is a foldable constant), then run one AES
  // encrypt-last and one AES decrypt-last round: x86 pins the standalone AES-NI
  // aesenclast/aesdeclast, AArch64/ARM apply the native aese/aesd last-round.
  auto *A64 = B.CreateZExt(A, I64);
  auto *C64 = B.CreateZExt(C, I64);
  auto *Lane0 = B.CreateOr(A64, B.CreateShl(C64, B.getInt64(32)));
  auto *Lane1 = B.CreateOr(C64, B.CreateShl(A64, B.getInt64(32)));
  llvm::Value *St = llvm::UndefValue::get(V2i64);
  St = B.CreateInsertElement(St, Lane0, uint64_t(0));
  St = B.CreateInsertElement(St, Lane1, uint64_t(1));
  llvm::Value *Key1 = llvm::UndefValue::get(V2i64);
  Key1 = B.CreateInsertElement(
      Key1, B.CreateXor(Lane0, B.getInt64(0x9E3779B97F4A7C15ULL)), uint64_t(0));
  Key1 = B.CreateInsertElement(
      Key1, B.CreateXor(Lane1, B.getInt64(0xC2B2AE3D27D4EB4FULL)), uint64_t(1));
  llvm::Value *Key2 = llvm::UndefValue::get(V2i64);
  Key2 = B.CreateInsertElement(
      Key2, B.CreateXor(Lane0, B.getInt64(0xD1B54A32D192ED03ULL)), uint64_t(0));
  Key2 = B.CreateInsertElement(
      Key2, B.CreateXor(Lane1, B.getInt64(0xA54FF53A5F1D36F1ULL)), uint64_t(1));

  auto aesLast = [&](llvm::Value *Stv, llvm::Value *K1,
                     llvm::Value *K2) -> llvm::Value * {
    if (IsX86) {
      auto *E = B.CreateIntrinsic(llvm::Intrinsic::x86_aesni_aesenclast, {},
                                  {Stv, K1});
      auto *Dc = B.CreateIntrinsic(llvm::Intrinsic::x86_aesni_aesdeclast, {},
                                   {Stv, K2});
      return B.CreateXor(E, Dc);
    }
    auto *D = B.CreateBitCast(Stv, V16i8);
    auto *k1 = B.CreateBitCast(K1, V16i8);
    auto *k2 = B.CreateBitCast(K2, V16i8);
    // Keep AArch64 and ARM intrinsic IDs out of a single ?: — they are distinct
    // enum values and mixing them in one conditional is a deprecated conversion.
    llvm::Intrinsic::ID EseID, EsdID;
    if (IsA64) {
      EseID = llvm::Intrinsic::aarch64_crypto_aese;
      EsdID = llvm::Intrinsic::aarch64_crypto_aesd;
    } else {
      EseID = llvm::Intrinsic::arm_neon_aese;
      EsdID = llvm::Intrinsic::arm_neon_aesd;
    }
    auto *E = B.CreateIntrinsic(EseID, {}, {D, k1});
    auto *Dc = B.CreateIntrinsic(EsdID, {}, {D, k2});
    auto *X = B.CreateXor(E, Dc);
    return B.CreateBitCast(X, V2i64);
  };

  // Reduce the 128-bit combined result to a scalar: xor the two 64-bit lanes,
  // then xor-fold the halves into i32.
  auto *R = aesLast(St, Key1, Key2);
  auto *Mix = B.CreateXor(B.CreateExtractElement(R, uint64_t(0)),
                          B.CreateExtractElement(R, uint64_t(1)));
  auto *S = B.CreateTrunc(B.CreateXor(Mix, B.CreateLShr(Mix, B.getInt64(32))),
                          I32);

  // Fold into the usual data-dependent diamond + PHI so the L1 passes have
  // integer arithmetic (and a branch) to transform.
  auto *T = B.CreateXor(B.CreateXor(B.CreateAdd(A, C), B.CreateSub(A, C)),
                        B.getInt32(0x5C5C));
  auto *U = B.CreateOr(B.CreateAnd(S, C), B.CreateAdd(T, B.getInt32(33203)));
  auto *BaseV = B.CreateAdd(S, U);
  B.CreateCondBr(B.CreateICmpNE(B.CreateAnd(B.CreateXor(A, C), B.getInt32(1)),
                                B.getInt32(0)),
                 Then, Else);

  B.SetInsertPoint(Then);
  auto *RT = B.CreateAdd(BaseV, A);
  B.CreateBr(Merge);

  B.SetInsertPoint(Else);
  auto *RE = B.CreateXor(BaseV, C);
  B.CreateBr(Merge);

  B.SetInsertPoint(Merge);
  auto *Pc = B.CreatePHI(I32, 2);
  Pc->addIncoming(RT, Then);
  Pc->addIncoming(RE, Else);
  B.CreateRet(Pc);
  assert(!llvm::verifyModule(*M, &llvm::errs()));
  return M;
}

// One AES key-schedule assist (AESKEYGENASSIST) — completes the AES-NI
// instruction family (aesenc/aesdec/aesimc/aesenclast/aesdeclast, plus
// pclmulqdq via polymul) with the *key-generation* helper, a distinct hardware
// opcode no other shape reaches.  x86/x86-64 emit the AES-NI `aeskeygenassist`
// (llvm.x86.aesni.aeskeygenassist, 66 0F3A DF imm8 — the "aesni" substring makes
// detectTargetFeaturesX86 add +aes; it applies SubWord/RotWord and XORs an
// immediate round constant).  Unlike the round instructions it has no ARM crypto
// dual, so — exactly like the SSE4.1-only PHMINPOSUW shape (vphminpos128) — every
