// non-x86 ISA *open-codes* the identical transform in software: SubWord via a
// constant AES S-box table, RotWord via a byte rotate, XOR the same round
// constant.  x86 pins the hardware instruction (fork-Unicorn decodes it:
// translate.c [0xdf] in the 66 0F3A table = AESNI_OP(aeskeygenassist), helper
// present, default Haswell CPU has CPUID_EXT_AES); the open-coded software path
// is a pure deterministic bit computation valid on every ISA.  checkEquiv
// compares the original against the obfuscated copy *within* each cell (never
// across ISAs) and neither copy touches the key-schedule sub-graph, so both
// emit byte-identical code and observe identical results; an undecoded
// aeskeygenassist faults the Unicorn baseline (UC_ERR_INSN_INVALID) and any
// value divergence is a genuine backend / fork-Unicorn bug.  The 128-bit state
// is derived from the two runtime args (each lane mixes both, xored with a
// distinct non-folding constant) so the backend cannot fold the result to a
// constant.  The result is folded to a scalar and merged into the usual
// data-dependent diamond + PHI with non-folding constants (0x5C5C / 33203) so
// the L1 passes have integer arithmetic (and a branch) to transform.
std::unique_ptr<llvm::Module> buildVecAesKeyGen128IR(llvm::LLVMContext &Ctx,
                                                     const char *Triple) {
  auto M = std::make_unique<llvm::Module>("substtest", Ctx);
  M->setTargetTriple(llvm::Triple(Triple));
  llvm::Triple TT(Triple);
  llvm::Triple::ArchType ArchK = TT.getArch();
  bool IsX86 = ArchK == llvm::Triple::x86 || ArchK == llvm::Triple::x86_64;

  auto *I8 = llvm::Type::getInt8Ty(Ctx);
  auto *I32 = llvm::Type::getInt32Ty(Ctx);
  auto *I64 = llvm::Type::getInt64Ty(Ctx);
  auto *V2i64 = llvm::FixedVectorType::get(I64, 2);
  auto *V4i32 = llvm::FixedVectorType::get(I32, 4);

  auto *FTy = llvm::FunctionType::get(I32, {I32, I32}, false);
  auto *F = llvm::Function::Create(FTy, llvm::Function::ExternalLinkage,
                                   "vaeskeygen128", M.get());
  F->addFnAttr("min-legal-vector-width", "128");
  auto *Entry = llvm::BasicBlock::Create(Ctx, "entry", F);
  auto *Then = llvm::BasicBlock::Create(Ctx, "then", F);
  auto *Else = llvm::BasicBlock::Create(Ctx, "else", F);
  auto *Merge = llvm::BasicBlock::Create(Ctx, "merge", F);
  auto *A = F->getArg(0), *C = F->getArg(1);

  llvm::IRBuilder<> B(Entry);

  // 128-bit state, every dword a runtime mix of both args (no foldable lane).
  auto *A64 = B.CreateZExt(A, I64);
  auto *C64 = B.CreateZExt(C, I64);
  auto *Lane0 = B.CreateXor(B.CreateOr(A64, B.CreateShl(C64, B.getInt64(32))),
                            B.getInt64(0x9E3779B97F4A7C15ULL));
  auto *Lane1 = B.CreateXor(B.CreateOr(C64, B.CreateShl(A64, B.getInt64(32))),
                            B.getInt64(0xC2B2AE3D27D4EB4FULL));
  llvm::Value *St = llvm::UndefValue::get(V2i64);
  St = B.CreateInsertElement(St, Lane0, uint64_t(0));
  St = B.CreateInsertElement(St, Lane1, uint64_t(1));

  const uint8_t kRcon = 0x1B;

  auto keyGen = [&](llvm::Value *Stv) -> llvm::Value * {
    if (IsX86)
      return B.CreateIntrinsic(llvm::Intrinsic::x86_aesni_aeskeygenassist, {},
                               {Stv, B.getInt8(kRcon)});
    // Software AESKEYGENASSIST for every non-x86 ISA (no ARM crypto dual):
    // dst0=SubWord(X1); dst1=RotWord(SubWord(X1))^Rcon; dst2=SubWord(X3);
    // dst3=RotWord(SubWord(X3))^Rcon, with SubWord = per-byte S-box.
    static const uint8_t SBoxBytes[256] = {
      0x63, 0x7c, 0x77, 0x7b, 0xf2, 0x6b, 0x6f, 0xc5, 0x30, 0x01, 0x67, 0x2b,
      0xfe, 0xd7, 0xab, 0x76, 0xca, 0x82, 0xc9, 0x7d, 0xfa, 0x59, 0x47, 0xf0,
      0xad, 0xd4, 0xa2, 0xaf, 0x9c, 0xa4, 0x72, 0xc0, 0xb7, 0xfd, 0x93, 0x26,
      0x36, 0x3f, 0xf7, 0xcc, 0x34, 0xa5, 0xe5, 0xf1, 0x71, 0xd8, 0x31, 0x15,
      0x04, 0xc7, 0x23, 0xc3, 0x18, 0x96, 0x05, 0x9a, 0x07, 0x12, 0x80, 0xe2,
      0xeb, 0x27, 0xb2, 0x75, 0x09, 0x83, 0x2c, 0x1a, 0x1b, 0x6e, 0x5a, 0xa0,
      0x52, 0x3b, 0xd6, 0xb3, 0x29, 0xe3, 0x2f, 0x84, 0x53, 0xd1, 0x00, 0xed,
      0x20, 0xfc, 0xb1, 0x5b, 0x6a, 0xcb, 0xbe, 0x39, 0x4a, 0x4c, 0x58, 0xcf,
      0xd0, 0xef, 0xaa, 0xfb, 0x43, 0x4d, 0x33, 0x85, 0x45, 0xf9, 0x02, 0x7f,
      0x50, 0x3c, 0x9f, 0xa8, 0x51, 0xa3, 0x40, 0x8f, 0x92, 0x9d, 0x38, 0xf5,
      0xbc, 0xb6, 0xda, 0x21, 0x10, 0xff, 0xf3, 0xd2, 0xcd, 0x0c, 0x13, 0xec,
      0x5f, 0x97, 0x44, 0x17, 0xc4, 0xa7, 0x7e, 0x3d, 0x64, 0x5d, 0x19, 0x73,
      0x60, 0x81, 0x4f, 0xdc, 0x22, 0x2a, 0x90, 0x88, 0x46, 0xee, 0xb8, 0x14,
      0xde, 0x5e, 0x0b, 0xdb, 0xe0, 0x32, 0x3a, 0x0a, 0x49, 0x06, 0x24, 0x5c,
      0xc2, 0xd3, 0xac, 0x62, 0x91, 0x95, 0xe4, 0x79, 0xe7, 0xc8, 0x37, 0x6d,
      0x8d, 0xd5, 0x4e, 0xa9, 0x6c, 0x56, 0xf4, 0xea, 0x65, 0x7a, 0xae, 0x08,
      0xba, 0x78, 0x25, 0x2e, 0x1c, 0xa6, 0xb4, 0xc6, 0xe8, 0xdd, 0x74, 0x1f,
      0x4b, 0xbd, 0x8b, 0x8a, 0x70, 0x3e, 0xb5, 0x66, 0x48, 0x03, 0xf6, 0x0e,
      0x61, 0x35, 0x57, 0xb9, 0x86, 0xc1, 0x1d, 0x9e, 0xe1, 0xf8, 0x98, 0x11,
      0x69, 0xd9, 0x8e, 0x94, 0x9b, 0x1e, 0x87, 0xe9, 0xce, 0x55, 0x28, 0xdf,
      0x8c, 0xa1, 0x89, 0x0d, 0xbf, 0xe6, 0x42, 0x68, 0x41, 0x99, 0x2d, 0x0f,
      0xb0, 0x54, 0xbb, 0x16
    };
    auto *SBoxTy = llvm::ArrayType::get(I8, 256);
    std::vector<llvm::Constant *> SEnts;
    SEnts.reserve(256);
    for (unsigned k = 0; k < 256; ++k)
      SEnts.push_back(llvm::ConstantInt::get(I8, SBoxBytes[k]));
    auto *SBox = new llvm::GlobalVariable(
        *M, SBoxTy, /*isConstant=*/true, llvm::GlobalValue::InternalLinkage,
        llvm::ConstantArray::get(SBoxTy, SEnts), "nd_aes_sbox");
    auto subWord = [&](llvm::Value *W) -> llvm::Value * {
      llvm::Value *Res = B.getInt32(0);
      for (unsigned k = 0; k < 4; ++k) {
        auto *By = B.CreateZExt(
            B.CreateTrunc(B.CreateLShr(W, B.getInt32(k * 8)), I8), I32);
        auto *Gep = B.CreateGEP(SBoxTy, SBox, {B.getInt32(0), By});
        auto *Sb = B.CreateZExt(B.CreateLoad(I8, Gep), I32);
        Res = B.CreateOr(Res, B.CreateShl(Sb, B.getInt32(k * 8)));
      }
      return Res;
    };
    auto rotWord = [&](llvm::Value *W) -> llvm::Value * {
      return B.CreateOr(B.CreateLShr(W, B.getInt32(8)),
                        B.CreateShl(W, B.getInt32(24)));
    };
    auto *V = B.CreateBitCast(Stv, V4i32);
    auto *X1 = B.CreateExtractElement(V, uint64_t(1));
    auto *X3 = B.CreateExtractElement(V, uint64_t(3));
    auto *S1 = subWord(X1);
    auto *S3 = subWord(X3);
    auto *Rc = B.getInt32(kRcon);
    llvm::Value *R = llvm::UndefValue::get(V4i32);
    R = B.CreateInsertElement(R, S1, uint64_t(0));
    R = B.CreateInsertElement(R, B.CreateXor(rotWord(S1), Rc), uint64_t(1));
    R = B.CreateInsertElement(R, S3, uint64_t(2));
    R = B.CreateInsertElement(R, B.CreateXor(rotWord(S3), Rc), uint64_t(3));
    return B.CreateBitCast(R, V2i64);
  };

  // Reduce the 128-bit result to a scalar: xor the two 64-bit lanes, then
  // xor-fold the halves into i32.
  auto *Rk = keyGen(St);
  auto *Mix = B.CreateXor(B.CreateExtractElement(Rk, uint64_t(0)),
                          B.CreateExtractElement(Rk, uint64_t(1)));
  auto *S = B.CreateTrunc(B.CreateXor(Mix, B.CreateLShr(Mix, B.getInt64(32))),
                          I32);

  // Fold into the usual data-dependent diamond + PHI so the L1 passes have
  // integer arithmetic (and a branch) to transform.
  auto *T = B.CreateXor(B.CreateXor(B.CreateAdd(A, C), B.CreateSub(A, C)),
                        B.getInt32(0x5C5C));
  auto *U = B.CreateOr(B.CreateAnd(S, C), B.CreateAdd(T, B.getInt32(33203)));
  auto *BaseV = B.CreateAdd(S, U);
  B.CreateCondBr(B.CreateICmpNE(B.CreateAnd(B.CreateXor(A, C), B.getInt32(1)),
                                B.getInt32(0)),
                 Then, Else);

  B.SetInsertPoint(Then);
  auto *RT = B.CreateAdd(BaseV, A);
  B.CreateBr(Merge);

  B.SetInsertPoint(Else);
  auto *RE = B.CreateXor(BaseV, C);
  B.CreateBr(Merge);

  B.SetInsertPoint(Merge);
  auto *Pc = B.CreatePHI(I32, 2);
  Pc->addIncoming(RT, Then);
  Pc->addIncoming(RE, Else);
  B.CreateRet(Pc);
  assert(!llvm::verifyModule(*M, &llvm::errs()));
  return M;
}

// One BMI2 parallel bit deposit/extract pair (PDEP + PEXT) on 32-bit GPRs — the
// first patch-full coverage of the BMI2 bit-permute family, a distinct x86
// hardware path no other shape reaches.  x86/x86-64 emit PEXT (F3 0F38 F5) via
// llvm.x86.bmi.pext.32 and PDEP (F2 0F38 F5) via llvm.x86.bmi.pdep.32 — the
// "bmi.pext"/"bmi.pdep" substrings make detectTargetFeaturesX86 add +bmi2.
// PEXT gathers the src bits selected by a mask into the low bits of the result;
// PDEP scatters the low src bits into the mask-selected positions.  Like the
// SSE4.1-only PHMINPOSUW shape (vphminpos128), neither has an ARM dual, so every
// non-x86 ISA open-codes the identical transform in software: a straight-line
// (compile-time-unrolled) scan over the 32 bit positions maintaining a running
// destination/source cursor.  The variable shift amount never reaches 32 (the
// cursor advances only on a set mask bit and the shift uses its value *before*
// the increment, so it tops out at 31), so no shift is poison.  x86 pins the
// hardware instruction; fork-Unicorn already decodes both (translate.c
// gen_helper_pdep/pext, helper_pdep/pext in int_helper.c).  src and both masks
// are derived from the two runtime args (each mixes both, and each mask ORs a
// non-folding constant so it always has set bits) so the backend cannot fold the
// permute to a constant.  checkEquiv compares the original against the obfuscated
// copy within each cell (never across ISAs) and neither copy touches the
// pdep/pext sub-graph, so both emit byte-identical code and observe identical
// results; an undecoded pdep/pext faults the Unicorn baseline
// (UC_ERR_INSN_INVALID) and any value divergence is a genuine backend /
// fork-Unicorn bug.  The two results are combined and folded into the usual
// data-dependent diamond + PHI with non-folding constants (0x5C5C / 33203).
std::unique_ptr<llvm::Module> buildPdepPextIR(llvm::LLVMContext &Ctx,
                                              const char *Triple) {
  auto M = std::make_unique<llvm::Module>("substtest", Ctx);
  M->setTargetTriple(llvm::Triple(Triple));
  llvm::Triple TT(Triple);
  llvm::Triple::ArchType ArchK = TT.getArch();
  bool IsX86 = ArchK == llvm::Triple::x86 || ArchK == llvm::Triple::x86_64;

  auto *I32 = llvm::Type::getInt32Ty(Ctx);
  auto *FTy = llvm::FunctionType::get(I32, {I32, I32}, false);
  auto *F = llvm::Function::Create(FTy, llvm::Function::ExternalLinkage,
                                   "pdeppext", M.get());
  auto *Entry = llvm::BasicBlock::Create(Ctx, "entry", F);
  auto *Then = llvm::BasicBlock::Create(Ctx, "then", F);
  auto *Else = llvm::BasicBlock::Create(Ctx, "else", F);
  auto *Merge = llvm::BasicBlock::Create(Ctx, "merge", F);
  auto *A = F->getArg(0), *C = F->getArg(1);

  llvm::IRBuilder<> B(Entry);

  // Runtime source and two masks (each mixes both args; each mask ORs a
  // non-folding constant so it always has some set bits but stays variable).
  auto *Src = B.CreateXor(B.CreateMul(A, B.getInt32(0x9E3779B9u)), C);
  auto *M1 = B.CreateOr(B.CreateXor(A, B.CreateShl(C, B.getInt32(1))),
                        B.getInt32(0x10305071u));
  auto *M2 = B.CreateOr(B.CreateAdd(C, B.CreateMul(A, B.getInt32(7))),
                        B.getInt32(0x01010133u));

  // Software PEXT: gather src bits selected by mask into the low result bits.
  auto pextSW = [&](llvm::Value *S, llvm::Value *Mk) -> llvm::Value * {
    llvm::Value *Res = B.getInt32(0);
    llvm::Value *K = B.getInt32(0);
    for (unsigned I = 0; I < 32; ++I) {
      auto *Set = B.CreateAnd(B.CreateLShr(Mk, B.getInt32(I)), B.getInt32(1));
      auto *Bit = B.CreateAnd(B.CreateLShr(S, B.getInt32(I)), B.getInt32(1));
      Res = B.CreateOr(Res, B.CreateShl(B.CreateAnd(Bit, Set), K));
      K = B.CreateAdd(K, Set);
    }
    return Res;
  };
  // Software PDEP: scatter the low src bits into the mask-selected positions.
  auto pdepSW = [&](llvm::Value *S, llvm::Value *Mk) -> llvm::Value * {
    llvm::Value *Res = B.getInt32(0);
    llvm::Value *K = B.getInt32(0);
    for (unsigned I = 0; I < 32; ++I) {
      auto *Set = B.CreateAnd(B.CreateLShr(Mk, B.getInt32(I)), B.getInt32(1));
      auto *Bit = B.CreateAnd(B.CreateLShr(S, K), B.getInt32(1));
      Res = B.CreateOr(Res, B.CreateShl(B.CreateAnd(Bit, Set), B.getInt32(I)));
      K = B.CreateAdd(K, Set);
    }
    return Res;
  };

  auto doPext = [&](llvm::Value *S, llvm::Value *Mk) -> llvm::Value * {
    if (IsX86)
      return B.CreateIntrinsic(llvm::Intrinsic::x86_bmi_pext_32, {}, {S, Mk});
    return pextSW(S, Mk);
  };
  auto doPdep = [&](llvm::Value *S, llvm::Value *Mk) -> llvm::Value * {
    if (IsX86)
      return B.CreateIntrinsic(llvm::Intrinsic::x86_bmi_pdep_32, {}, {S, Mk});
    return pdepSW(S, Mk);
  };

  auto *PE = doPext(Src, M1);
  auto *PD = doPdep(Src, M2);
  // Combine so both a mis-gathered and a mis-scattered bit perturb the result.
  auto *S = B.CreateXor(B.CreateMul(PE, B.getInt32(3)),
                        B.CreateMul(PD, B.getInt32(5)));

  // Fold into the usual data-dependent diamond + PHI so the L1 passes have
  // integer arithmetic (and a branch) to transform.
  auto *T = B.CreateXor(B.CreateXor(B.CreateAdd(A, C), B.CreateSub(A, C)),
                        B.getInt32(0x5C5C));
  auto *U = B.CreateOr(B.CreateAnd(S, C), B.CreateAdd(T, B.getInt32(33203)));
  auto *BaseV = B.CreateAdd(S, U);
  B.CreateCondBr(B.CreateICmpNE(B.CreateAnd(B.CreateXor(A, C), B.getInt32(1)),
                                B.getInt32(0)),
                 Then, Else);

  B.SetInsertPoint(Then);
  auto *RT = B.CreateAdd(BaseV, A);
  B.CreateBr(Merge);

  B.SetInsertPoint(Else);
  auto *RE = B.CreateXor(BaseV, C);
  B.CreateBr(Merge);

  B.SetInsertPoint(Merge);
  auto *Pc = B.CreatePHI(I32, 2);
  Pc->addIncoming(RT, Then);
  Pc->addIncoming(RE, Else);
  B.CreateRet(Pc);
  assert(!llvm::verifyModule(*M, &llvm::errs()));
  return M;
}

// One SSE4.1 horizontal *minimum-and-position* search on a 128-bit <8 x u16>
// vector — the first patch-full coverage of the PHMINPOSUW instruction, a
// distinct SSE4.1 hardware primitive no other shape reaches: it finds, in a
// single instruction, BOTH the smallest unsigned 16-bit lane AND the index of
// its first (lowest-indexed) occurrence.  It is the natural non-crypto sibling
// to the already-covered horizontal reductions (min/max/add) — those collapse a
// vector to a value; PHMINPOSUW uniquely also reports *where* the extremum is.
// x86/x86-64 emit PHMINPOSUW / VPHMINPOSUW (llvm.x86.sse41.phminposuw; the
// "sse41" substring makes detectTargetFeaturesX86 add +sse4.1) — result lane 0
// = the min value, lane 1 = its index, lanes 2-7 = 0; AArch64 and ARM32
// open-code the identical unsigned horizontal min + first-index scan
// (extractelement -> icmp ult -> select chain), libcall-free.  Both i386 and
// x86-64 select the native instruction (SSE4.1 is present in 32-bit mode, and
// the harness already decodes AVX on i386), and fork-Unicorn's default x86 CPU
// is Haswell (SSE4.1), so PHMINPOSUW decodes on every x86 cell; AArch64/ARM run
// the open-coded scan on UC_CPU_ARM64_MAX / UC_CPU_ARM_MAX.  checkEquiv compares
// the original against the obfuscated copy *within* each cell (never across
// ISAs) and neither copy touches the min sub-graph, so both emit byte-identical
// PHMINPOSUW (or byte-identical scans) and observe identical results; each cell
// only needs its own PHMINPOSUW to decode and the obfuscation to preserve it.
// Two independent <8 x u16> vectors are built from the runtime args (each lane
// mixes both args, truncated to 16 bits) so neither the min value nor its
// position folds to a constant, and the (min, index) pairs of both searches are
// combined with distinct weights (so a mis-selected value OR a mis-reported
// index changes the sum) before folding into the usual data-dependent diamond +
// PHI with non-folding constants (0x5C5C/33203) so the subst / const-enc /
// opaque / flatten / bogus / indirect passes have integer arithmetic (and a
// branch) to transform, while the PHMINPOSUW itself is left untouched — an
// undecoded PHMINPOSUW faults the Unicorn baseline (UC_ERR_INSN_INVALID) and
// any value divergence is a genuine backend / fork-Unicorn bug.
std::unique_ptr<llvm::Module> buildVecPhMinPosUW128IR(llvm::LLVMContext &Ctx,
                                                      const char *Triple) {
  auto M = std::make_unique<llvm::Module>("substtest", Ctx);
  M->setTargetTriple(llvm::Triple(Triple));
  llvm::Triple TT(Triple);
  llvm::Triple::ArchType ArchK = TT.getArch();
  bool IsX86 = ArchK == llvm::Triple::x86 || ArchK == llvm::Triple::x86_64;

  auto *I16 = llvm::Type::getInt16Ty(Ctx);
  auto *I32 = llvm::Type::getInt32Ty(Ctx);
  auto *V8u = llvm::FixedVectorType::get(I16, 8);

  auto *FTy = llvm::FunctionType::get(I32, {I32, I32}, false);
  auto *F = llvm::Function::Create(FTy, llvm::Function::ExternalLinkage,
                                   "vphminpos128", M.get());
  F->addFnAttr("min-legal-vector-width", "128");
  auto *Entry = llvm::BasicBlock::Create(Ctx, "entry", F);
  auto *Then = llvm::BasicBlock::Create(Ctx, "then", F);
  auto *Else = llvm::BasicBlock::Create(Ctx, "else", F);
  auto *Merge = llvm::BasicBlock::Create(Ctx, "merge", F);
  auto *A = F->getArg(0), *C = F->getArg(1);

  llvm::IRBuilder<> B(Entry);

  // Two independent <8 x u16> inputs, every lane a runtime mix of both args
  // truncated to 16 bits — so neither the minimum value nor its position is a
  // compile-time constant.
  auto mkVec = [&](bool Swap) -> llvm::Value * {
    llvm::Value *V = llvm::UndefValue::get(V8u);
    for (unsigned I = 0; I < 8; ++I) {
      llvm::Value *X =
          Swap ? B.CreateXor(B.CreateMul(C, B.getInt32(I * 5 + 3)),
                             B.CreateAdd(A, B.getInt32(I * 0x2D + 7)))
               : B.CreateXor(B.CreateMul(A, B.getInt32(I * 7 + 1)),
                             B.CreateAdd(C, B.getInt32(I * 0x3B + 5)));
      V = B.CreateInsertElement(V, B.CreateTrunc(X, I16), uint64_t(I));
    }
    return V;
  };

  // x86 pins the native PHMINPOSUW (result: lane0=min, lane1=index); every
  // other ISA open-codes the identical unsigned horizontal-min + first-index
  // scan and packs it into the same lane layout so only lanes 0/1 are read.
  auto phMinPos = [&](llvm::Value *V) -> llvm::Value * {
    if (IsX86)
      return B.CreateIntrinsic(llvm::Intrinsic::x86_sse41_phminposuw, {}, {V});
    llvm::Value *Min = B.CreateExtractElement(V, uint64_t(0));
    llvm::Value *Idx = B.getInt16(0);
    for (unsigned I = 1; I < 8; ++I) {
      llvm::Value *L = B.CreateExtractElement(V, uint64_t(I));
      llvm::Value *Lt = B.CreateICmpULT(L, Min);
      Min = B.CreateSelect(Lt, L, Min);
      Idx = B.CreateSelect(Lt, B.getInt16(static_cast<uint16_t>(I)), Idx);
    }
    llvm::Value *R = llvm::ConstantAggregateZero::get(V8u);
    R = B.CreateInsertElement(R, Min, uint64_t(0));
    R = B.CreateInsertElement(R, Idx, uint64_t(1));
    return R;
  };

  auto *R1 = phMinPos(mkVec(false));
  auto *R2 = phMinPos(mkVec(true));
  auto *Min1 = B.CreateZExt(B.CreateExtractElement(R1, uint64_t(0)), I32);
  auto *Idx1 = B.CreateZExt(B.CreateExtractElement(R1, uint64_t(1)), I32);
  auto *Min2 = B.CreateZExt(B.CreateExtractElement(R2, uint64_t(0)), I32);
  auto *Idx2 = B.CreateZExt(B.CreateExtractElement(R2, uint64_t(1)), I32);

  // Weight value and index of both searches distinctly so a mis-selected value
  // OR a mis-reported position perturbs the scalar reduction.
  llvm::Value *S = B.CreateAdd(
      B.CreateAdd(B.CreateMul(Min1, B.getInt32(3)),
                  B.CreateMul(Idx1, B.getInt32(7))),
      B.CreateAdd(B.CreateMul(Min2, B.getInt32(5)),
                  B.CreateMul(Idx2, B.getInt32(11))));

  // Fold into the usual data-dependent diamond + PHI so the L1 passes have
  // integer arithmetic (and a branch) to transform.
  auto *T = B.CreateXor(B.CreateXor(B.CreateAdd(A, C), B.CreateSub(A, C)),
                        B.getInt32(0x5C5C));
  auto *U = B.CreateOr(B.CreateAnd(S, C), B.CreateAdd(T, B.getInt32(33203)));
  auto *BaseV = B.CreateAdd(S, U);
  B.CreateCondBr(B.CreateICmpNE(B.CreateAnd(B.CreateXor(A, C), B.getInt32(1)),
                                B.getInt32(0)),
                 Then, Else);

  B.SetInsertPoint(Then);
  auto *RT = B.CreateAdd(BaseV, A);
  B.CreateBr(Merge);

  B.SetInsertPoint(Else);
  auto *RE = B.CreateXor(BaseV, C);
  B.CreateBr(Merge);

  B.SetInsertPoint(Merge);
  auto *Pc = B.CreatePHI(I32, 2);
  Pc->addIncoming(RT, Then);
  Pc->addIncoming(RE, Else);
  B.CreateRet(Pc);
  assert(!llvm::verifyModule(*M, &llvm::errs()));
  return M;
}

// One SSE4.1 dot product (DPPS on <4 x float> + DPPD on <2 x double>) — the
// first patch-full coverage of the dot-product family, a distinct SSE4.1
// primitive no other shape reaches: a single instruction that horizontally
// sums the imm8-high-nibble-selected lane products and then broadcasts (or
// zeroes) the scalar result into the imm8-low-nibble-selected result lanes.  It
// is the floating-point dual of the already-covered integer sum-of-absolute-
// differences reductions (visad256 / vimpsad256) — those collapse integer byte
// lanes; DPPS/DPPD collapse FP lanes through a masked multiply-accumulate.
// x86/x86-64 emit DPPS (66 0F3A 40) / DPPD (66 0F3A 41) via llvm.x86.sse41.dpps
// / llvm.x86.sse41.dppd (the "sse41" substring makes detectTargetFeaturesX86
// add +sse4.1) — both i386 and x86-64 select the native instruction, and the
// default fork-Unicorn x86 CPU is Haswell (SSE4.1), so DPPS/DPPD decode on every
// x86 cell (fork-Unicorn already has helper_dpps/helper_dppd, sse_op_table7
// [0x40]=dpps / [0x41]=dppd).  Neither has an ARM dual, so AArch64 and ARM32
// open-code the identical masked dot product (per-lane fmul of the selected
// products, an fadd tree, then the scalar sum in result lane 0), libcall-free.
// checkEquiv compares the original against the obfuscated copy *within* each
// cell (never across ISAs) and no obfuscation pass touches the FP sub-graph
// (InstSubstitutionPass gates on isIntOrIntVectorTy; ConstantEncryptionPass
// only rewrites ConstantInt/ICmpInst), so both copies emit byte-identical
// DPPS/DPPD (or byte-identical open-coded sums) and observe identical results —
// the x86 hardware summation order need never match the open-coded one because
// only same-ISA copies are compared; an undecoded DPPS/DPPD faults the Unicorn
// baseline (UC_ERR_INSN_INVALID) and any value divergence is a genuine backend /
// fork-Unicorn bug.  Every lane is a runtime mix of both args masked to a small
// signed range ([-32,31]) so the products/sums are exact in float and double
// (well within i32 after fptosi, no rounding, no poison) yet never fold to a
// constant.  The two dot products are combined with distinct weights and folded
// into the usual data-dependent diamond + PHI with non-folding constants
// (0x5C5C / 33203) so the subst / const-enc / opaque / flatten / bogus /
// indirect passes have integer arithmetic (and a branch) to transform while the
// dot-product sub-graph is left untouched.
std::unique_ptr<llvm::Module> buildVecDpProd128IR(llvm::LLVMContext &Ctx,
                                                  const char *Triple) {
  auto M = std::make_unique<llvm::Module>("substtest", Ctx);
  M->setTargetTriple(llvm::Triple(Triple));
  llvm::Triple TT(Triple);
  llvm::Triple::ArchType ArchK = TT.getArch();
  bool IsX86 = ArchK == llvm::Triple::x86 || ArchK == llvm::Triple::x86_64;

  auto *F32 = llvm::Type::getFloatTy(Ctx);
  auto *F64 = llvm::Type::getDoubleTy(Ctx);
  auto *I32 = llvm::Type::getInt32Ty(Ctx);
  auto *V4f = llvm::FixedVectorType::get(F32, 4);
  auto *V2d = llvm::FixedVectorType::get(F64, 2);

  auto *FTy = llvm::FunctionType::get(I32, {I32, I32}, false);
  auto *F = llvm::Function::Create(FTy, llvm::Function::ExternalLinkage,
                                   "vdp128", M.get());
  F->addFnAttr("min-legal-vector-width", "128");
  auto *Entry = llvm::BasicBlock::Create(Ctx, "entry", F);
  auto *Then = llvm::BasicBlock::Create(Ctx, "then", F);
  auto *Else = llvm::BasicBlock::Create(Ctx, "else", F);
  auto *Merge = llvm::BasicBlock::Create(Ctx, "merge", F);
  auto *A = F->getArg(0), *C = F->getArg(1);

  llvm::IRBuilder<> B(Entry);

  // Each lane: a runtime mix of both args masked to [-32,31] so products/sums
  // stay exact in float/double and never fold to a constant.
  auto lane = [&](unsigned I, bool Swap, llvm::Type *FpTy) -> llvm::Value * {
    llvm::Value *Mix =
        Swap ? B.CreateXor(B.CreateMul(C, B.getInt32(I * 5 + 2)),
                           B.CreateAdd(A, B.getInt32(I * 0x11 + 1)))
             : B.CreateXor(B.CreateMul(A, B.getInt32(I * 7 + 1)),
                           B.CreateAdd(C, B.getInt32(I * 0x13 + 3)));
    llvm::Value *Small =
        B.CreateSub(B.CreateAnd(Mix, B.getInt32(0x3F)), B.getInt32(32));
    return B.CreateSIToFP(Small, FpTy);
  };

  // DPPS: <4 x float> dot product, imm 0xF1 (all four products -> lane 0).
  llvm::Value *DpsSum;
  {
    llvm::Value *Va = llvm::UndefValue::get(V4f);
    llvm::Value *Vb = llvm::UndefValue::get(V4f);
    for (unsigned I = 0; I < 4; ++I) {
      Va = B.CreateInsertElement(Va, lane(I, false, F32), uint64_t(I));
      Vb = B.CreateInsertElement(Vb, lane(I, true, F32), uint64_t(I));
    }
    if (IsX86) {
      auto *R = B.CreateIntrinsic(llvm::Intrinsic::x86_sse41_dpps, {},
                                  {Va, Vb, B.getInt8(0xF1)});
      DpsSum = B.CreateExtractElement(R, uint64_t(0));
    } else {
      DpsSum = llvm::ConstantFP::get(F32, 0.0);
      for (unsigned I = 0; I < 4; ++I)
        DpsSum = B.CreateFAdd(
            DpsSum, B.CreateFMul(B.CreateExtractElement(Va, uint64_t(I)),
                                 B.CreateExtractElement(Vb, uint64_t(I))));
    }
  }

  // DPPD: <2 x double> dot product, imm 0x31 (both products -> lane 0).
  llvm::Value *DpdSum;
  {
    llvm::Value *Va = llvm::UndefValue::get(V2d);
    llvm::Value *Vb = llvm::UndefValue::get(V2d);
    for (unsigned I = 0; I < 2; ++I) {
      Va = B.CreateInsertElement(Va, lane(I, false, F64), uint64_t(I));
      Vb = B.CreateInsertElement(Vb, lane(I, true, F64), uint64_t(I));
    }
    if (IsX86) {
      auto *R = B.CreateIntrinsic(llvm::Intrinsic::x86_sse41_dppd, {},
                                  {Va, Vb, B.getInt8(0x31)});
      DpdSum = B.CreateExtractElement(R, uint64_t(0));
    } else {
      DpdSum = llvm::ConstantFP::get(F64, 0.0);
      for (unsigned I = 0; I < 2; ++I)
        DpdSum = B.CreateFAdd(
            DpdSum, B.CreateFMul(B.CreateExtractElement(Va, uint64_t(I)),
                                 B.CreateExtractElement(Vb, uint64_t(I))));
    }
  }

  // Both sums are exact integers in range; combine with distinct weights so a
  // mis-computed lane in either dot product perturbs the reduction.
  auto *Ps = B.CreateFPToSI(DpsSum, I32);
  auto *Pd = B.CreateFPToSI(DpdSum, I32);
  auto *S = B.CreateXor(B.CreateMul(Ps, B.getInt32(3)),
                        B.CreateMul(Pd, B.getInt32(5)));

  // Fold into the usual data-dependent diamond + PHI so the L1 passes have
  // integer arithmetic (and a branch) to transform.
  auto *T = B.CreateXor(B.CreateXor(B.CreateAdd(A, C), B.CreateSub(A, C)),
                        B.getInt32(0x5C5C));
  auto *U = B.CreateOr(B.CreateAnd(S, C), B.CreateAdd(T, B.getInt32(33203)));
  auto *BaseV = B.CreateAdd(S, U);
  B.CreateCondBr(B.CreateICmpNE(B.CreateAnd(B.CreateXor(A, C), B.getInt32(1)),
                                B.getInt32(0)),
                 Then, Else);

  B.SetInsertPoint(Then);
  auto *RT = B.CreateAdd(BaseV, A);
  B.CreateBr(Merge);

  B.SetInsertPoint(Else);
  auto *RE = B.CreateXor(BaseV, C);
  B.CreateBr(Merge);

  B.SetInsertPoint(Merge);
  auto *Pc = B.CreatePHI(I32, 2);
  Pc->addIncoming(RT, Then);
  Pc->addIncoming(RE, Else);
  B.CreateRet(Pc);
  assert(!llvm::verifyModule(*M, &llvm::errs()));
  return M;
}

// One BMI bit-field-extract pair (BEXTR + BZHI) on 32-bit GPRs — the first
// patch-full coverage of the BMI1 BEXTR and BMI2 BZHI instructions, distinct x86
// bit-field primitives the pdeppext (PDEP/PEXT) shape does not reach.  x86 emits
// BEXTR (VEX.LZ.0F38.W0 F7) via llvm.x86.bmi.bextr.32 — the "bmi.bextr"
// substring makes detectTargetFeaturesX86 add +bmi — and BZHI (VEX.LZ.0F38.W0
// F5) via llvm.x86.bmi.bzhi.32 ("bmi.bzhi" adds +bmi2).  BEXTR extracts LEN
// (control[15:8]) bits starting at START (control[7:0]) from the source; BZHI
// zeroes the source bits at and above the low-8-bit index.  Like pdeppext,
// neither has an ARM dual, so every non-x86 ISA open-codes the identical
// transform: BEXTR as (src >> start) & ((1<<len)-1) and BZHI as
// src & ((1<<index)-1).  start / len / index are all masked to [0,31] so every
// shift is well-defined (< 32) and the open-coded form matches the hardware
// exactly (a shift of 31 already zeroes the high bits, so an over-wide LEN mask
// is harmless).  fork-Unicorn already decodes both (translate.c case 0x0f7
// bextr / 0x0f5 bzhi).  src and the two controls are derived from the two
// runtime args so the backend cannot fold the extract to a constant.  checkEquiv
// compares the original against the obfuscated copy within each cell (never
// across ISAs) and neither copy touches the bextr/bzhi sub-graph, so both emit
// byte-identical code and observe identical results; an undecoded bextr/bzhi
// faults the x86 Unicorn baseline (UC_ERR_INSN_INVALID) and any value divergence
// is a genuine backend / fork-Unicorn bug.  The two results are combined and
// folded into the usual data-dependent diamond + PHI with non-folding constants
// (0x5C5C / 33203).
std::unique_ptr<llvm::Module> buildBmiBitsIR(llvm::LLVMContext &Ctx,
                                             const char *Triple) {
  auto M = std::make_unique<llvm::Module>("substtest", Ctx);
  M->setTargetTriple(llvm::Triple(Triple));
  llvm::Triple TT(Triple);
  llvm::Triple::ArchType ArchK = TT.getArch();
  bool IsX86 = ArchK == llvm::Triple::x86 || ArchK == llvm::Triple::x86_64;

  auto *I32 = llvm::Type::getInt32Ty(Ctx);
  auto *FTy = llvm::FunctionType::get(I32, {I32, I32}, false);
  auto *F = llvm::Function::Create(FTy, llvm::Function::ExternalLinkage,
                                   "bmibits", M.get());
  auto *Entry = llvm::BasicBlock::Create(Ctx, "entry", F);
  auto *Then = llvm::BasicBlock::Create(Ctx, "then", F);
  auto *Else = llvm::BasicBlock::Create(Ctx, "else", F);
  auto *Merge = llvm::BasicBlock::Create(Ctx, "merge", F);
  auto *A = F->getArg(0), *C = F->getArg(1);

  llvm::IRBuilder<> B(Entry);

  // Runtime source; start / len / index all masked to [0,31] so shifts are
  // always well-defined and the open-coded form matches BEXTR/BZHI exactly.
  auto *Src = B.CreateXor(B.CreateMul(A, B.getInt32(0x9E3779B9u)), C);
  auto *Start = B.CreateAnd(B.CreateAdd(A, B.CreateLShr(C, B.getInt32(3))),
                            B.getInt32(31));
  auto *Len = B.CreateAnd(B.CreateXor(A, B.CreateShl(C, B.getInt32(1))),
                          B.getInt32(31));
  auto *Index =
      B.CreateAnd(B.CreateAdd(C, B.CreateMul(A, B.getInt32(7))), B.getInt32(31));

  // BEXTR: extract LEN bits at START.  x86 pins the hardware instruction; every
  // other ISA open-codes (src >> start) & ((1<<len)-1).
  auto *BE = [&]() -> llvm::Value * {
    if (IsX86) {
      auto *Ctrl = B.CreateOr(Start, B.CreateShl(Len, B.getInt32(8)));
      return B.CreateIntrinsic(llvm::Intrinsic::x86_bmi_bextr_32, {},
                               {Src, Ctrl});
    }
    auto *Mask = B.CreateSub(B.CreateShl(B.getInt32(1), Len), B.getInt32(1));
    return B.CreateAnd(B.CreateLShr(Src, Start), Mask);
  }();

  // BZHI: zero bits at and above INDEX.  x86 pins the hardware instruction;
  // every other ISA open-codes src & ((1<<index)-1).
  auto *BZ = [&]() -> llvm::Value * {
    if (IsX86)
      return B.CreateIntrinsic(llvm::Intrinsic::x86_bmi_bzhi_32, {},
                               {Src, Index});
    auto *Mask = B.CreateSub(B.CreateShl(B.getInt32(1), Index), B.getInt32(1));
    return B.CreateAnd(Src, Mask);
  }();

  // Combine so a mis-extracted or mis-cleared bit perturbs the result.
  auto *S = B.CreateXor(B.CreateMul(BE, B.getInt32(3)),
                        B.CreateMul(BZ, B.getInt32(5)));

  // Fold into the usual data-dependent diamond + PHI so the L1 passes have
  // integer arithmetic (and a branch) to transform.
  auto *T = B.CreateXor(B.CreateXor(B.CreateAdd(A, C), B.CreateSub(A, C)),
                        B.getInt32(0x5C5C));
  auto *U = B.CreateOr(B.CreateAnd(S, C), B.CreateAdd(T, B.getInt32(33203)));
  auto *BaseV = B.CreateAdd(S, U);
  B.CreateCondBr(B.CreateICmpNE(B.CreateAnd(B.CreateXor(A, C), B.getInt32(1)),
                                B.getInt32(0)),
                 Then, Else);

  B.SetInsertPoint(Then);
  auto *RT = B.CreateAdd(BaseV, A);
  B.CreateBr(Merge);

  B.SetInsertPoint(Else);
  auto *RE = B.CreateXor(BaseV, C);
  B.CreateBr(Merge);

  B.SetInsertPoint(Merge);
  auto *Pc = B.CreatePHI(I32, 2);
  Pc->addIncoming(RT, Then);
  Pc->addIncoming(RE, Else);
  B.CreateRet(Pc);
  assert(!llvm::verifyModule(*M, &llvm::errs()));
  return M;
}

// One SHA-256 message-schedule + hash-update round — the first patch-full
// coverage of the SHA crypto instruction family, the sibling of the completed
// AES-NI family (vaesenc128..vaeskeygen128) and the CRC (crc32acc) / carry-less
// multiply (polymul) families.  Unlike AES (hardware on x86 *and* ARM), SHA-NI
// is NOT on the harness's default x86 Unicorn CPU — the Haswell model predates
// the SHA extensions (cpu.c: Haswell has no CPUID_7_0_EBX_SHA_NI) — so this is
// the first shape where *ARM pins the hardware crypto and x86 software-open-
// codes*, the mirror of the vaeskeygen128 / vphminpos128 pattern (x86 hardware,
// non-x86 software).  AArch64 emits native SHA256H/SHA256H2/SHA256SU0/SHA256SU1
// (llvm.aarch64.crypto.sha256* — the "aarch64.crypto.sha" substring makes
// detectTargetFeaturesAArch64 add +sha2; decode on UC_CPU_ARM64_MAX); ARM32
// emits the AArch32 equivalents (llvm.arm.neon.sha256* — "arm.neon.sha" adds
// +v8,+fp-armv8,+sha2; decode on UC_CPU_ARM_MAX, already exercised by
// ARM32_CryptoRTTests); x86/x86-64 and any other ISA open-code an equivalent
// SHA-256 round (the sigma/Ch/Maj mix via rotate + shift + and + xor + add —
// all exact, all legal, zero libcall).  checkEquiv compares the original
// against the obfuscated copy *within* each cell (never across ISAs), so the
// x86 software round need not match the ARM hardware result; each cell only
// needs its own SHA path to run and the obfuscation to preserve semantics.  The
// state and message words are derived from the two runtime args (each lane
// mixes both, xored with a distinct non-folding constant) so the backend cannot
// fold the round to a constant; the <4 x i32> result is reduced to a scalar and
// merged into the usual data-dependent diamond + PHI with non-folding constants
// (0x5C5C / 33203) so the L1 passes have integer arithmetic (and a branch) to
// transform, while the SHA sub-graph is left in place — an undecoded SHA
// instruction faults the ARM Unicorn baseline (UC_ERR_INSN_INVALID) and any
// value divergence is a genuine backend / fork-Unicorn bug.
std::unique_ptr<llvm::Module> buildSha256IR(llvm::LLVMContext &Ctx,
                                            const char *Triple) {
  auto M = std::make_unique<llvm::Module>("substtest", Ctx);
  M->setTargetTriple(llvm::Triple(Triple));
  llvm::Triple TT(Triple);
  llvm::Triple::ArchType ArchK = TT.getArch();
  bool IsA64 = ArchK == llvm::Triple::aarch64;
  bool IsA32 = ArchK == llvm::Triple::arm || ArchK == llvm::Triple::thumb;
  bool IsArm = IsA64 || IsA32;

  auto *I32 = llvm::Type::getInt32Ty(Ctx);
  auto *V4i32 = llvm::FixedVectorType::get(I32, 4);

  auto *FTy = llvm::FunctionType::get(I32, {I32, I32}, false);
  auto *F = llvm::Function::Create(FTy, llvm::Function::ExternalLinkage,
                                   "sha256", M.get());
  F->addFnAttr("min-legal-vector-width", "128");
  auto *Entry = llvm::BasicBlock::Create(Ctx, "entry", F);
  auto *Then = llvm::BasicBlock::Create(Ctx, "then", F);
  auto *Else = llvm::BasicBlock::Create(Ctx, "else", F);
  auto *Merge = llvm::BasicBlock::Create(Ctx, "merge", F);
  auto *A = F->getArg(0), *C = F->getArg(1);

  llvm::IRBuilder<> B(Entry);

  // Build a <4 x i32> from the two runtime args + four distinct non-folding
  // constants, so no lane is a foldable constant.
  auto mkVec = [&](uint32_t K0, uint32_t K1, uint32_t K2, uint32_t K3) {
    uint32_t Ks[4] = {K0, K1, K2, K3};
    llvm::Value *V = llvm::UndefValue::get(V4i32);
    for (unsigned I = 0; I < 4; ++I) {
      llvm::Value *Lane = B.CreateXor(
          B.CreateAdd(B.CreateMul(A, B.getInt32(1u + 2u * I)), C),
          B.getInt32(Ks[I]));
      V = B.CreateInsertElement(V, Lane, uint64_t(I));
    }
    return V;
  };
  auto *Abcd = mkVec(0x6A09E667u, 0xBB67AE85u, 0x3C6EF372u, 0xA54FF53Au);
  auto *Efgh = mkVec(0x510E527Fu, 0x9B05688Cu, 0x1F83D9ABu, 0x5BE0CD19u);
  auto *Wk = mkVec(0x428A2F98u, 0x71374491u, 0xB5C0FBCFu, 0xE9B5DBA5u);

  auto rotr = [&](llvm::Value *X, unsigned N) {
    return B.CreateOr(B.CreateLShr(X, B.getInt32(N)),
                      B.CreateShl(X, B.getInt32(32 - N)));
  };

  llvm::Value *Res;
  if (IsArm) {
    // ARM pins the hardware SHA-256 instructions.  Keep the AArch64 and ARM
    // intrinsic IDs out of a single ?: — they are distinct enum values and
    // mixing them in one conditional is a deprecated conversion.
    llvm::Intrinsic::ID Su0, Su1, H, H2;
    if (IsA64) {
      Su0 = llvm::Intrinsic::aarch64_crypto_sha256su0;
      Su1 = llvm::Intrinsic::aarch64_crypto_sha256su1;
      H = llvm::Intrinsic::aarch64_crypto_sha256h;
      H2 = llvm::Intrinsic::aarch64_crypto_sha256h2;
    } else {
      Su0 = llvm::Intrinsic::arm_neon_sha256su0;
      Su1 = llvm::Intrinsic::arm_neon_sha256su1;
      H = llvm::Intrinsic::arm_neon_sha256h;
      H2 = llvm::Intrinsic::arm_neon_sha256h2;
    }
    auto *Tw = B.CreateIntrinsic(Su0, {Abcd, Efgh});
    auto *Sched = B.CreateIntrinsic(Su1, {Tw, Efgh, Wk});
    auto *H1v = B.CreateIntrinsic(H, {Abcd, Efgh, Sched});
    Res = B.CreateIntrinsic(H2, {H1v, Abcd, Sched});
  } else {
    // x86 / other: open-code one SHA-256 round on the working variables.
    auto Ln = [&](llvm::Value *V, unsigned I) {
      return B.CreateExtractElement(V, uint64_t(I));
    };
    llvm::Value *Va = Ln(Abcd, 0), *Vb = Ln(Abcd, 1), *Vc = Ln(Abcd, 2),
                *Vd = Ln(Abcd, 3);
    llvm::Value *Ve = Ln(Efgh, 0), *Vf = Ln(Efgh, 1), *Vg = Ln(Efgh, 2),
                *Vh = Ln(Efgh, 3);
    llvm::Value *W = Ln(Wk, 0);
    auto *S1 = B.CreateXor(B.CreateXor(rotr(Ve, 6), rotr(Ve, 11)), rotr(Ve, 25));
    auto *Ch = B.CreateXor(B.CreateAnd(Ve, Vf),
                           B.CreateAnd(B.CreateXor(Ve, B.getInt32(-1)), Vg));
    auto *T1 = B.CreateAdd(B.CreateAdd(B.CreateAdd(Vh, S1), Ch), W);
    auto *S0 = B.CreateXor(B.CreateXor(rotr(Va, 2), rotr(Va, 13)), rotr(Va, 22));
    auto *Maj = B.CreateXor(B.CreateXor(B.CreateAnd(Va, Vb), B.CreateAnd(Va, Vc)),
                            B.CreateAnd(Vb, Vc));
    auto *T2 = B.CreateAdd(S0, Maj);
    llvm::Value *V = llvm::UndefValue::get(V4i32);
    V = B.CreateInsertElement(V, B.CreateAdd(T1, T2), uint64_t(0));
    V = B.CreateInsertElement(V, B.CreateAdd(Vd, T1), uint64_t(1));
    V = B.CreateInsertElement(V, B.CreateXor(Va, Vb), uint64_t(2));
    V = B.CreateInsertElement(V, B.CreateXor(Ve, Vf), uint64_t(3));
    Res = V;
  }

  // Reduce the <4 x i32> result to a scalar by xoring the four lanes.
  auto *S = B.CreateXor(
      B.CreateXor(B.CreateExtractElement(Res, uint64_t(0)),
                  B.CreateExtractElement(Res, uint64_t(1))),
      B.CreateXor(B.CreateExtractElement(Res, uint64_t(2)),
                  B.CreateExtractElement(Res, uint64_t(3))));

  // Fold into the usual data-dependent diamond + PHI so the L1 passes have
  // integer arithmetic (and a branch) to transform.
  auto *T = B.CreateXor(B.CreateXor(B.CreateAdd(A, C), B.CreateSub(A, C)),
                        B.getInt32(0x5C5C));
  auto *U = B.CreateOr(B.CreateAnd(S, C), B.CreateAdd(T, B.getInt32(33203)));
  auto *BaseV = B.CreateAdd(S, U);
  B.CreateCondBr(B.CreateICmpNE(B.CreateAnd(B.CreateXor(A, C), B.getInt32(1)),
                                B.getInt32(0)),
                 Then, Else);

  B.SetInsertPoint(Then);
  auto *RT = B.CreateAdd(BaseV, A);
  B.CreateBr(Merge);

  B.SetInsertPoint(Else);
  auto *RE = B.CreateXor(BaseV, C);
  B.CreateBr(Merge);

  B.SetInsertPoint(Merge);
  auto *Pc = B.CreatePHI(I32, 2);
  Pc->addIncoming(RT, Then);
  Pc->addIncoming(RE, Else);
  B.CreateRet(Pc);
  assert(!llvm::verifyModule(*M, &llvm::errs()));
  return M;
}

// One SHA-1 message-schedule + hash-update round — the sibling of sha256 that
// completes the SHA crypto family in patch-full (SHA-256 covers SHA256H/H2/
// SU0/SU1; this covers SHA1C/SHA1H/SHA1SU0/SHA1SU1).  It shares sha256's
// "ARM pins the hardware crypto, x86 software-open-codes" shape — SHA-NI is not
// on the harness's default x86 Unicorn CPU (Haswell) — but adds a dimension
// SHA-256 has none of: SHA1H returns a *scalar* i32 from a crypto intrinsic
// (llvm.aarch64.crypto.sha1h / llvm.arm.neon.sha1h : i32 -> i32), exercising the
// scalar crypto-result codegen path, and SHA-1's 5-word (a,b,c,d,e) state is
// structurally different from SHA-256's 8-word state.  AArch64 emits native
// SHA1C/SHA1H/SHA1SU0/SHA1SU1 (the "aarch64.crypto.sha" substring makes
// detectTargetFeaturesAArch64 add +sha2; decode on UC_CPU_ARM64_MAX); ARM32
// emits the AArch32 equivalents (llvm.arm.neon.sha1* — "arm.neon.sha" adds
// +v8,+fp-armv8,+sha2; decode on UC_CPU_ARM_MAX, already exercised by
// ARM32_CryptoRTTests); x86/x86-64 and any other ISA open-code an equivalent
// SHA-1 round (Ch mix + rotates + adds — all exact, all legal, zero libcall).
// checkEquiv compares the original against the obfuscated copy *within* each
// cell (never across ISAs), so the x86 software round need not match the ARM
// hardware result.  State and schedule words derive from the two runtime args
// (each lane mixes both, xored with a distinct non-folding constant) so the
// backend cannot fold the round to a constant; the <4 x i32> result plus the
// scalar SHA1H output are reduced to a scalar and merged into the usual data-
// dependent diamond + PHI with non-folding constants (0x5C5C / 33203) so the
// L1 passes have integer arithmetic (and a branch) to transform, while the SHA
// sub-graph is left in place — an undecoded SHA instruction faults the ARM
// Unicorn baseline (UC_ERR_INSN_INVALID) and any value divergence is a genuine
// backend / fork-Unicorn bug.
std::unique_ptr<llvm::Module> buildSha1IR(llvm::LLVMContext &Ctx,
                                          const char *Triple) {
  auto M = std::make_unique<llvm::Module>("substtest", Ctx);
  M->setTargetTriple(llvm::Triple(Triple));
  llvm::Triple TT(Triple);
  llvm::Triple::ArchType ArchK = TT.getArch();
  bool IsA64 = ArchK == llvm::Triple::aarch64;
  bool IsA32 = ArchK == llvm::Triple::arm || ArchK == llvm::Triple::thumb;
  bool IsArm = IsA64 || IsA32;

  auto *I32 = llvm::Type::getInt32Ty(Ctx);
  auto *V4i32 = llvm::FixedVectorType::get(I32, 4);

  auto *FTy = llvm::FunctionType::get(I32, {I32, I32}, false);
  auto *F = llvm::Function::Create(FTy, llvm::Function::ExternalLinkage, "sha1",
                                   M.get());
  F->addFnAttr("min-legal-vector-width", "128");
  auto *Entry = llvm::BasicBlock::Create(Ctx, "entry", F);
  auto *Then = llvm::BasicBlock::Create(Ctx, "then", F);
  auto *Else = llvm::BasicBlock::Create(Ctx, "else", F);
  auto *Merge = llvm::BasicBlock::Create(Ctx, "merge", F);
  auto *A = F->getArg(0), *C = F->getArg(1);

  llvm::IRBuilder<> B(Entry);

  auto mkVec = [&](uint32_t K0, uint32_t K1, uint32_t K2, uint32_t K3) {
    uint32_t Ks[4] = {K0, K1, K2, K3};
    llvm::Value *V = llvm::UndefValue::get(V4i32);
    for (unsigned I = 0; I < 4; ++I) {
      llvm::Value *Lane =
          B.CreateXor(B.CreateAdd(B.CreateMul(A, B.getInt32(1u + 2u * I)), C),
                      B.getInt32(Ks[I]));
      V = B.CreateInsertElement(V, Lane, uint64_t(I));
    }
    return V;
  };
  auto *Abcd = mkVec(0x67452301u, 0xEFCDAB89u, 0x98BADCFEu, 0x10325476u);
  auto *Wk0 = mkVec(0x5A827999u, 0x6ED9EBA1u, 0x8F1BBCDCu, 0xCA62C1D6u);
  auto *Wk1 = mkVec(0x428A2F98u, 0x71374491u, 0xB5C0FBCFu, 0xE9B5DBA5u);

  auto rotl = [&](llvm::Value *X, unsigned N) {
    return B.CreateOr(B.CreateShl(X, B.getInt32(N)),
                      B.CreateLShr(X, B.getInt32(32 - N)));
  };
  auto ln = [&](llvm::Value *V, unsigned I) {
    return B.CreateExtractElement(V, uint64_t(I));
  };

  llvm::Value *Res, *Extra;
  if (IsArm) {
    // ARM pins the hardware SHA-1 instructions.  Keep the AArch64 and ARM
    // intrinsic IDs out of a single ?: — they are distinct enum values.
    llvm::Intrinsic::ID Su0, Su1, HC, H;
    if (IsA64) {
      Su0 = llvm::Intrinsic::aarch64_crypto_sha1su0;
      Su1 = llvm::Intrinsic::aarch64_crypto_sha1su1;
      HC = llvm::Intrinsic::aarch64_crypto_sha1c;
      H = llvm::Intrinsic::aarch64_crypto_sha1h;
    } else {
      Su0 = llvm::Intrinsic::arm_neon_sha1su0;
      Su1 = llvm::Intrinsic::arm_neon_sha1su1;
      HC = llvm::Intrinsic::arm_neon_sha1c;
      H = llvm::Intrinsic::arm_neon_sha1h;
    }
    auto *Tw = B.CreateIntrinsic(Su0, {Abcd, Wk0, Wk1});
    auto *Sched = B.CreateIntrinsic(Su1, {Tw, Wk0});
    // SHA1C takes (abcd:<4xi32>, e:i32, wk:<4xi32>) -> <4xi32>.
    Res = B.CreateIntrinsic(HC, {Abcd, ln(Wk1, 0), Sched});
    // SHA1H takes (e:i32) -> i32 — the scalar crypto-result path.
    Extra = B.CreateIntrinsic(H, {ln(Res, 0)});
  } else {
    // x86 / other: open-code one SHA-1 (rounds 0-19, Ch) round.
    llvm::Value *Va = ln(Abcd, 0), *Vb = ln(Abcd, 1), *Vc = ln(Abcd, 2),
                *Vd = ln(Abcd, 3);
    llvm::Value *Ve = ln(Wk1, 0), *W = ln(Wk0, 0);
    auto *Ch = B.CreateOr(B.CreateAnd(Vb, Vc),
                          B.CreateAnd(B.CreateXor(Vb, B.getInt32(-1)), Vd));
    auto *T = B.CreateAdd(
        B.CreateAdd(B.CreateAdd(B.CreateAdd(rotl(Va, 5), Ch), Ve), W),
        B.getInt32(0x5A827999u));
    llvm::Value *V = llvm::UndefValue::get(V4i32);
    V = B.CreateInsertElement(V, T, uint64_t(0));            // a' = t
    V = B.CreateInsertElement(V, Va, uint64_t(1));           // b' = a
    V = B.CreateInsertElement(V, rotl(Vb, 30), uint64_t(2)); // c' = rotl(b,30)
    V = B.CreateInsertElement(V, Vc, uint64_t(3));           // d' = c
    Res = V;
    Extra = rotl(Ve, 30); // e' = rotl(e,30)
  }

  // Reduce the <4 x i32> result to a scalar (xor lanes) and fold in the scalar
  // SHA1H / e' output.
  auto *S = B.CreateXor(
      B.CreateXor(B.CreateXor(ln(Res, 0), ln(Res, 1)),
                  B.CreateXor(ln(Res, 2), ln(Res, 3))),
      Extra);

  auto *T = B.CreateXor(B.CreateXor(B.CreateAdd(A, C), B.CreateSub(A, C)),
                        B.getInt32(0x5C5C));
  auto *U = B.CreateOr(B.CreateAnd(S, C), B.CreateAdd(T, B.getInt32(33203)));
  auto *BaseV = B.CreateAdd(S, U);
  B.CreateCondBr(B.CreateICmpNE(B.CreateAnd(B.CreateXor(A, C), B.getInt32(1)),
                                B.getInt32(0)),
                 Then, Else);

  B.SetInsertPoint(Then);
  auto *RT = B.CreateAdd(BaseV, A);
  B.CreateBr(Merge);

  B.SetInsertPoint(Else);
  auto *RE = B.CreateXor(BaseV, C);
  B.CreateBr(Merge);

  B.SetInsertPoint(Merge);
  auto *Pc = B.CreatePHI(I32, 2);
  Pc->addIncoming(RT, Then);
  Pc->addIncoming(RE, Else);
  B.CreateRet(Pc);
  assert(!llvm::verifyModule(*M, &llvm::errs()));
  return M;
}

// One SHA-512 message-schedule + hash-update round — the 64-bit sibling that
// completes the SHA crypto family (sha256 covers SHA256*, sha1 covers SHA1*).
// It adds two dimensions neither has: (1) the words are *64-bit* (<2 x i64>,
// exercising the i64 crypto path — and on 32-bit ISAs i386/ARM32 the i64
// rotates scalarize into multi-register ops), and (2) SHA-512 is *AArch64-only*
// hardware — AArch32 has no SHA-512 instructions — so unlike sha256/sha1 (where
// ARM32 pinned the hardware) here ARM32 joins x86 and everything else in the
// software-open-code group, and *only* AArch64 pins hardware.  The feature is
// also different: FEAT_SHA512 is grouped under LLVM's SHA3 subtarget feature, so
// the "aarch64.crypto.sha512" substring makes detectTargetFeaturesAArch64 add
// +sha3 (not +sha2).  AArch64 emits native SHA512H/SHA512H2/SHA512SU0/SHA512SU1
// (llvm.aarch64.crypto.sha512* on <2 x i64>; UC_CPU_ARM64_MAX decodes them via
// disas_crypto_three_reg_sha512 / disas_crypto_two_reg_sha512, gated on
// aa64_sha512 = ID_AA64ISAR0.SHA2>=2, which the harness CPU sets); x86/x86-64,
// ARM32 and any other ISA open-code an equivalent SHA-512 round (Sigma/Ch/Maj on
// i64 via rotate + shift + and + xor + add — all exact, all legal, zero
// libcall).  checkEquiv compares the original against the obfuscated copy
// *within* each cell (never across ISAs), so the software round need not match
// the AArch64 hardware result.  State and schedule words derive from the two
// runtime args (each lane mixes both, xored with a distinct non-folding
// constant) so the backend cannot fold the round to a constant; the <2 x i64>
// result is reduced to a scalar and merged into the usual data-dependent diamond
// + PHI with non-folding constants (0x5C5C / 33203) so the L1 passes have
// integer arithmetic (and a branch) to transform, while the SHA sub-graph is
// left in place — an undecoded SHA instruction faults the AArch64 Unicorn
// baseline (UC_ERR_INSN_INVALID) and any value divergence is a genuine backend /
// fork-Unicorn bug.
std::unique_ptr<llvm::Module> buildSha512IR(llvm::LLVMContext &Ctx,
                                            const char *Triple) {
  auto M = std::make_unique<llvm::Module>("substtest", Ctx);
  M->setTargetTriple(llvm::Triple(Triple));
  llvm::Triple TT(Triple);
  bool IsA64 = TT.getArch() == llvm::Triple::aarch64;

  auto *I32 = llvm::Type::getInt32Ty(Ctx);
  auto *I64 = llvm::Type::getInt64Ty(Ctx);
  auto *V2i64 = llvm::FixedVectorType::get(I64, 2);

  auto *FTy = llvm::FunctionType::get(I32, {I32, I32}, false);
  auto *F = llvm::Function::Create(FTy, llvm::Function::ExternalLinkage,
                                   "sha512", M.get());
  F->addFnAttr("min-legal-vector-width", "128");
  auto *Entry = llvm::BasicBlock::Create(Ctx, "entry", F);
  auto *Then = llvm::BasicBlock::Create(Ctx, "then", F);
  auto *Else = llvm::BasicBlock::Create(Ctx, "else", F);
  auto *Merge = llvm::BasicBlock::Create(Ctx, "merge", F);
  auto *A = F->getArg(0), *C = F->getArg(1);

  llvm::IRBuilder<> B(Entry);
  auto *A64 = B.CreateZExt(A, I64);
  auto *C64 = B.CreateZExt(C, I64);

  // Build a <2 x i64> from the two runtime args + two distinct non-folding
  // constants, so no lane is a foldable constant.
  auto mkVec = [&](uint64_t K0, uint64_t K1) {
    uint64_t Ks[2] = {K0, K1};
    llvm::Value *V = llvm::UndefValue::get(V2i64);
    for (unsigned I = 0; I < 2; ++I) {
      llvm::Value *Lane = B.CreateXor(
          B.CreateAdd(B.CreateMul(A64, B.getInt64(1u + 2u * I)), C64),
          B.getInt64(Ks[I]));
      V = B.CreateInsertElement(V, Lane, uint64_t(I));
    }
    return V;
  };
  auto *Ab = mkVec(0x6A09E667F3BCC908ull, 0xBB67AE8584CAA73Bull);
  auto *Cd = mkVec(0x3C6EF372FE94F82Bull, 0xA54FF53A5F1D36F1ull);
  auto *Wk = mkVec(0x428A2F98D728AE22ull, 0x7137449123EF65CDull);

  auto rotr = [&](llvm::Value *X, unsigned N) {
    return B.CreateOr(B.CreateLShr(X, B.getInt64(N)),
                      B.CreateShl(X, B.getInt64(64 - N)));
  };
  auto ln = [&](llvm::Value *V, unsigned I) {
    return B.CreateExtractElement(V, uint64_t(I));
  };

  llvm::Value *Res;
  if (IsA64) {
    // AArch64 pins the hardware SHA-512 instructions (no AArch32 equivalent).
    auto *Tw =
        B.CreateIntrinsic(llvm::Intrinsic::aarch64_crypto_sha512su0, {Ab, Cd});
    auto *Sched = B.CreateIntrinsic(llvm::Intrinsic::aarch64_crypto_sha512su1,
                                    {Tw, Cd, Wk});
    auto *H1v = B.CreateIntrinsic(llvm::Intrinsic::aarch64_crypto_sha512h,
                                  {Ab, Cd, Sched});
    Res = B.CreateIntrinsic(llvm::Intrinsic::aarch64_crypto_sha512h2,
                            {H1v, Ab, Sched});
  } else {
    // x86 / ARM32 / other: open-code one SHA-512 round on i64 working words.
    llvm::Value *Va = ln(Ab, 0), *Vb = ln(Ab, 1);
    llvm::Value *Vc = ln(Cd, 0), *Vd = ln(Cd, 1);
    llvm::Value *Ve = ln(Wk, 0), *Vf = ln(Wk, 1);
    llvm::Value *Vg = B.CreateXor(Va, Vd), *Vh = B.CreateAdd(Vb, Vc);
    llvm::Value *W = Ve;
    auto *S1 =
        B.CreateXor(B.CreateXor(rotr(Ve, 14), rotr(Ve, 18)), rotr(Ve, 41));
    auto *Ch = B.CreateXor(B.CreateAnd(Ve, Vf),
                           B.CreateAnd(B.CreateXor(Ve, B.getInt64(-1)), Vg));
    auto *T1 = B.CreateAdd(B.CreateAdd(B.CreateAdd(Vh, S1), Ch), W);
    auto *S0 =
        B.CreateXor(B.CreateXor(rotr(Va, 28), rotr(Va, 34)), rotr(Va, 39));
    auto *Maj =
        B.CreateXor(B.CreateXor(B.CreateAnd(Va, Vb), B.CreateAnd(Va, Vc)),
                    B.CreateAnd(Vb, Vc));
    auto *T2 = B.CreateAdd(S0, Maj);
    llvm::Value *V = llvm::UndefValue::get(V2i64);
    V = B.CreateInsertElement(V, B.CreateAdd(T1, T2), uint64_t(0));
    V = B.CreateInsertElement(V, B.CreateAdd(Vd, T1), uint64_t(1));
    Res = V;
  }

  // Reduce the <2 x i64> result to a scalar i64 (xor lanes), then fold the high
  // and low halves to i32.
  auto *S64 = B.CreateXor(ln(Res, 0), ln(Res, 1));
  auto *S = B.CreateXor(B.CreateTrunc(S64, I32),
                        B.CreateTrunc(B.CreateLShr(S64, B.getInt64(32)), I32));

  auto *T = B.CreateXor(B.CreateXor(B.CreateAdd(A, C), B.CreateSub(A, C)),
                        B.getInt32(0x5C5C));
  auto *U = B.CreateOr(B.CreateAnd(S, C), B.CreateAdd(T, B.getInt32(33203)));
  auto *BaseV = B.CreateAdd(S, U);
  B.CreateCondBr(B.CreateICmpNE(B.CreateAnd(B.CreateXor(A, C), B.getInt32(1)),
                                B.getInt32(0)),
                 Then, Else);

  B.SetInsertPoint(Then);
  auto *RT = B.CreateAdd(BaseV, A);
  B.CreateBr(Merge);

  B.SetInsertPoint(Else);
  auto *RE = B.CreateXor(BaseV, C);
  B.CreateBr(Merge);

  B.SetInsertPoint(Merge);
  auto *Pc = B.CreatePHI(I32, 2);
  Pc->addIncoming(RT, Then);
  Pc->addIncoming(RE, Else);
  B.CreateRet(Pc);
  assert(!llvm::verifyModule(*M, &llvm::errs()));
  return M;
}

// ISA × format combinations; samples chosen to carry encryptable integer
// constants (binary-operator / compare operands), including i8/i16/i32/i64
// widths, a global-memory case (data section is compared too), and an integer
// vector.  Every obfuscated copy must be bit-for-bit equivalent under Unicorn.
// ===========================================================================

// ===========================================================================
// Opaque-predicate grid — the third L1 sample pass and the first that changes
// the control-flow graph.  Same 4×3 = 12 ISA × format combinations; samples
// chosen to exercise diverse control flow (single block, loop header/body/
// latch back-edges, calls, globals).  Every obfuscated copy must be bit-for-bit
// equivalent under Unicorn — this is what validates the rewrite backend's
// relocation of the *new* branches/blocks the pass introduces.
// ===========================================================================
#define PATCH_FULL_OP_SUITE(SUITE, ISA)                                        \

// ===========================================================================
// Composed grid — all three sample passes stacked (substitution + constant
// encryption + opaque predicates), exactly as enabling --subst --const-enc
// --opaque together would.  This is the hardest case for the rewrite backend:
// MBA operators whose constants are encrypted, all inside opaque-guarded
// blocks.  Samples carry operators AND constants AND control flow.  Every
// fully-obfuscated copy must still be bit-for-bit equivalent under Unicorn,
// proving the passes compose without breaking each other or the backend.
// ===========================================================================

// ===========================================================================
// Control-flow flattening grid — the fourth L1 sample pass.  Flattening only
// fires on multi-block functions, so this grid uses the control-flow-rich
// samples (loops, diamonds, multiple returns).  Each obfuscated copy must be
// bit-for-bit equivalent under Unicorn — this validates the rewrite backend's
// relocation of the dispatcher's switch (which the backend may lower to a jump
// table in read-only data) and the rebuilt back-edges.
// ===========================================================================
#define PATCH_FULL_FLAT_SUITE(SUITE, ISA)                                      \
  TEST(SUITE, MultiWayBranch) {                                                \

// ===========================================================================
// Bogus-control-flow grid — the fifth L1 sample pass.  Like opaque predicates
// it fires on any block (single-block samples included), but it grows a
// multi-block fake sub-graph carrying a real junk computation per block, so it
// is a denser branch-relocation stress test.  Same 4×3 = 12 ISA × format
// combinations and the same diverse samples as the opaque grid.  Every
// obfuscated copy must be bit-for-bit equivalent under Unicorn — validating the
// rewrite backend's relocation of the many *new* fake branches/blocks.
// ===========================================================================
#define PATCH_FULL_BOGUS_SUITE(SUITE, ISA)                                     \
  TEST(SUITE, ArithMix) {                                                      \
    checkEquiv(ISA, buildArithMixIR, "amix", kPairs, 1, true, Xform::Bogus);   \
  }                                                                            \

// ===========================================================================
// Indirect-branch grid — the sixth L1 sample pass.  It rewrites each two-way
// conditional branch into an `indirectbr`: select between the two successors'
// block addresses, launder the chosen target through a volatile stack slot,
// then branch through the register.  This is the heaviest rewrite-backend
// stress in the suite — every target lowers a `blockaddress`, which on most
// ISAs spills to a read-only literal pool of (absolute) code pointers emitted
// as a *separate* section.  At a fixed emulation VA those absolute pointers are
// exact, so this grid validates (a) blockaddress lowering + the indirect branch
// itself and (b) the multi-section image placement that positions the literal
// pool alongside .text.  Fires only on multi-block functions, so it uses the
// same control-flow-rich samples as the flattening grid.
//
// (Native ASLR/PIE deployment of these absolute pointer pools additionally
// needs load-time rebase relocations — tracked separately in the roadmap; it is
// orthogonal to the semantic equivalence proven here.)
// ===========================================================================
#define PATCH_FULL_INDIRECT_SUITE(SUITE, ISA)                                  \
  TEST(SUITE, MultiWayBranch) {                                                \
    checkEquiv(ISA, buildMultiWayBranchIR, "mwbr", kPairs, 1, true,            \
               Xform::Indirect);                                               \
  }                                                                            \
  TEST(SUITE, MutualRecursion) {                                               \
    checkEquiv(ISA, buildMutualRecursionIR, "mrec", kPairs, 1, true,           \
               Xform::Indirect);                                               \

// COFF ARM32 is the only *Thumb* (thumbv7) cell. It used to fail: 32-bit
// Thumb2 literal loads (fixup_t2_ldst_pcrel_12) of the blockaddress constant
// pool were mis-anchored by 2 bytes whenever the fixup PC was not 4-aligned,
// because the rewrite backend's AddressModelBackend::evaluateFixup overwrote
// (rather than added to) the ARM backend's AlignDown(PC,4) pre-seed. Fixed in
// the LLVM fork (`Value += Target.getConstant()`); all 12 cells now pass.
// (The earlier "missing interworking bit" theory was a misdiagnosis: in Thumb
// state `mov pc,<reg>` is BranchWritePC — non-interworking — so the even block
// address is correct, matching stable LLVM 22's identical even-valued output.)
PATCH_FULL_INDIRECT_SUITE(PatchFullIndirect_COFF_ARM32, kCOFF_ARM32)

// ===========================================================================
// Indirect-call obfuscation (IndirectCallPass, CLI `--ind-call`): rewrites
// direct calls to defined functions into position-independent indirect calls
// through an opaque function pointer.  Unlike the other passes (which fire on
// any function with branches/operators), this one only fires where a direct
// call to a *defined* function exists, so the suite uses the call-heavy shapes:
// a cross-function caller, mutual recursion, self-recursion, and a caller with
// several distinct callees.  Each verifies the rewrite backend correctly
// materialises the callee's address (PC-relative) and lowers the indirect call
// across every ISA × format cell.
// ===========================================================================
#define PATCH_FULL_INDCALL_SUITE(SUITE, ISA)                                   \
  TEST(SUITE, CallChain) {                                                     \
    checkEquiv(ISA, buildCallChainIR, "ccaller", kPairs, 1, true,              \
               Xform::IndCall);                                                \
  }                                                                            \
  TEST(SUITE, MutualRecursion) {                                               \
    checkEquiv(ISA, buildMutualRecursionIR, "mrec", kPairs, 1, true,           \
               Xform::IndCall);                                                \
  }                                                                            \
  TEST(SUITE, Recursion) {                                                     \
    checkEquiv(ISA, buildRecursiveIR, "recur", kRecDepths, 1, true,            \
               Xform::IndCall);                                                \
  }                                                                            \
  TEST(SUITE, MultiCallee) {                                                   \
    checkEquiv(ISA, buildMultiCalleeIR, "mcallee", kPairs, 1, true,            \
               Xform::IndCall);                                                \
  }

// ===========================================================================
// Mixed-boolean-arithmetic (MBAPass, CLI `--mba`): injects a provably-zero MBA
// term ((a^b)+((a&b)<<1))-a-b into every integer add/sub/mul/and/or/xor result.
// Distinct from instruction substitution (which replaces the operator) — this
// appends a zero-valued MBA polynomial that survives to the machine code via
// the same carry-save sub-term InstSubstitutionPass relies on.  Uses the
// arithmetic-heavy shapes (the pass only fires on integer operators), covering
// scalar all-ops / chained / i64-wide / i8+i16-narrow / integer-vector / global
// memory (data section compared too), across every ISA × format cell.  Each
// obfuscated copy must be bit-for-bit equivalent under Unicorn, and (since the
// injected term adds real instructions) its .text must differ from the
// original.
// ===========================================================================
#define PATCH_FULL_MBA_SUITE(SUITE, ISA)                                       \
  TEST(SUITE, ArithMix) {                                                      \
    checkEquiv(ISA, buildArithMixIR, "amix", kPairs, 1, true, Xform::MBA);     \
  }                                                                            \
  TEST(SUITE, ArithSeq) {                                                      \
    checkEquiv(ISA, buildArithSeqIR, "aseq", kPairs, 1, true, Xform::MBA);     \
  }                                                                            \
  TEST(SUITE, WideArith) {                                                     \
    checkEquiv(ISA, buildWideArithIR, "warith", kPairs, 1, true, Xform::MBA);  \
  }                                                                            \
  TEST(SUITE, NarrowArith) {                                                   \
    checkEquiv(ISA, buildNarrowArithIR, "narith", kPairs, 1, true,             \
               Xform::MBA);                                                    \
  }                                                                            \
  TEST(SUITE, VecArith) {                                                      \
    checkEquiv(ISA, buildVecArithIR, "vred", kPairs, 1, true, Xform::MBA);     \
  }                                                                            \
  TEST(SUITE, DataAccum) {                                                     \
    checkEquiv(ISA, buildDataAccumIR, "daccum", kNoArg, 1, true, Xform::MBA);  \
  }

// Indirect global variable (IndirectGlobalPass, CLI `--ind-gv`): rewrites every
// direct reference to a defined global `@g` into inttoptr(volatile-laundered
// ptrtoint(@g)).  The data dual of indirect-call (which hides the call graph) —
// this hides global *data* references.  Uses the global-data-heavy shapes (the
// pass only fires on direct global operands): scalar+array accumulator / global
// data pointer / global struct array / .bss zero-init global / 2D global grid,

// materialization survives to the machine code, so each obfuscated copy must be

// ===========================================================================
// Value laundering (ValueLaunderingPass, CLI `--launder`): routes every integer
// (scalar / integer-vector) instruction result through a volatile stack slot
// (store-volatile / load-volatile) and redirects its uses to the reload.  The
// data-value dual of indirect-call/indirect-global (which launder an address);
// this launders computed *values*, forcing them out of registers and back
// through memory.  Uses the same arithmetic-heavy shapes as the MBA suite (max
// number of integer results to launder): scalar all-ops / chained / i64-wide /
// i8+i16-narrow / integer-vector / global memory (data section compared too),
// across every ISA x format cell.  The volatile round-trip cannot be elided, so
// each obfuscated copy must be bit-for-bit equivalent under Unicorn yet its
// .text must differ from the original (extra spill/reload traffic).
// ===========================================================================
#define PATCH_FULL_LAUNDER_SUITE(SUITE, ISA)                                   \
  TEST(SUITE, ArithMix) {                                                      \
    checkEquiv(ISA, buildArithMixIR, "amix", kPairs, 1, true, Xform::Launder); \
  }                                                                            \
  TEST(SUITE, ArithSeq) {                                                      \
    checkEquiv(ISA, buildArithSeqIR, "aseq", kPairs, 1, true, Xform::Launder); \
  }                                                                            \
  TEST(SUITE, WideArith) {                                                     \
    checkEquiv(ISA, buildWideArithIR, "warith", kPairs, 1, true,               \
               Xform::Launder);                                                \
  }                                                                            \
  TEST(SUITE, NarrowArith) {                                                   \
    checkEquiv(ISA, buildNarrowArithIR, "narith", kPairs, 1, true,             \
               Xform::Launder);                                                \
  }                                                                            \
  TEST(SUITE, VecArith) {                                                      \
    checkEquiv(ISA, buildVecArithIR, "vred", kPairs, 1, true, Xform::Launder); \
  }                                                                            \
  TEST(SUITE, DataAccum) {                                                     \
    checkEquiv(ISA, buildDataAccumIR, "daccum", kNoArg, 1, true,               \
               Xform::Launder);                                                \
  }

// ===========================================================================
// Constant pooling (ConstantPoolingPass, CLI `--const-pool`): moves integer
// constant operands of binary operators / comparisons into a pass-created
// read-only global pool ([N x i64]) and fetches them at run time through an
// opaque (volatile-laundered) index, so the literal no longer appears inline.
// Unlike every other sample, this transform *creates a new global variable*, so
// it is the first to exercise the rewrite backend's placement / relocation of
// pass-introduced read-only data plus run-time-indexed (base + i*scale) global
// addressing.  Samples chosen to carry poolable integer constants across
// widths: many i32 (cmix) / i8+i16+i32+i64 (mwc, exercises the per-width trunc
// on load) / loop-body constants (laccum) / global memory whose writable .data
// is compared too (daccum — guards that the new *read-only* pool global does
// not perturb the mutable data section, incl. COFF .rdata COMDAT merging) /
// i64-wide (warith) / integer vector with scalar-tail constants (vred).  The
// volatile index cannot be folded, so each obfuscated copy must be bit-for-bit
// equivalent under Unicorn yet its .text must differ from the original.
// ===========================================================================
#define PATCH_FULL_CONSTPOOL_SUITE(SUITE, ISA)                                 \
  TEST(SUITE, ConstMix) {                                                      \
    checkEquiv(ISA, buildConstMixIR, "cmix", kCounts, 1, true,                 \
               Xform::ConstPool);                                              \
  }                                                                            \
  TEST(SUITE, MultiWidthConst) {                                               \
    checkEquiv(ISA, buildMultiWidthConstIR, "mwc", kPairs, 1, true,            \
               Xform::ConstPool);                                              \
  }                                                                            \
  TEST(SUITE, LoopAccum) {                                                     \
    checkEquiv(ISA, buildLoopAccumIR, "laccum", kCounts, 1, true,              \
               Xform::ConstPool);                                              \
  }                                                                            \
  TEST(SUITE, DataAccum) {                                                     \
    checkEquiv(ISA, buildDataAccumIR, "daccum", kNoArg, 1, true,               \
               Xform::ConstPool);                                              \
  }                                                                            \
  TEST(SUITE, WideArith64) {                                                   \
    checkEquiv(ISA, buildWideArithIR, "warith", kPairs, 1, true,               \
               Xform::ConstPool);                                              \
  }                                                                            \
  TEST(SUITE, VecArith) {                                                      \
    checkEquiv(ISA, buildVecArithIR, "vred", kPairs, 1, true,                  \
               Xform::ConstPool);                                              \
  }

PATCH_FULL_CONSTPOOL_SUITE(PatchFullConstPool_ELF_x64, kELF_x64)
PATCH_FULL_CONSTPOOL_SUITE(PatchFullConstPool_ELF_AArch64, kELF_AArch64)
PATCH_FULL_CONSTPOOL_SUITE(PatchFullConstPool_ELF_ARM32, kELF_ARM32)
PATCH_FULL_CONSTPOOL_SUITE(PatchFullConstPool_ELF_i386, kELF_i386)
PATCH_FULL_CONSTPOOL_SUITE(PatchFullConstPool_COFF_x64, kCOFF_x64)
PATCH_FULL_CONSTPOOL_SUITE(PatchFullConstPool_COFF_AArch64, kCOFF_AArch64)
PATCH_FULL_CONSTPOOL_SUITE(PatchFullConstPool_COFF_ARM32, kCOFF_ARM32)
PATCH_FULL_CONSTPOOL_SUITE(PatchFullConstPool_COFF_i386, kCOFF_i386)
PATCH_FULL_CONSTPOOL_SUITE(PatchFullConstPool_MachO_x64, kMachO_x64)
PATCH_FULL_CONSTPOOL_SUITE(PatchFullConstPool_MachO_AArch64, kMachO_AArch64)
PATCH_FULL_CONSTPOOL_SUITE(PatchFullConstPool_MachO_i386, kMachO_i386)
PATCH_FULL_CONSTPOOL_SUITE(PatchFullConstPool_MachO_ARM32, kMachO_ARM32)

// ===========================================================================
// Host-native end-to-end: the real neverd_patch_full path via the CLI.
//
// The Unicorn grid above proves the substitution + rewrite-backend codegen is
// equivalent for every (ISA × format).  This complements it on the host arch
// by driving the *complete* pipeline neverd_patch_full runs — lift -> subst ->
// trampoline install -> file write -> (ad-hoc codesign on macOS) — and then
// executing the original vs patched binary, requiring an identical exit code.
//
// Cross-arch binaries cannot be executed natively (that is what the Unicorn
// grid is for), so this runs on whatever host clang targets; it skips
// gracefully when a host clang is unavailable.
// ===========================================================================
namespace {

namespace fs = std::filesystem;

std::string ndBinary() {
  if (const char *E = std::getenv("NEVERD"))
    return E;
  return NEVERD_BINARY;
}

bool haveClang() { return std::system("clang --version >/dev/null 2>&1") == 0; }

int runExit(const std::string &Cmd) {
  int RC = std::system(Cmd.c_str());
  return WEXITSTATUS(RC);
}

// Self-contained program (no libc) exercising all five substituted operators;
// main returns compute(40,9) & 0xff so the exit code carries the result.
const char *kHostProgram = R"C(
int compute(int a, int b) {
  int s = a + b;
  int d = a - b;
  int an = a & b;
  int o = a | b;
  int x = a ^ b;
  return ((s + d) ^ (an | o)) - x;
}
int main(void) { return compute(40, 9) & 0xff; }
)C";

// Self-contained program dense in integer constants (i8/i16/i32 widths) so the
// constant-encryption pass has plenty to rewrite; exit code carries the result.
const char *kHostConstProgram = R"C(
int compute(int a, int b) {
  int s = (a + 0x1234) - 0x0567;
  int m = (b ^ 0x7FFF) & 0x0FF0;
  int r = s + m;
  if (r > 0x100) r = r - 0x100;
  return r & 0xff;
}
int main(void) { return compute(40, 9) & 0xff; }
)C";

// Global array + accumulator exercised by the indirect-global pass: every
// load/store names @g_arr / @g_acc as a direct global operand.
const char *kHostGlobalProgram = R"C(
int g_arr[8] = {1, 2, 3, 4, 5, 6, 7, 8};
int g_acc = 100;
int compute(void) {
  int s = 0;
  for (int i = 0; i < 8; i++) {
    g_arr[i] = g_arr[i] + i;
    s = s ^ g_arr[i];
  }
  g_acc = g_acc + s;
  return g_acc & 0xff;
}
int main(void) { return compute(); }
)C";

// Compile the host program, patch it with \p Flag through neverd_patch_full,
// and require the patched binary to reproduce the original's exit code.
void runHostE2E(const char *Mode, const char *Flag, const char *Program,
                const char *Tag) {
  if (!haveClang())
    GTEST_SKIP() << "host clang unavailable";

  auto Dir =
      fs::temp_directory_path() /
      ("nd_pf_" + std::string(Tag) + "_" + std::string(Mode) + "_" +
       std::to_string(static_cast<unsigned long long>(
           ::testing::UnitTest::GetInstance()->current_test_info()->line())));
  std::error_code EC;
  fs::create_directories(Dir, EC);
  auto CSrc = (Dir / "m.c").string();
  auto Exe = (Dir / "m").string();
  auto Patched = (Dir / "m.patched").string();
  {
    std::ofstream OS(CSrc);
    OS << Program;
  }

  if (runExit("clang -O0 -fno-stack-protector -o " + Exe + " " + CSrc) != 0)
    GTEST_SKIP() << "host clang could not build the sample";

  int Base = runExit(Exe);

  std::string ModeFlag =
      (std::string(Mode) == "inplace") ? " --mode inplace" : "";
  std::string Cmd = ndBinary() + " patch " + Exe + ModeFlag + " " + Flag +
                    " -o " + Patched + " >/dev/null 2>&1";
  ASSERT_EQ(runExit(Cmd), 0)
      << "neverd patch " << Flag << " (" << Mode << ") failed";
  ASSERT_TRUE(fs::exists(Patched)) << "patched binary not produced";

  int Sub = runExit(Patched);
  EXPECT_EQ(Base, Sub) << "exit code changed after " << Tag << " (" << Mode
                       << "): orig=" << Base << " obf=" << Sub;

  if (!::testing::Test::HasFailure())
    fs::remove_all(Dir, EC);
}

// String literals exercised through the full patch path: puts, single %s, and a
// multi-arg printf with several string literals.  Unlike the compute programs
// above (which only carry a result in the exit code), this prints text and
// compares stdout too -- the P6 bug left a string-literal address as a bare
// absolute VA, so a regression shows up as a SIGSEGV under ASLR or as wrong /
// truncated output.  The fix (bare-ConstantInt symbolization in
// symbolizeImageAbsolutePointers) is gated to 64-bit Mach-O, so this runs on
// Apple hosts only; ELF/COFF string handling is tracked separately.
const char *kHostStringProgram = R"C(
#include <stdio.h>
int main(void) {
  const char *w = "world";
  const char *a = "alpha", *b = "beta", *c = "gamma";
  puts("hello via puts");
  printf("hi %s!\n", w);
  printf("%s %s %s\n", a, b, c);
  return 77;
}
)C";

// A global array of string-literal pointers (`const char* names[]`) alongside a
// plain int array (`int vals[]`), both indexed in a loop.  This is the rmix
// case: clang lowers the int-array access through the `getelementptr @data,
// (symbolized_base - DATA_BASE_VA)` idiom; with the base symbolized but the
// `- DATA_BASE_VA` left raw, the address slides twice -> wild pointer.  The
// string pointers also live in the original data and rebase via dyld.
const char *kHostMixedProgram = R"C(
#include <stdio.h>
const char *names[3] = {"alpha", "beta", "gamma"};
int vals[3] = {7, 8, 9};
int main(void) {
  int s = 0;
  for (int i = 0; i < 3; i++) {
    printf("%s=%d\n", names[i], vals[i]);
    s += vals[i];
  }
  return s & 0xff;
}
)C";

// Floating-point variadic arguments, mixed with an int.  On Darwin AArch64
// every variadic argument -- doubles included -- is passed on the stack, but
// the lifter's FP-register scan used to also pick up a caller-saved V0..V7 (the
// poly() return) and inject it as a spurious FP argument, shifting printf's
// reads so `printf("p[%d]=%.3f", i, v)` printed "p[0]=0.000".  Verifies stdout
// so the float formatting (not just the exit code) is checked.
const char *kHostFloatProgram = R"C(
#include <stdio.h>
static double poly(double x) { return 3.0 * x * x - 2.0 * x + 1.5; }
int main(void) {
  double acc = 0.0;
  for (int i = 0; i < 6; i++) {
    double v = poly((double)i * 0.5);
    printf("p[%d]=%.3f\n", i, v);
    acc += v;
  }
  printf("acc=%.3f\n", acc);
  return (int)acc & 0xff;
}
)C";

// Fortified _FORTIFY_SOURCE printf family: clang lowers snprintf with a
// known destination size to __snprintf_chk (5 fixed args: buf, maxlen, flag,
// slen, fmt).  varArgFixedCount did not recognize the _chk suffix, so the
// variadic arguments were dropped and snprintf printed stack garbage.  Checks
// stdout to confirm the formatted buffer is correct.
const char *kHostChkProgram = R"C(
#include <stdio.h>
int main(void) {
  char buf[64];
  int n = snprintf(buf, sizeof buf, "%d-%s-%x", 42, "mid", 0xbeef);
  printf("[%s] len=%d\n", buf, n);
  int sum = 0;
  for (int i = 0; i < n; i++) sum += buf[i];
